title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
萬曆紀元秋八月復當賓興
天下士巡按湖廣監察御史
舒鰲以故事檄岱暨敎授黃
銳周希正學正蕭大謙趙以
康敎諭陳一定鍾沛朱寬殷
乾左懋貞司試事左布政使
===
施堯臣右布政使陳瑞司提
調按察使王世貞僉事蔡一
槐司監試旣入棘百執事受
約束御史唯恧唯愼乃合提
學副使姚弘謨所選士二千
七百有奇三試之錄其雋九
十及文以
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

萬曆紀元秋八月，復當賓興天下士。巡按湖廣監察御史舒鰲以故事檄岱，暨敎授黃銳、周希正，學正蕭大謙、趙以康，敎諭陳一定、鍾沛、朱寬、殷乾、左懋貞司試事；左布政使施堯臣、右布政使陳瑞司提調；按察使王世貞、僉事蔡一槐司監試。旣入棘，百執事受約束，御史唯恧唯愼，乃合提學副使姚弘謨所選士二千七百有奇三試之，錄其雋九十，及文以
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the eighth month, in autumn, of the first year of the Wanli era (1573), it was once again the time to welcome and recommend the scholars of the realm. Following precedent, the Regional Inspector of Huguang and Investigating Censor Shu Ao 舒鰲 issued an official summons to me, [Li] Dai 李岱, together with the Prefectural Instructors Huang Rui 黃銳 and Zhou Xizheng 周希正; the Subprefectural Instructors Xiao Daqian 蕭大謙 and Zhao Yikang 趙以康; and the County Instructors Chen Yiding 陳一定, Zhong Pei 鍾沛, Zhu Kuan 朱寬, Yin Qian 殷乾, and Zuo Maozhen 左懋貞, to take charge of examining. The Left Administration Commissioner Shi Yaochen 施堯臣 and the Right Administration Commissioner Chen Rui 陳瑞 served as Proctors; the Surveillance Commissioner Wang Shizhen 王世貞 and the Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Cai Yihuai 蔡一槐 served as Monitors. Once we entered the thorny compound, all the hundred functionaries accepted the regulations. With the Censor acting with the utmost humility and caution, we gathered the more than two thousand seven hundred scholars selected by the Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Yao Hongmo 姚弘謨 and tested them in three sessions, recording ninety of the most outstanding among them, along with their essays, to…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
獻岱不佞以職事序首簡始岱
讀相如子虛而怪之以為夸
張少實且楚雖大何至乃匹
漢上林而自稍長益習見楚
圖經地志則
神州之內五嶽者楚得其一其
視嶽而加尊者楚又得其一
所謂岑崟參差日月蔽虧交
錯糾紛上干青雲之狀不易
指數岷峨導波自萬里來匯
為洞庭黏天浩瀚扶輿之秀
結而成丹青赭堊雌雄黃白
瑊玏玄厲之屬瑰奇異狀吾
故恨賦之未盡也夫地靈則
punctuated: 獻。岱不佞，以職事序首簡。始岱讀相如《子虛》而怪之，以為夸張少實；且楚雖大，何至乃匹漢上林？而自稍長，益習見楚圖經地志，則神州之內，五嶽者，楚得其一；其視嶽而加尊者，楚又得其一。所謂岑崟參差，日月蔽虧，交錯糾紛，上干青雲之狀，不易指數。岷、峨導波，自萬里來，匯為洞庭，黏天浩瀚。扶輿之秀，結而成丹、青、赭、堊、雌雄黃、白瑊、玏、玄厲之屬，瑰奇異狀，吾故恨賦之未盡也。夫地靈則
translation_en:
… present it to the throne. Unworthy though I, Dai, am, by virtue of my official duties I write the preface for the opening pages.

When I, Dai, first read Sima Xiangru's司馬相如 Rhapsody on Sir Fantasy (Zixu fu 子虛賦), I found it strange, considering it exaggerated and lacking in factual substance; moreover, great though Chu was, how could it possibly rival the Shanglin Park of the Han? Yet as I grew older and became increasingly familiar with the illustrated treatises and local gazetteers of Chu, I realized that within the Sacred Continent, of the Five Marchmounts, Chu possesses one [Mount Heng 衡山]; and of that which is ranked like a marchmount and held in even greater veneration [Mount Taihe 太和山 / Wudang 武當山], Chu also possesses one. What the rhapsody describes as craggy and jagged peaks, screening and eclipsing the sun and moon, interlocking in tangled profusion and towering up into the blue clouds—such sights cannot easily be counted on the fingers. The waters guided from Mounts Min and Emei come from ten thousand li away to converge as Lake Dongting, a vast expanse merging with the sky. The vital beauty of nature condenses to form cinnabar, azurite, red ochre, white clay, orpiment and realgar, white fluorite, veined stones, black whetstones, and the like, in extraordinary and marvelous shapes—so that I came instead to regret that the rhapsody had not exhausted them all! Now, that sacred geography gives rise to …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人傑蓋自古記之矣當周之
季其南紀有仲山甫尹吉甫
者出而弘將相之業以振其
微功成而交相頌以蓽路籃
縷之楚有臣如鬪穀孫叔為
之左提右挈而後先伯夫豈
亦棫樸思齊之遺士固有興
===
於待者耶孔子南游楚雖不
遂獲東周而率其徒相與講
明皇王之術六籍大指七十
子之倫其五楚焉而楚自是
稱有文矣乃僅能以其變風
變雅之旨創矩矱而為騷若
賦如屈平宋玉唐勒景差者
punctuated: 人傑，蓋自古記之矣。當周之季，其南紀有仲山甫、尹吉甫者，出而弘將相之業，以振其微，功成而交相頌。以蓽路籃縷之楚，有臣如鬪穀、孫叔，為之左提右挈而後先伯。夫豈亦《棫樸》、《思齊》之遺，士固有興於待者耶？孔子南游楚，雖不遂獲東周，而率其徒相與講明皇王之術、六籍大指。七十子之倫，其五楚焉，而楚自是稱有文矣。乃僅能以其變風、變雅之旨，創矩矱而為騷、若賦，如屈平、宋玉、唐勒、景差者，
translation_en: … outstanding men, as has indeed been recorded since antiquity. During the decline of the Zhou dynasty, in its southern regions there emerged men such as Zhong Shanfu 仲山甫 and Yin Jifu 尹吉甫, who expanded the achievements of generals and chief ministers to revive its waning fortunes, and when their deeds were accomplished, they sang each other's praises. Even with Chu 楚 in its early days of rough carts and tattered clothes, it had ministers like Dou Gu 鬪穀 [Dou Guwutu 鬪穀於菟] and Sunshu 孫叔 [Sunshu Ao 孫叔敖], who assisted and supported it on left and right, so that earlier and later it achieved hegemony. Could this too not be the legacy of the odes "Oak Thickets" (Yupu 棫樸) and "Reverent and莊" (Siqi 思齊), whereby scholars naturally arise when awaited? When Confucius traveled south to Chu, although he did not succeed in bringing about an Eastern Zhou revival, he led his disciples in elucidating together the arts of sovereigns and kings and the great principles of the Six Classics. Among the ranks of his seventy disciples, five were from Chu, and from that time onward Chu was renowned for its literary culture. Yet afterward, it was only able to take the purport of the Changed Airs (bianfeng 變風) and Changed Odes (bianya 變雅) to establish new standards and compose elegies (sao 騷) and rhapsodies (fu 賦)—through men such as Qu Ping 屈平 [Qu Yuan 屈原], Song Yu 宋玉, Tang Le 唐勒, and Jing Cuo 景差…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
至襄陽之杜而變始極其於
稱亦甚著第令天下謂文士
足張楚而已不聞其以孔子
之道衍而爲公卿將相之業
何也今以岱之無似幸而用
玆役獲竊觀楚之山川土風
又幸而獲從事竟諸生業其
噲拔汪瀚珍竒疊發恍若凌
巨飈踐名嶽入海而探寳藏
卽無論其選者彬彬乎名實
中竅其所不能盡者亦尚芃
芃然足以備異日之采庶幾
哉楚秀有徵矣自
明興不爲騷賦之一端以礙士而
punctuated: 至襄陽之杜，而變始極，其於稱亦甚著。第令天下謂文士足張楚而已，不聞其以孔子之道，衍而爲公卿將相之業，何也？今以岱之無似，幸而用玆役，獲竊觀楚之山川土風，又幸而獲從事竟諸生業，其噲拔汪瀚、珍竒疊發，恍若凌巨飈、踐名嶽、入海而探寳藏。卽無論其選者彬彬乎名實中竅，其所不能盡者，亦尚芃芃然足以備異日之采。庶幾哉，楚秀有徵矣！自明興，不爲騷賦之一端以礙士，而
translation_en: …down to Du of Xiangyang [Du Fu 杜甫], when the transformation finally reached its pinnacle, and their renown became extraordinarily illustrious. Yet this only caused the empire to say that literary men sufficed to make Chu great, while one never heard of them extending the Way of Confucius into the achievements of high ministers, generals, and chancellors—why is that? Now, unworthy as I, Dai, am, I have had the good fortune through this assignment to venture a look at the mountains, rivers, and local customs of Chu, and the further good fortune to engage in reading through the examination essays of the candidates. Their lofty brilliance and vast depth, with rare wonders bursting forth one after another, made me feel as if I were riding a great gale, treading upon famous sacred peaks, or entering the sea to plumb a treasure house. Even setting aside those selected, who in their refined balance of reputation and reality hit the mark, those whom the quota could not accommodate are still flourishing enough to be held in reserve for selection on a future day. Truly, the excellence of Chu is well attested! Since the rise of the Ming, the court has not used the single narrow path of elegies and rhapsodies (sao and fu) to constrain scholars, but…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
大指在尊經術廣時務冀以
是得人焉縣官用諸生佩法
孔子亦既有年其於所謂經
術時務者
上固精求之而下亦佹得之矣盍
亦思所以善其後乎夫仲山
尹吉二甫叔世之毗也鬭榖
===
孫叔偏雄之輔也其下者至
不知有經術然各能以其材
成其主之業而顯其名况於
今
聖天子握
乾符秉
冲睿委柄股肱良臣用以弼成治
punctuated: 大指在尊經術、廣時務，冀以是得人焉。縣官用諸生佩法孔子，亦既有年。其於所謂經術、時務者，上固精求之，而下亦佹得之矣，盍亦思所以善其後乎？夫仲山、尹吉二甫，叔世之毗也；鬭榖、孫叔，偏雄之輔也。其下者至不知有經術，然各能以其材成其主之業而顯其名。况於今聖天子握乾符、秉冲睿，委柄股肱良臣，用以弼成治
translation_en: … the overarching aim lies in honoring classical learning and broadening knowledge of current affairs, hoping thereby to obtain capable men. The imperial court has employed students who model themselves upon Confucius for many years now. As for what are called classical learning and current affairs, those above have certainly sought them with precision, and those below have likewise attained them before long—why not, then, give thought to how to bring this to a good outcome afterward? Now, Zhongshan Fu 仲山甫 and Yin Jifu 尹吉甫 were coadjutors of a declining age; Dou Guw菟 (Ziwen) 鬭榖於菟 and Sunshu Ao 孫叔敖 were ministers to regional hegemons. The lesser ones among them did not even know that classical learning existed, yet each was able through his own talents to accomplish his ruler's enterprise and make his own name illustrious. How much more so today, when the sacred Son of Heaven holds the talisman of Heaven, possesses youthful wisdom, and entrusts authority to worthy ministers who serve as his limbs, using them to assist in perfecting governance…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
化而子之鄉在江沱汝漢者
去文王之季而四者乎其猶
在成康之際而被周南召南
之化爲獨深者乎諸生第勗
之孔子之業行而頌聲作天
下奉以爲穆如清風若二南
者知其不爲牢愁離騷之說
===
明也楚自是稱多賢矣是舉
也巡撫湖廣右僉都御史趙
賢首勵風猷以倡文敎而巡
撫貴州兼督湖北軍務右副
都御史蔡文撫治鄖陽前右
僉都御史凌雲翼今右副都
御史湯賓提督南贛軍務右
punctuated:
化，而子之鄉在江沱汝漢者，去文王之季而四者乎？其猶在成康之際，而被《周南》、《召南》之化爲獨深者乎？諸生第勗之。孔子之業行而頌聲作，天下奉以爲穆如清風，若《二南》者，知其不爲《牢愁》、《離騷》之說明也，楚自是稱多賢矣。
是舉也，巡撫湖廣右僉都御史趙賢首勵風猷以倡文敎；而巡撫貴州兼督湖北軍務右副都御史蔡文、撫治鄖陽前右僉都御史凌雲翼、今右副都御史湯賓、提督南贛軍務右
translation_en:
…transformation, and when your homeland along the Jiang, Tuo, Ru, and Han rivers is four eras [?] removed from the end of King Wen's time? Or is it as though we were still in the age of Kings Cheng and Kang, receiving the transforming influence of the "Airs of Zhou and the South" (Zhounan) and "Airs of Shao and the South" (Shaonan) with singular depth? You students, simply exert yourselves in this! When the enterprise of Confucius is carried out and songs of praise arise, the world will revere them as "gentle as a clear breeze," like the "Two Souths" (Ernan); it is evident that they will not be the discourses of "Melancholy" (Laochou) or "Encountering Sorrow" (Lisao), and Chu from this point on will be renowned for its abundance of worthies!

In this undertaking, Grand Coordinator of Huguang and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Zhao Xian 趙賢 was the first to encourage moral conduct and governmental plans in order to champion literary and moral education; while Grand Coordinator of Guizhou concurrently Inspecting Military Affairs of Hubei and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Cai Wen 蔡文, Grand Coordinator of Yunyang and former Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Ling Yunyi 凌雲翼, the current Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Tang Bin 湯賓, and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs of Nan'gan and Right…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
僉都御史劉思問相與翊而
章之其有事楚者總兵官懷
寧侯孫世忠守備太監張堯
于役楚者南和伯方燁都督
僉事蔣克謙工科都給事中
吳文佳兵科右給事中張楚
城刑部員外郎潘頤龍戶部
===
主事羅良禎工部主事曹慎
中書舍人蔣務樵勞於棘之
外者左參政鄭雲鋈右參政
楊栢右參議李貴和郭崇嗣
胡僖王璇副使楊一魁史嗣
元邊維垣徐栢馬顧澤僉事
戢汝止余一龍賈館蘇璜李
punctuated: 僉都御史劉思問，相與翊而章之。其有事楚者：總兵官懷寧侯孫世忠、守備太監張堯；于役楚者：南和伯方燁、都督僉事蔣克謙、工科都給事中吳文佳、兵科右給事中張楚城、刑部員外郎潘頤龍、戶部主事羅良禎、工部主事曹慎、中書舍人蔣務樵；勞於棘之外者：左參政鄭雲鋈、右參政楊栢、右參議李貴和、郭崇嗣、胡僖、王璇、副使楊一魁、史嗣元、邊維垣、徐栢、馬顧澤、僉事戢汝止、余一龍、賈館、蘇璜、李
translation_en: …Assistant Censor-in-Chief Liu Siwen 劉思問, mutually assisted and made it illustrious. Those holding responsibilities in Chu [Huguang] include the Regional Commander, Marquis of Huaining Sun Shizhong 孫世忠, and the Grand Commandant in Charge of Defense, Palace Eunuch Zhang Yao 張堯; those on official duty in Chu include the Earl of Nanhe Fang Ye 方燁, Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Jiang Keqian 蔣克謙, Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Works Wu Wenjia 吳文佳, Right Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War Zhang Chucheng 張楚城, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice Pan Yilong 潘頤龍, Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue Luo Liangzhen 羅良禎, Secretary in the Ministry of Works Cao Shen 曹慎, and Drafter Jiang Wuqiao 蔣務樵; those who labored outside the examination compound include Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zheng Yunwu 鄭雲鋈, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Yang Bo 楊栢, Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Li Guihe 李貴和, Guo Chongsi 郭崇嗣, Hu Xi 胡僖, and Wang Xuan 王璇, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yang Yikui 楊一魁, Shi Siyuan 史嗣元, Bian Weiyuan 邊維垣, Xu Bo 徐栢, and Ma Guze 馬顧澤, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Ji Ruzhi 戢汝止, Yu Yilong 余一龍, Jia Guan 賈館, Su Huang 蘇璜, and Li…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
克敬署都指揮僉事馮銳勞
於先者入
賀右參政胡邦竒副使盧仲佃
署都指揮僉事劉大勛陞任
左參議舒應龍副使徐學謨
僉事馮子京皆例得書若棘
之內外執事則具錄中矣
===
浙江台州府儒學教授郭岱
謹序
punctuated:
克敬，署都指揮僉事馮銳。勞於先者：入賀右參政胡邦竒、副使盧仲佃、署都指揮僉事劉大勛，陞任左參議舒應龍、副使徐學謨、僉事馮子京，皆例得書。若棘之內外執事，則具錄中矣。
浙江台州府儒學教授郭岱謹序。
translation_en:
…[Li] Ke敬 (Li Kejing 李克敬), and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Feng Rui 馮銳. Those who labored beforehand—Right Administration Vice Commissioner Hu Bangqi 胡邦竒, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lu Zhongdian 盧仲佃, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Liu Daxun 劉大勛, who went to court to offer congratulations; as well as Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Shu Yinglong 舒應龍, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Xuemo 徐學謨, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Feng Zijing 馮子京, who have been promoted to other posts—are all entitled by precedent to be recorded here. As for the functionaries who served both inside and outside the examination compound, they are listed in full within this record.
Respectfully prefaced by Guo Dai 郭岱, Confucian School Instructor of Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
萬曆元年湖廣鄉試
監臨官
巡按湖廣監察御史舒　鰲〔子化江西德興縣人乙丑進士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左布政使施堯臣〔欽甫直隸青陽縣人庚戌進士〕
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右布政使陳　瑞〔孔麟福建長樂縣人癸丑進士〕
監試官
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使王世貞〔元美直隸太倉州人丁未進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司僉事蔡一槐〔景明福建晋江縣人己未進士〕
===
考試官
浙江台州府儒學教授郭　岱〔瞻東廣東番禺縣籍江西龍泉縣人壬子貢士〕
江西九江府儒學教授黃　銳〔汝新廣東揭陽縣人乙卯貢士〕
同考試官
廣東南雄府儒學教授周希正〔道甫廣西宣化縣人己酉貢士〕

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
□□
生而知之者上也
待其人而後行故曰苟不至德至道不凝
焉
天下大悅書曰丕顯哉文王謨丕承哉武
王烈佑啟我後人咸以正無缺
易
蒙以養正聖功也
===
上九鼎玉鉉大吉无不利象曰玉鉉在上
剛柔節也
問焉而以言其受命也如嚮无有遠近幽
深遂知來物
有天地然後萬物生焉
書
文命敷于四海祗承于帝曰后克艱厥后
臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏德
學于古訓乃有獲
punctuated:
□□
「生而知之者，上也。」
「待其人而後行。故曰：『苟不至德，至道不凝焉。』」
「天下大悅。《書》曰：『丕顯哉，文王謨！丕承哉，武王烈！佑啟我後人，咸以正無缺。』」

《易》
「蒙以養正，聖功也。」
「上九，鼎玉鉉，大吉，无不利。《象》曰：『玉鉉在上，剛柔節也。』」
「問焉而以言，其受命也如嚮，无有遠近幽深，遂知來物。」
「有天地，然後萬物生焉。」

《書》
「文命敷于四海，祗承于帝。曰：『后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。』」
「學于古訓乃有獲。」
translation_en:
[Four Books (Sishu)]
"Those who are born with possession of knowledge are the highest class of men." [Analects 16.9]
"They wait for the proper man, and then they are set in motion. Hence it is said, 'Unless there be consummate virtue, the supreme Path cannot be solidified in practice.'" [Doctrine of the Mean 27]
"All under Heaven was greatly delighted. The Book of Documents (Shu) says, 'How illustrious were the plans of King Wen! How greatly carried on were the achievements of King Wu! They aid and enlighten us, their descendants, so that all proceeds with rectitude and without deficiency.'" [Mencius 3B.9]

Classic of Changes (Yi)
"By means of youthful ignorance to nourish rectitude is the sacred task of the sage." [Hexagram 4, Meng, Commentary on the Judgment]
"Top Nine: The cauldron has rings of jade. Great good fortune; nothing that is not advantageous. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Rings of jade at the top: firm and yielding are in due measure.'" [Hexagram 50, Ding]
"When one puts a question to the milfoil stalks and speaks through them, they receive the charge like an echo; whether the matter be distant or near, obscure or deep, one thereby knows the things that are to come." [Great Treatise (Xici) I.10]
"Only after there are Heaven and Earth are the myriad things born." [Sequence of the Hexagrams (Xugua)]

Book of Documents (Shu)
"His civilizing ordinance was spread throughout the Four Seas, and he reverently responded to the Emperor, saying: 'If the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of his sovereignty, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of his ministry, government will be well ordered, and the black-haired people will be earnest in virtue.'" [Counsels of the Great Yu (Da Yu mo)]
"It is by studying the lessons of antiquity that one attains results." [Charge to Yue (Yue ming), Part III]

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
嚴恭寅畏天命自度
聰明齊聖小大之臣咸懷忠良其侍御僕
從罔匪正人以旦夕承弼厥辟
詩
蒹葭蒼蒼白露為霜所謂伊人在水一方
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天魚在于渚或潛在
淵樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維穀他山
之石可以攻玉
虎拜稽首天子萬年
===
日就月將學有緝熈于光明佛時仔肩示
我顯德行
春秋
春王正月公敗齊師于長勺〔莊公十年〕冬
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十
有二月已亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕夏公
會齊侯于夾谷公至自夾谷〔定公十年〕
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
punctuated:
嚴恭寅畏，天命自度。
聰明齊聖，小大之臣咸懷忠良；其侍御僕從，罔匪正人，以旦夕承弼厥辟。
《詩》
蒹葭蒼蒼，白露為霜。所謂伊人，在水一方。
鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。魚在于渚，或潛在淵。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維穀。他山之石，可以攻玉。
虎拜稽首，天子萬年。
日就月將，學有緝熈于光明。佛時仔肩，示我顯德行。
《春秋》
春王正月，公敗齊師于長勺。〔莊公十年〕冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月已亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷，公至自夾谷。〔定公十年〕
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。
translation_en:
"He was grave, respectful, reverent, and awestruck; he measured himself by the Mandate of Heaven."

"Intelligent, perceptive, solemn, and sage; his ministers, both small and great, all cherished loyalty and goodness; and among his attendants, charioteers, and personal servants, there were none who were not upright men, morning and evening assisting and correcting their sovereign."

Book of Odes (Shi):

"The reeds and rushes are deeply green, / And the white dew is turned to frost. / The person of whom I speak / Is on the other side of the water."

"The crane cries in the nine marshes, / And its voice is heard in the heavens. / The fish lies by the islet, / Or sinks into the deep pool. / Pleasant is that garden, / Where the sandalwood trees stand, / And beneath them is the paper-mulberry. / The stones of those other hills / May be used to polish jade."

"Hu bowed with his head to the ground: / 'May the Son of Heaven live for ten thousand years!'"

"With daily progress and monthly advance, / I will learn until there is a continuous brightness leading to illumination. / Assist me in bearing this heavy burden upon my shoulders, / And show me how to display virtuous conduct."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):

"In spring, in the King's first month, the Duke defeated the army of Qi at Changshao." [Tenth year of Duke Zhuang] "In winter, the Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Little Zhu, and Guang, the Heir Apparent of Qi, to invade Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they made a covenant together at Xi." [Ninth year of Duke Xiang] "In summer, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The Duke arrived from Jiagu." [Tenth year of Duke Ding]

"In the eighth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a man of Zhu at Cheng." …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
〔僖公元年〕
夏四月己巳晉侯齊師宋師秦師及楚人
戰于城濮〔僖公二十有八年〕戊子晉人
及秦人戰于令狐〔文公七年〕夏叔孫豹
會晉趙武楚屈建蔡公孫歸生衛石惡
陳孔奐鄭良霄許人曹人于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭〔宣公元年〕
公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕
===
禮記
天子之五官曰司徒司馬司空司士司寇
典司五眾天子之六府曰司土司木司
水司草司器司貨典司六職天子之六
工曰土工金工石工木工獸工草工典
制六材五官致貢曰享
五行四時十二月還相為本也
內和而外順則民瞻其顏色而弗與爭也
望其容貌而民不生易慢焉故德輝動
punctuated:
〔僖公元年〕。
夏四月己巳，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮〔僖公二十有八年〕；戊子，晉人及秦人戰于令狐〔文公七年〕；夏，叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚屈建、蔡公孫歸生、衛石惡、陳孔奐、鄭良霄、許人、曹人于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕。
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭〔宣公元年〕；公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕。

禮記
天子之五官，曰司徒、司馬、司空、司士、司寇，典司五眾。天子之六府，曰司土、司木、司水、司草、司器、司貨，典司六職。天子之六工，曰土工、金工、石工、木工、獸工、草工，典制六材。五官致貢曰享。
五行、四時、十二月，還相為本也。
內和而外順，則民瞻其顏色而弗與爭也，望其容貌而民不生易慢焉。故德輝動
translation_en:
… [First year of Duke Xi].
“In summer, in the fourth month, on the jisi day, the Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought with the men of Chu at Chengpu” [Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi]; “On the wuzi day, the men of Jin and the men of Qin fought at Linghu” [Seventh year of Duke Wen]; “In summer, Shusun Bao met with Zhao Wu of Jin, Qu Jian of Chu, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Shi E of Wei, Kong Huan of Chen, Liang Xiao of Zheng, the men of Xu, and the men of Cao at Song” [Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang].
“The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met with the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng” [First year of Duke Xuan]; “The Duke met with the army of Jin at Wa” [Eighth year of Duke Ding].

Record of Rites (Liji)
“The Son of Heaven’s Five Officers are called the Minister of Education (Situ), the Minister of War (Sima), the Minister of Works (Sikong), the Director of Servitors (Sishi), and the Minister of Justice (Sikou); they are in charge of the five multitudes. The Son of Heaven’s Six Storehouses are called the Director of Soil (Situ), the Director of Wood (Simu), the Director of Water (Sishui), the Director of Grass (Sicao), the Director of Vessels (Siqi), and the Director of Goods (Sihuo); they are in charge of the six duties. The Son of Heaven’s Six Artisans are called the Earth Artisan (Tugong), the Metal Artisan (Jingong), the Stone Artisan (Shigong), the Wood Artisan (Mugong), the Animal Artisan (Shougong), and the Grass Artisan (Caogong); they are in charge of fashioning the six materials. When the Five Officers present their tribute, it is called ‘offering’ (xiang).”
“The Five Phases, the four seasons, and the twelve months in turn serve as the foundation for one another.”
“When there is harmony within and compliance without, the people will look upon his countenance and not contend with him; they will gaze upon his demeanor and the people will not give rise to轻蔑 [disrespect or negligence]. Therefore, when the radiance of virtue stirs…”

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於內而民莫不承聽理發諸外而民莫
不承順
王言如絲其出如綸
第貳場
論
君志定而天下之治成
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令郡國舉孝弟有行義詔〔地節三年〕
擬唐以姚崇爲紫微令誥〔開元元年〕
===
擬宋以敧器論賜宰臣王曾等謝表〔乾興元年〕
判語〔五條〕
官文書稽程
市司評物價
宿衛人兵仗
斷罪引律令
造作不如法
第叁場
punctuated:
於內，而民莫不承聽；理發諸外，而民莫不承順。
王言如絲，其出如綸。

第貳場
論：
君志定而天下之治成。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢令郡國舉孝弟有行義詔〔地節三年〕。
擬唐以姚崇爲紫微令誥〔開元元年〕。
擬宋以《敧器論》賜宰臣王曾等謝表〔乾興元年〕。
判語〔五條〕：
官文書稽程、市司評物價、宿衛人兵仗、斷罪引律令、造作不如法。

第叁場
translation_en:
… within, and there are none among the people who do not hearken and obey; when principle manifests outwardly, there are none among the people who do not submit and comply.
The king's words are like silk threads, yet they issue forth like cords.

Second Session
Discourse:
"When the ruler's will is fixed, the governance of all under Heaven is accomplished."
Imperial Edict, Mandate, and Memorial [examinees choose one]:
Imitation of the Han Dynasty Imperial Edict Ordering the Commanderies and Principalities to Recommend Those Who Are Filial, Fraternal, and of Righteous Conduct [third year of the Dijie reign (67 BCE)].
Imitation of the Tang Dynasty Mandate Appointing Yao Chong (姚崇) as Secretariat Director [first year of the Kaiyuan reign (713)].
Imitation of the Song Dynasty Memorial of Gratitude from Grand Councilor Wang Zeng (王曾) and Others Upon Being Bestowed the Discourse on the Tilting Vessel [first year of the Qianxing reign (1022)].
Legal Judgments [five items]:
Delays in Official Documents; Assessment of Commodity Prices by Market Officials; Weapons and Armor of Palace Guards; Citing Statutes and Ordinances in Pronouncing Sentences; Manufacturing Not in Accordance with Regulations.

Third Session

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
策五道
問古推功者重開創語德者歸守成殆未
有以易也我
高皇帝逐胡元定寓縣再闢天地驅一世之椎
結而冠裳之不亦功倍堯舜哉其良法
媺意提衡畔渙顜若畫一蓋二百有餘
禩而天下謐如也
文皇戡家難
孝皇敦身範赫然聲施異世焉其後先顯承之
===
烈亦能舉其大略否
今上業方在茂齡而薄海內外奉澤共慶搢紳
黔黎交口而頌
聖質以為過周成漢昭萬萬夫萬古莫二之功
我
高皇既擅之乃
今上秉齊聖履
大寶益富春秋萬古
嗣盛之德此其時矣將何脩而可以比於
punctuated:
策五道

問：古推功者重開創，語德者歸守成，殆未有以易也。我高皇帝逐胡元、定寓縣，再闢天地，驅一世之椎結而冠裳之，不亦功倍堯、舜哉！其良法媺意，提衡畔渙，顜若畫一，蓋二百有餘禩而天下謐如也。文皇戡家難，孝皇敦身範，赫然聲施異世焉。其後先顯承之烈，亦能舉其大略否？今上業方在茂齡，而薄海內外奉澤共慶，搢紳黔黎交口而頌聖質，以為過周成、漢昭萬萬。夫萬古莫二之功，我高皇既擅之；乃今上秉齊聖，履大寶，益富春秋，萬古嗣盛之德，此其時矣。將何脩而可以比於
translation_en:
Five Policy Questions

Question: In antiquity, those who extolled meritorious achievement attached weight to founding a dynasty, while those who spoke of virtue attributed it to preserving what had been accomplished; this is an assessment that can scarcely be altered. Our Exalted Emperor [the Hongwu Emperor, Zhu Yuanzhang] expelled the northern barbarian Yuan, pacified the realm and its counties, opened up heaven and earth anew, and took a generation of people wearing mallet-shaped topknots and clad them in caps and robes—was his achievement not double that of Yao and Shun? His fine laws and admirable intentions maintained the balance and restrained waywardness, clear and uniform as if drawn with a single stroke, so that for more than two hundred years the world has remained tranquil. The Cultured Emperor [the Yongle Emperor, Zhu Di] quelled the troubles within the imperial house, and the Filial Emperor [the Hongzhi Emperor, Zhu Youtang] earnestly cultivated his personal conduct as a model; their illustrious renown has extended across subsequent generations. As for the glorious achievements by which they successively carried forward the dynastic legacy, can you also recount their general outlines?

His Present Majesty is now in his flourishing youth, yet within and beyond the four seas all receive his beneficence and rejoice together; officials and commoners alike praise his sacred disposition with one voice, considering him to surpass King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han ten thousand times over. Now, achievement unmatched in ten thousand ages has already been monopolized by our Exalted Emperor; and today His Present Majesty, endowed with comprehensive sageliness, has ascended the Great Treasure [the throne] with many years of youth ahead of him—for the virtue of succeeding to and maintaining prosperity across ten thousand ages, this is the very time! What then should be cultivated so that he may be compared to…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
先皇觀也諸生爲精言之不佞將以聞於
上
問天官家言談說災祥禍福若指諸掌其
大槩三焉有遠而不變者如元會所紀
陽九百六之類是也有近而可推者日
月薄蝕五星躔度正犯之類是也有卒
來而不可究者彗孛凌變寒暑霜雹震
𩆝水旱之類是也然推天以徵人則於
法有合有不合推人以徵天則於數有
===
驗有不驗果何也說者以爲三代時人
主之精誠徹於天天視聽爲一而後不
能盡然又謂太史失其官躔野變其度
而不盡能一一應然歟否耶當
世宗末海內報災異者不虛月而其奏祥者輒
上聞然至於今而寰宇寧晏夷狄賓服民心忻
如也即往者心翼小小而
聖主喆輔交相爲儆固借此益脩其德以仰承
仁愛顧其數有可推而其道有可盡者
punctuated:
先皇觀也？諸生爲精言之，不佞將以聞於上。

問：天官家言，談說災祥禍福若指諸掌，其大槩三焉：有遠而不變者，如《元會》所紀陽九、百六之類是也；有近而可推者，日月薄蝕、五星躔度正犯之類是也；有卒來而不可究者，彗孛凌變、寒暑霜雹、震𩆝水旱之類是也。然推天以徵人，則於法有合有不合；推人以徵天，則於數有驗有不驗，果何也？說者以爲三代時人主之精誠徹於天，天視聽爲一，而後不能盡然；又謂太史失其官，躔野變其度，而不盡能一一應。然歟？否耶？當世宗末，海內報災異者不虛月，而其奏祥者輒上聞；然至於今，而寰宇寧晏，夷狄賓服，民心忻如也。即往者心翼小小，而聖主、喆輔交相爲儆，固借此益脩其德，以仰承仁愛。顧其數有可推，而其道有可盡者
translation_en:
… that of the Former Emperor? Let you students expound upon this with precision, and I, unworthy as I am, shall present your words to the Emperor.

Question: When specialists in astrological calendrics discuss calamities, auspicies, misfortune, and good fortune as clearly as pointing to the palm of one's hand, their theories fall roughly into three categories. First, there are distant cycles that do not change, such as the "Yang Nine" (yangjiu) and "Hundred and Six" (bailiu) epochs recorded in the Cosmic Cycles (Yuanhui). Second, there are near phenomena that can be calculated, such as solar and lunar eclipses and the regular orbital paths and encroachments of the Five Planets. Third, there are sudden occurrences that cannot be fathomed, such as the anomalous appearances of comets, unseasonable cold and heat, frost and hail, thunderbolts, and floods and droughts. Yet when one calculates heavenly phenomena to verify human affairs, the methods sometimes match and sometimes do not; and when one examines human affairs to verify heavenly phenomena, the numerical regularities are sometimes borne out and sometimes not. Why is this indeed so? Commentators hold that during the Three Dynasties, the utmost sincerity of rulers penetrated to Heaven, so that Heaven's seeing and hearing were one with humanity's, whereas in later ages this could no longer be fully realized; others say that the Grand Scribes lost their expertise and the celestial field-allocations altered their degrees, so that phenomena could no longer correspond one by one in every case. Is this so, or is it not? Toward the end of the reign of Emperor Shizong (r. 1521–1567), reports of calamities and anomalies from within the seas came in without a single month passing empty, while memorials reporting auspicious signs were likewise constantly presented to the throne; yet down to the present day, the realm is tranquil and at peace, the border peoples submit in allegiance, and the hearts of the people are joyful. Even when in recent times there have been moments of cautious trepidation over minor portents [?], the Sage Ruler and his wise Chief Ministers have mutually admonished one another, assuredly using these occasions to further cultivate their virtue so as to reverently receive Heaven's benevolent love. Still, are there numerical principles therein that can be calculated, and a Way that can be fully exhausted…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
乎諸生毋以不經對
問史有二家左氏志編年而太史公列傳
紀其得失亦大略相當自荀悅袁宏之
流祖左氏班固陳壽范曄之倫業司馬
由陳范而晉南北朝至勝國猶宗之而
左氏蓋寥寥也至宋涑水氏始略法其
凡而著通鑑業以佐人主治道而已
明興國大政閟於金匱石室而不得窺然以脩
金匱石室而不得窺然以脩史者徵之代出
===
人手其賢否不一也不至無矛盾否
國史家乘其亦可信而徵否吾欲用班固蘭
臺例盡出
國史之藏而使賢而才者司其事務合於昔
賢之所謂三長者而後成書宋以後事
別列爲編年而續涑水氏以備
人主乙夜之覽不識有可以當之者否不佞請
因諸君子以觀倚相之緒
問西漢尚事功不如東漢矜節義固也然
punctuated:
乎？諸生毋以不經對。
問：史有二家，左氏志編年，而太史公列傳紀，其得失亦大略相當。自荀悅、袁宏之流祖左氏，班固、陳壽、范曄之倫業司馬，由陳、范而晉、南北朝至勝國猶宗之，而左氏蓋寥寥也。至宋涑水氏，始略法其凡而著《通鑑》，業以佐人主治道而已。明興，國大政閟於金匱石室而不得窺，然以脩金匱石室而不得窺然以脩史者徵之，代出人手，其賢否不一也，不至無矛盾否？國史、家乘，其亦可信而徵否？吾欲用班固蘭臺例，盡出國史之藏，而使賢而才者司其事，務合於昔賢之所謂「三長」者而後成書；宋以後事，別列爲編年而續涑水氏，以備人主乙夜之覽，不識有可以當之者否？不佞請因諸君子以觀倚相之緒。
問：西漢尚事功，不如東漢矜節義，固也。然
translation_en:
…? Gentlemen, do not reply with uncanonical talk.

Question: In historiography there are two schools: Master Zuo (Zuo Qiuming 左丘明) recorded events chronologically by year, while the Grand Scribes (Sima Tan 司馬談 and Sima Qian 司馬遷) arrayed biographies and basic annals; their respective merits and defects are roughly balanced. Since the likes of Xun Yue 荀悅 and Yuan Hong 袁宏 took Master Zuo as their model, while the cohort of Ban Gu 班固, Chen Shou 陳壽, and Fan Ye 范曄 carried on the enterprise of Sima Qian, from Chen Shou and Fan Ye down through the Jin, the Northern and Southern Dynasties, and to the conquered dynasty [the Yuan], historians still followed Sima Qian's tradition, whereas followers of Master Zuo were few and far between. Not until the Gentleman of Sushui (Sima Guang 司馬光) in the Song did anyone roughly adopt Zuo's general principles to compose the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian 通鑑), taking it as his business simply to assist the ruler in the way of governance.

Since the rise of the Ming, the great affairs of state have been locked away in the golden coffers and stone chambers where none may peer into them [a duplicate phrase in the transcription is elided here]. Yet if we verify them through those who have compiled history, the accounts come from the hands of different people across generations, whose worthiness and capability are not uniform—can they avoid being free of contradictions? As for state histories and family chronicles, can they too be trusted and cited as evidence? I should like to follow Ban Gu's precedent at the Orchid Terrace (Lantai 蘭臺), bringing out all the treasures of the state history and having worthy and talented men take charge of the matter, insisting that they fulfill what former worthies called the "three strengths" [literary skill, scholarship, and insight] before completing a book; and for events after the Song, separately arranging them in chronological order to continue the work of the Gentleman of Sushui, so as to provide for the ruler's reading during the second watch of the night. I do not know whether there is anyone capable of undertaking this? Unworthy as I am, I beg to rely on you gentlemen to observe the legacy of Yi Xiang 倚相 [the learned scribe of Chu].

Question: That the Western Han esteemed practical achievement and was not the equal of the Eastern Han in prizing moral integrity is certainly true. Yet…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
事功之效能立見於國而節義則先養
名而晚收效且寺人黨錮之禍亦云有
以激之夫晉人貴清談六代開靡詞其
驅江左而削弱亡論已末宋之季明理
學者視其人何啻天壤乃入朝而奮袂
以稱恢復羣居而斂襟以談性命或者
謂宋勢之不復振亦與有力焉何也
國家履恒泰之運治平久而弘正間有倡古
文辭者其儔頗推揚之大槩少伸而多
===
抑其卓然欲以節明志者往往抗諫諍
而殉封疆君子稱之天下北孽虜南孽
倭搢紳先生投筆而脩羽檄之業暴起
騰貴及至於性命之學興雲合而景從
而一切下視為土苴為焦螟也是四者
於古之所矜尚同耶異耶其於世果孰
益而孰損也諸生有辨志之學否
問今天下為邊害者毋如虜為漕害者毋
如河即小夫孺子能言之而今虜已幸
punctuated:
事功之效能立見於國，而節義則先養名而晚收效，且寺人黨錮之禍，亦云有以激之。夫晉人貴清談，六代開靡詞，其驅江左而削弱，亡論已。末宋之季，明理學者，視其人何啻天壤？乃入朝而奮袂以稱恢復，羣居而斂襟以談性命，或者謂宋勢之不復振，亦與有力焉，何也？國家履恒泰之運，治平久，而弘正間有倡古文辭者，其儔頗推揚之，大槩少伸而多抑；其卓然欲以節明志者，往往抗諫諍而殉封疆，君子稱之；天下北孽虜、南孽倭，搢紳先生投筆而脩羽檄之業，暴起騰貴；及至於性命之學興，雲合而景從，而一切下視為土苴、為焦螟也。是四者，於古之所矜尚，同耶？異耶？其於世果孰益而孰損也？諸生有辨志之學否？
問：今天下為邊害者毋如虜，為漕害者毋如河，即小夫孺子能言之。而今虜已幸
translation_en:
…the effectiveness of practical achievements can be seen immediately in the state, whereas moral integrity and righteousness first cultivate reputation and only yield results late; moreover, the disasters of the eunuchs and the Partisan Prohibitions (Danggu) are also said to have been provoked by them. As for the men of the Jin dynasty valuing pure conversation (qingtan) and the Six Dynasties initiating florid diction, that these drove the regime south of the lower Yangtze into weakness goes without saying. Toward the end of the late Song, how could those who illuminated the learning of principle (lixue) be compared to those earlier men as anything less than heaven and earth? Yet when they entered court they shook their sleeves to proclaim restoration, and when they gathered in groups they straightened their collars to discourse on human nature and destiny; some say that the failure of Song power to revive was also partly their doing—why is that? Our dynasty has trodden a fortune of enduring peace; governance and tranquility lasted long, and during the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) eras there were those who championed archaic prose and diction, whose peers praised and promoted them considerably, though in general they were rarely advanced and mostly suppressed. Those who stood out in wishing to manifest their aspirations through moral integrity often offered defiant remonstrance or died as martyrs on the frontiers, and gentlemen praised them. When the realm suffered the scourge of the northern caitiffs in the north and the scourge of the dwarf pirates (Wo) in the south, gentry officials cast aside their brushes to cultivate the business of feathered military dispatches, rising suddenly to high rank and honor. And when the learning of human nature and destiny arose, followers gathered like clouds and trailed like shadows, looking down on everything else as mere dirt and dregs or as microscopic mites. Are these four trends the same as, or different from, what was prized in antiquity? Which of them truly benefits the world, and which harms it? Do you students possess the learning to discern aspirations?

Question: That in the realm today nothing is a greater menace to the frontiers than the northern caitiffs, and nothing is a greater menace to canal transport than the Yellow River, even petty men and children can state. Yet now the caitiffs have fortunately…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
款塞矣河幸一切徙去漕道通矣說者
乃尚謂虜款不足恃一旦而解盟而邊
患猶故也河徙不足恃一旦而横潰而
漕患猶故也卽胡以待之詩云迨天之
未陰雨徹彼桑土綢繆牖戶今所以綢
繆者何策也主計之臣議通海漕以助
河業已睹其效矣將遂漕海耶抑姑爲
道以俟緩急耶而功名之士尚欲計復
河套未已也夫海漕可暫通而河套似
===
不可復也亦能明其所以否諸生異日
爲
國家用覩玆二者恐不宜默默也其悉以對
punctuated: 款塞矣，河幸一切徙去，漕道通矣。說者乃尚謂：「虜款不足恃，一旦而解盟，而邊患猶故也；河徙不足恃，一旦而横潰，而漕患猶故也，卽胡以待之？」《詩》云：「迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖戶。」今所以綢繆者何策也？主計之臣議通海漕以助河，業已睹其效矣，將遂漕海耶？抑姑爲道以俟緩急耶？而功名之士尚欲計復河套未已也。夫海漕可暫通，而河套似不可復也，亦能明其所以否？諸生異日爲國家用，覩玆二者，恐不宜默默也。其悉以對。
translation_en: …submitted to our borders, and fortunately the Yellow River has completely shifted its course away, so that the Grand Canal transport route is clear. Yet commentators still say: "The submission of the northern caitiffs cannot be relied upon; should they one day break the covenant, the border troubles will be just as before. The shifting of the Yellow River cannot be relied upon; should it one day burst its banks and flood wildly, the troubles with grain transport will be just as before—how then shall we be prepared to meet them?" The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "Before the sky is dark with rain, I strip the mulberry roots and bind closely my window and door." What policies do we have today for such precautionary binding? The ministers in charge of fiscal planning have proposed opening sea transport to supplement the river route, and we have already seen its effectiveness. Shall we then permanently transport grain by sea, or merely maintain it as an alternative route to await emergencies? Meanwhile, men eager for achievement and fame still never cease plotting to recover the Ordos Loop (Hetao). Now, sea transport can be opened temporarily, whereas the Ordos Loop seems impossible to recover—can you also explain the reasons why? When you students are employed by the state in the future and witness these two matters, I fear it would not be fitting for you to remain silent. Respond in full to all of this.
