The achievement of all-encompassing regulation is communicated through words; although it has not yet reached the utmost breadth of instructive practice, those who look up to the promulgation of the canons of governance and obey the imperial instructions will never transgress them. From the hidden it thus becomes illustrious, just as what begins with the smallness of fine silk threads is followed by the greatness of a braided cord. In sum, when the sovereign issues commands like silk threads and braided cords, the world possesses the civil pattern of warp and woof; words indeed cannot be dispensed with. Precisely because when they go forth they are like braided cords, one must be cautious with them at their very inception when they are like fine silk threads. How much more so when his words are even greater than silk threads—what then will their going forth be like, and how could he lead the world with frivolous speech? Even so, this is not all. From this, the Left Scribe records them and later generations transmit them—which of these is not such words? Therefore Yi Yin 伊尹 told the King of Shang: "Great are the king's words!" and also said: "Pure is the king's mind!" Why is this? Because the mind is indeed that from which words issue. If one who wishes to be cautious in speech establishes sincerity in order to cultivate his words, then his words will have few faults and the world will take them as its model.

Second Session
Discourse
"When the Ruler's Will is Fixed, the Governance of the World is Accomplished"
Li Deng 李登

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭殷批據理揮霍亹亹數千言而忠義
之氣溢於詞表
同考試官教諭鍾批識遠思深蓋養之裕而發之粹
者用錄以式
考試官教授黃批詞指詳懇非苟作者
考試官教授郭批以雄才發真見佳哉
人主以一身而致天下之治者無他定其所以
治天下之本而已本者何志是也夫天下至廣
也萬幾至殷繁也歸而取足於吾至微之志而
===
日有餘者何也吾無志於治而聽吾不制之軀
以殉物之欲物羣起而入之吾甫有志而未定
而遽以其有限之聰明而究天下之聞見天下
得以聞見之不及者而蔽之𨠑𨠑乎擾擾乎治
日遠於我而吾不覺物爲主而我爲役吾志定
而天下之才用於我宰制萬物之柄在我而不
在物物爲役而我爲主我爲役是我先天下憂
也我爲主是我先天下理也是故奮然而師千
古之聖帝哲王以爲必可法者所以定此志也
punctuated:
同考試官教諭殷批：據理揮霍，亹亹數千言，而忠義之氣溢於詞表。
同考試官教諭鍾批：識遠思深，蓋養之裕而發之粹者，用錄以式。
考試官教授黃批：詞指詳懇，非苟作者。
考試官教授郭批：以雄才發真見，佳哉！
人主以一身而致天下之治者，無他，定其所以治天下之本而已。本者何？志是也。夫天下至廣也，萬幾至殷繁也，歸而取足於吾至微之志而日有餘者，何也？吾無志於治，而聽吾不制之軀以殉物之欲，物羣起而入之；吾甫有志而未定，而遽以其有限之聰明而究天下之聞見，天下得以聞見之不及者而蔽之。𨠑𨠑乎，擾擾乎，治日遠於我，而吾不覺物爲主而我爲役。吾志定，而天下之才用於我，宰制萬物之柄在我而不在物，物爲役而我爲主。我爲役，是我先天下憂也；我爲主，是我先天下理也。是故奮然而師千古之聖帝哲王，以爲必可法者，所以定此志也；
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Yin: Grounded in principle and sweeping in style, it flows tirelessly for several thousand words, while a spirit of loyalty and righteousness brims over the surface of the language.
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhong: Far-sighted in vision and profound in thought; this comes from one whose cultivation is abundant and whose expression is pure. It is hereby recorded to serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner, Professor Huang: The diction and intent are detailed and earnest; this is not the work of a careless writer.
Comment by Examiner, Professor Guo: Expressing true insight through vigorous talent—admirable indeed!
That by which a ruler, in his single person, brings about the governance of the empire is nothing other than establishing the foundation for governing the empire. What is this foundation? It is the will. Now, the empire is vast in the extreme, and the myriad affairs of state are complex in the extreme; yet if one turns inward to draw sufficiency from one's own most subtle will, there is more than enough day after day—why is this? If I have no will toward governance, and allow my unrestrained body to pursue the desires of external things, then things will rise up in swarms and invade it. If I have just begun to form a will but it is not yet settled, and I rashly use my limited intelligence to exhaust the sights and sounds of the empire, then the empire will be able to obscure me with what lies beyond my sights and sounds. Dizzily and chaotically, good governance grows daily more distant from me, and without my realizing it, external things become the master and I become the servant. When my will is settled, the talents of the empire are employed by me; the handle that directs and controls the myriad things rests in me and not in external things, so that things become the servant and I become the master. When I am the servant, I suffer anxiety before the empire does; when I am the master, I bring order before the empire does. Therefore, rousing oneself to take the sage emperors and wise kings of all antiquity as teachers, regarding them as models that must certainly be emulated, is the means to settle this will; …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
學古訓崇正學明善惡辨邪正俱所以端此定
也蓋程氏之言曰君志定而天下之治成甚矣
人主之志之不易定也晨辨色而至晦宴息其
居處靡匪雕甍重錦文繡也是以四體誘之也
其所進靡匪五齊八珍水陸之共也是以口誘
之也其所御靡匪曼聲冶容趙衞姝異之選也
是以耳目誘之也其所指使靡匪便辟善柔當
先而好爲逢者也是以頤氣誘之也然則人主
之一身其僅屬我者方寸耳不待遠而五官百
骸之用爭出其所誘以爲勝而所謂方寸者岌
岌乎日爲之動而不吾屬矣方寸之地旣日爲
之動而不吾屬則自數者之外天下復爭出其
近似者以誘之而其欲日益廣其志日益以不
定嗟乎人主之身非一人之身而天下之身也
是故志一移於女謁而章華叢臺之側膏首袨
服者出羔鴈壅而失時矣志一移於賄貨而析
秋毫者出民媮衣食以苟旦夕之命而室若掃
矣志一移於游畋而三河之選蹄出民不敢禾
punctuated: 學古訓、崇正學、明善惡、辨邪正，俱所以端此定也。蓋程氏之言曰：「君志定而天下之治成。」甚矣，人主之志之不易定也！晨辨色而至晦宴息，其居處靡匪雕甍、重錦、文繡也，是以四體誘之也；其所進靡匪五齊、八珍、水陸之共也，是以口誘之也；其所御靡匪曼聲、冶容、趙衞姝異之選也，是以耳目誘之也；其所指使靡匪便辟、善柔、當先而好爲逢者也，是以頤氣誘之也。然則人主之一身，其僅屬我者方寸耳。不待遠而五官百骸之用，爭出其所誘以爲勝，而所謂方寸者，岌岌乎日爲之動而不吾屬矣。方寸之地，旣日爲之動而不吾屬，則自數者之外，天下復爭出其近似者以誘之，而其欲日益廣，其志日益以不定。嗟乎！人主之身，非一人之身，而天下之身也。是故志一移於女謁，而章華、叢臺之側，膏首袨服者出，羔鴈壅而失時矣；志一移於賄貨，而析秋毫者出，民媮衣食以苟旦夕之命，而室若掃矣；志一移於游畋，而三河之選蹄出，民不敢禾…
translation_en: Studying ancient precepts, revering orthodox learning, clarifying good and evil, and distinguishing the crooked from the upright are all means by which to make upright this steadfastness of will. As Master Cheng [Cheng Yi 程頤] said: "When the ruler's will is fixed, the governance of All-under-Heaven is accomplished." How exceedingly difficult it is for a sovereign's will to be fixed! From the first light of dawn until he retires at nightfall, his dwellings consist of nothing if not carved roof-beams, layered brocades, and patterned embroideries—thus is he enticed through his four limbs. What is presented for his table consists of nothing if not the five ceremonial wines, the eight delicacies, and offerings from land and water—thus is he enticed through his mouth. Those who attend his person consist of nothing if not lingering voices, alluring countenances, and the choicest beauties of Zhao and Wei—thus is he enticed through his ears and eyes. Those whom he commands consist of nothing if not sycophants and smooth flatterers who rush to the fore and delight in pandering to his wishes—thus is he enticed through his slightest nod and air of command. Such being the case, in the sovereign's entire person, all that truly belongs to his own self is that square inch of the mind. Without even looking far afield, the functions of his five senses and hundred bones vie to bring forth their enticements to gain the upper hand, and what is called that square inch of the mind is precariously shaken day by day until it is no longer one's own. Once that square inch of the mind is daily shaken and no longer one's own, then beyond these several things, the whole world in turn vies to bring forth things of a similar sort to entice him; his desires grow broader by the day, and his will grows more unsettled by the day. Alas! The person of the sovereign is not the person of a single individual, but the person of All-under-Heaven. Therefore, the moment his will shifts toward female favorites and their solicitations, beside the Zhanghua and Cong Terraces there emerge women with anointed heads and resplendent garments, while the marriage gifts of lambs and wild geese are obstructed and the proper season for wedlock is lost. The moment his will shifts toward wealth and goods, there emerge men who split autumn hairs in their exactions; the common people scrape by for food and clothing merely to preserve their lives from morning to evening, and their homes are as if swept bare. The moment his will shifts toward pleasure excursions and hunting, the finest steeds of the Three Rivers region are brought forth, and the people dare not plant their grain…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
稼以待蹂踐矣志一移於土木而秦隴之材蔽
大江而出民併家而槁於楩梓之側矣志一移
於長生而方士出舍四民之業而談奇詭海則
有不返之楫矣志一移於黷武而良家子材官
者出九塞五嶺甌脫之地掊以待白骨矣誤不
盈方寸而禍立應於四海之遠萌不過頃刻而
膠結至於易世而不可解救吁亦大可畏哉明
主知其然故不求治於天下而求治於此志凜
凜焉若盂水之捧而不敢使有一毫之怠於一
===
切之可喜可動如所謂雕甍曲房重錦文繡者
若裋褐誅茅而不為誘所謂五齊八珍曼聲冶
容者若啗螘空花而不為誘所謂便辟善柔者
若廝養牧畯而不為誘吾日取古帝王之格言
以內驗於身心而外驗於人才以求所謂善惡
邪正之介而辨之吾敬天之志定而上帝儼然
而臨汝吾尊祖之志定而鬼神洋洋如在其上
如在其左右吾好賢之志定而彙征者響應於
巖谷之內吾去惡之志定而小人逆伏於魑魅
punctuated:
稼以待蹂踐矣；志一移於土木，而秦隴之材蔽大江而出，民併家而槁於楩梓之側矣；志一移於長生，而方士出，舍四民之業而談奇詭，海則有不返之楫矣；志一移於黷武，而良家子材官者出，九塞、五嶺、甌脫之地，掊以待白骨矣。誤不盈方寸，而禍立應於四海之遠；萌不過頃刻，而膠結至於易世而不可解救。吁！亦大可畏哉！

明主知其然，故不求治於天下，而求治於此志。凜凜焉若盂水之捧，而不敢使有一毫之怠。於一切之可喜可動，如所謂雕甍、曲房、重錦、文繡者，若裋褐、誅茅而不為誘；所謂五齊、八珍、曼聲、冶容者，若啗螘、空花而不為誘；所謂便辟、善柔者，若廝養、牧畯而不為誘。吾日取古帝王之格言，以內驗於身心，而外驗於人才，以求所謂善惡、邪正之介而辨之。吾敬天之志定，而上帝儼然而臨汝；吾尊祖之志定，而鬼神洋洋如在其上，如在其左右；吾好賢之志定，而彙征者響應於巖谷之內；吾去惡之志定，而小人逆伏於魑魅
translation_en:
…crops, only to await their being trampled under hoof. Once his will shifts toward lavish construction, timber from Qin and Long covers the Great River as it is floated out, and the people, whole families together, wither away beside the *pian* and catalpa logs. Once his will shifts toward immortality, magicians emerge, abandoning the occupations of the four classes of people to prattle about marvels and oddities, and on the seas there are oars that never return. Once his will shifts toward militarism, sons of good families and skilled soldiers come forth, and the borderlands of the Nine Frontiers, the Five Ridges, and the buffer zones are dug up to await their white bones. The error takes up less than a square inch of the mind, yet the calamity immediately reverberates to the farthest reaches of the Four Seas; its sprouting takes no more than an instant, yet it becomes so entangled that even after a change of reigns it cannot be untied or remedied. Alas, how greatly is this to be feared!

An enlightened ruler knows this to be so; therefore, he does not seek order in the empire, but seeks order in this very will of his. Reverently fearful, as if holding a bowl of water, he dares not allow a single hair's breadth of negligence. Toward all things that might delight or move him—such as what are called carved rafters, winding chambers, layered brocades, and patterned embroideries—he regards them like coarse woolens and thatched huts, and is not enticed. As for what are called the five ceremonial wines, the eight delicacies, alluring melodies, and seductive countenances, he regards them like eating ants or illusory flowers in the air, and is not enticed. As for what are called the obsequious and the artfully pliant, he regards them like menial servants and herdsmen, and is not enticed. Daily I take the maxims of the ancient emperors and kings to examine my own person and mind within, and to test men of talent without, seeking out the boundary between good and evil, the crooked and the upright, so as to distinguish them. When my will to revere Heaven is fixed, the Lord on High majestically looks down upon you; when my will to honor the ancestors is fixed, the spirits and gods are abundantly present, as if above and as if at one's left and right; when my will to love the worthy is fixed, those who advance together respond like an echo from within the crags and valleys; when my will to cast out evil is fixed, petty men cower in advance in the realm of demons and monsters…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之境而不敢動吾節用之志定而公私之庾不
待歲而自羨吾愛人之志定而老者佚少者無
夭札而壯者不盡力以至星辰序雨暘時五穀
登鳳皇儀於庭麒麟游於藪堯舜之所以獨稱
至者且以為志一動氣之驗而況其下者哉故
夫天下非乏才也吾志定則天下之才以其定
者為吾用而致吾志於天下吾志不定則天下
之才以其不定者為吾用而各致其私於天下
即亡論其甚者若所謂女謁賄貨遊畋土木長
===
生黷武而後不治也吾非不欲取其善者正者
而好之吾善惡邪正之介戰於中而賢不肖之
敵遽以戰於外賢者嘗逆閼吾欲而易不勝不
肖者嘗順導吾欲而易勝賢者一不勝則奉身
而求退不肖者不勝則多方以張其譽陰剌以
攻賢者所必救吏之直以觸吾所大諱譽則解
救則疑諱則怒吾志一不定而天下之事中變
矣故夫人主之於志也非精識不能辨也非至
敬不能持也非大勇不能決也內志定而朝之
punctuated: 之境而不敢動；吾節用之志定，而公私之庾不待歲而自羨；吾愛人之志定，而老者佚，少者無夭札，而壯者不盡力。以至星辰序，雨暘時，五穀登，鳳皇儀於庭，麒麟游於藪，堯、舜之所以獨稱至者，且以為志一動氣之驗，而況其下者哉！故夫天下非乏才也，吾志定，則天下之才以其定者為吾用，而致吾志於天下；吾志不定，則天下之才以其不定者為吾用，而各致其私於天下。即亡論其甚者若所謂女謁、賄貨、遊畋、土木、長生、黷武而後不治也，吾非不欲取其善者、正者而好之，吾善惡邪正之介戰於中，而賢不肖之敵遽以戰於外。賢者嘗逆閼吾欲而易不勝，不肖者嘗順導吾欲而易勝。賢者一不勝，則奉身而求退；不肖者不勝，則多方以張其譽，陰剌以攻賢者所必救，吏之直以觸吾所大諱。譽則解，救則疑，諱則怒。吾志一不定，而天下之事中變矣。故夫人主之於志也，非精識不能辨也，非至敬不能持也，非大勇不能決也。內志定，而朝之
translation_en: …the realms of mountain demons and dare not stir; when my resolve to economize on expenditures is fixed, public and private granaries will naturally overflow without waiting for a bumper harvest; when my resolve to love the people is fixed, the elderly will enjoy ease, the young will be free from premature death and pestilence, and the able-bodied will nothave their strength exhausted. Even to the point where the stars and constellations move in order, rain and sunshine come in their proper seasons, the five grains ripen abundantly, phoenixes display their majesty in the courtyard, and unicorns roam in the marshes—that by which Yao and Shun alone were acclaimed as the ultimate sages was moreover regarded as proof that when the will is unified it moves the vital force (qi), and how much more so for things beneath that! Therefore, the empire does not lack talent. When my resolve is fixed, the talents of the empire will serve me with what is fixed in them, carrying out my resolve throughout the empire; when my resolve is not fixed, the talents of the empire will serve me with what is unfixed in them, each pursuing his own selfish ends throughout the empire. That is to say nothing of extreme cases—where disorder only follows upon such things as female solicitation, bribery, excursion and hunting, grand construction, the pursuit of immortality, and the reckless use of military force. It is not that I do not wish to select the good and the upright and cherish them; rather, when the boundary between good and evil, perversity and rectitude battles within my mind, the rivalry between the worthy and the unworthy immediately breaks into battle on the outside. The worthy regularly go against and check my desires, and thus easily suffer defeat; the unworthy regularly accommodate and indulge my desires, and thus easily prevail. Once the worthy fail to prevail, they preserve their integrity and ask to retire; when the unworthy fail to prevail, they use every means to inflate their own reputation, secretly scheme to attack those whom the worthy are bound to rescue, and instigate [?] upright officials to violate my greatest taboos. When they are praised, my vigilance relaxes; when the worthy come to the rescue, I grow suspicious; when my taboos are violated, I become angry. Once my resolve wavers, the affairs of the empire undergo a sudden reversal midway. Therefore, as for a ruler's relation to his resolve: without refined discernment he cannot distinguish it; without the utmost reverence he cannot sustain it; without great courage he cannot decide upon it. When his inner resolve is fixed, then in the court…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
賢不肖未有雜進於吾前者也嗚呼以成湯之
聖爰正革而六服臣仲虺之所以戒之若恒主
曰志自滿九族乃離武周愼德之化浹而西旅
底貢厥獒太保乃以爲懼而用訓曰玩物喪志
又申之曰志以道寧夫定志之學豈少不足於
湯武哉而二公之所以諄偲而進說不已者何
也是亦可以惕然懼矣唐文皇之始其志若有
定於行仁義也故封德彝詘而魏徵之說伸而
貞觀治蓋未幾而志稍滿欲稍動高麗薛延陀
===
之役翠微玉華之繕隱然孽於十漸之時而不
自覺矣文皇之所謂定者非眞定而其於學淺
故也程氏之爲是言固所以示萬世人君之的
而要其時則不能無隱憂者當元祐之初政司
馬呂范諸賢用而慨然振刷欲幾聖帝哲王之
治天下若以爲君志之能定而不知其上束於
內敎之嚴而下安於欲竇之未啓耳無何紹述
之說行左右各以其誘進國是淆而司馬諸賢
爭之不能得君志之所謂定者安在也故靖康
punctuated: 賢不肖未有雜進於吾前者也。嗚呼！以成湯之聖，爰正革而六服臣，仲虺之所以戒之若恒主，曰：「志自滿，九族乃離。」武周愼德之化浹，而西旅底貢厥獒，太保乃以爲懼而用訓，曰：「玩物喪志。」又申之曰：「志以道寧。」夫定志之學，豈少不足於湯、武哉？而二公之所以諄偲而進說不已者何也？是亦可以惕然懼矣。唐文皇之始，其志若有定於行仁義也，故封德彝詘而魏徵之說伸，而貞觀治。蓋未幾而志稍滿、欲稍動，高麗、薛延陀之役，翠微、玉華之繕，隱然孽於「十漸」之時而不自覺矣。文皇之所謂定者，非眞定，而其於學淺故也。程氏之爲是言，固所以示萬世人君之的，而要其時則不能無隱憂者。當元祐之初政，司馬、呂、范諸賢用，而慨然振刷，欲幾聖帝哲王之治。天下若以爲君志之能定，而不知其上束於內敎之嚴，而下安於欲竇之未啓耳。無何，紹述之說行，左右各以其誘進，國是淆而司馬諸賢爭之不能得，君志之所謂定者安在也？故靖康
translation_en:
…the worthy and the unworthy have never indiscriminately advanced before me.

Alas! Even with the sagely virtue of Cheng Tang 成湯, when he undertook the righteous revolution and the six domains submitted as subjects, Zhong Hui 仲虺 admonished him as though he were an ordinary ruler, saying: "When the will is self-satisfied, the nine classes of kindred will become estranged." When the transforming influence of King Wu of Zhou's 周武王 careful attention to virtue had permeated everywhere, and the Western Lü 西旅 presented their mastiff in tribute, the Grand Guardian (Taibao 太保) took alarm at this and offered counsel, saying: "Dallying with curiosities saps the will." And he further elaborated: "The will is quieted through the Way." Now, could the learning of fixing the will have been even slightly deficient in Tang and Wu? Why then did those two ministers so earnestly and tirelessly press their advice? This, too, is enough to make one tremble with vigilance!

At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Wen of Tang 唐文皇 [Taizong 太宗], his will seemed fixed upon practicing benevolence and righteousness; thus Feng Deyi 封德彝 was rebuffed while Wei Zheng's 魏徵 arguments prevailed, and the Zhenguan 貞觀 era was well-governed. Yet before long, his will grew somewhat self-satisfied and his desires somewhat stirred; the campaigns against Koguryŏ 高麗 and the Xueyantuo 薛延陀, and the construction of the Cuiwei 翠微 and Yuhua 玉華 palaces, were already secretly sprouting at the time of the "Ten Gradual Declines" (Shijian 十漸) memorial without his even realizing it. What Emperor Wen called "fixing the will" was not true fixing, because his grounding in learning was shallow.

When Master Cheng 程氏 [Cheng Yi 程頤] spoke these words, he certainly intended to set forth the standard for rulers of ten thousand generations, yet considering his own time, he could not be without secret anxiety. At the outset of the Yuanyou 元祐 administration, worthies such as Sima 司馬 [Sima Guang 司馬光], Lü 呂 [Lü Gongzhu 呂公著], and Fan 范 [Fan Zuyu 范祖禹] were employed, and with high-minded vigor they carried out reforms, hoping to approach the governance of the sage emperors and wise kings. The empire seemed to believe that the ruler's will was mampu to be fixed, not knowing that above he was merely constrained by the strictness of palace instruction [under Empress Dowager Gao 高太后], while below he was content only because the floodgates of desire had not yet been opened. Before long, the doctrine of "continuing and述 following [Wang Anshi's New Policies]" (shaoshu 紹述) gained currency, those around him each advanced by means of their enticements, national policy became confused, and the followers of Sima and the other worthies contended against it in vain—where, then, was the so-called fixing of the ruler's will? Therefore, the Jingkang 靖康…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之禍吾以爲不在靖康而在熈寧帝志之不定
吾以爲不在熈寧而在元祐也當元祐時天下
之欲以所誘進者固已伏而窺帝志矣然則後
之有天下者慎無不定其志而爲小人窺也
同前
周弘瀹
同考試官敎諭左批〔詞旨疏暢筆力雅健錄之以式〕
𠊱
考試官敎授黄批〔精言傑思出人意表〕
===
考試官敎授郭批〔氣味冲然〕
論曰大君致天下之化有本而端天下之本有
機操而運之而化斯神矣夫以天下之大也而
大君以一人主之其幾務之繁而民物之夥紛
紛籍籍於統馭之下以望吾治而非有本焉以
操之機焉以運之則心日以勞神日以疲而天
下愈不可治誠知其本之所在而執其機則繁
以簡御博以約該斡旋於穆穆之中而振起於
昭昭之表如桴觸而響應形動而影隨有不知
punctuated:
之禍，吾以爲不在靖康而在熈寧；帝志之不定，吾以爲不在熈寧而在元祐也。當元祐時，天下之欲以所誘進者，固已伏而窺帝志矣。然則後之有天下者，慎無不定其志而爲小人窺也。

同前
周弘瀹
同考試官敎諭左批〔詞旨疏暢，筆力雅健，錄之以式𠊱。〕
考試官敎授黄批〔精言傑思，出人意表。〕
考試官敎授郭批〔氣味冲然。〕

論曰：大君致天下之化有本，而端天下之本有機；操而運之，而化斯神矣。夫以天下之大也，而大君以一人主之，其幾務之繁而民物之夥，紛紛籍籍於統馭之下以望吾治，而非有本焉以操之、機焉以運之，則心日以勞，神日以疲，而天下愈不可治。誠知其本之所在而執其機，則繁以簡御，博以約該，斡旋於穆穆之中，而振起於昭昭之表，如桴觸而響應，形動而影隨，有不知
translation_en:
… disaster of the Jingkang era, I hold, lay not in Jingkang (1126–1127) itself, but in the Xining era (1068–1077); and the instability of the emperors' resolve, I hold, lay not in Xining, but in the Yuanyou era (1086–1094). During the Yuanyou period, those in the realm who wished to advance themselves through enticements were already lying in wait and spying upon the Emperor's resolve. That being so, let future rulers who possess the empire take care lest they fail to fix their resolve and thus allow petty men to spy an opening!

Same topic as the preceding
By Zhou Hongyue 周弘瀹
Associate Examiner Instructor Zuo 左 comments: [The diction and purport are fluent and clear, the brushwork refined and vigorous; it is recorded here as a model for waiting candidates [? 𠊱].]
Examiner Professor Huang 黄 comments: [Choice words and outstanding thoughts that surpass ordinary expectations.]
Examiner Professor Guo 郭 comments: [Its flavor and spirit are serenely harmonious.]

The discourse reads: For the great sovereign to bring about the transformation of all under Heaven, there is a root; and for rectifying the root of all under Heaven, there is a pivot. Grasp and set it in motion, and transformation thereby becomes wondrous! Now, vast as the empire is, the great sovereign rules over it as a single man. With its myriad affairs of state so numerosos and its people and things so abundant—all bustling in profusion beneath his rule and looking to him for governance—if there is no root by which to grasp them and no pivot by which to set them in motion, then his mind will grow more toil-worn by the day, his spirit more exhausted by the day, and the empire all the more ungovernable. Truly, if he knows where the root lies and holds fast to its pivot, then complexity is governed through simplicity, breadth is encompassed through concision, things are turned and guided within profound stillness and roused to life in manifest brilliance—just as the drumstick strikes and the sound responds, or the form moves and the shadow follows, coming to pass without anyone knowing…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其然而然者矣人見大君之化之神也而孰知
其易簡直截若此哉本者何志是已機者何定
志是已君志定而天下之治成程伯子之言有
旨哉甞聞論治者曰樹之風聲彰之物采陳之
藝極訓之話言引之常秩約之紀綱禁之刑辟
使天下之事秩然惟吾之所欲而不敢違天下
之民肅然惟吾之所使而不敢攜貳而後天下
之治成玆顧略其文章條敎之節而歸之人主
心志念慮之微此其故何哉蓋的張而射者準
===
焉志有所期也獸伏而獵者從焉志有所獲也
志有期則神凝而不散志有獲則力專而不分
以不散之神重之以不分之力天下之事隨其
所爲罔不立就而何疑於治天下也乎噫甚哉
治天下者之不可不定其志也彼衷無所主者
感物而移念無所裁者因時而化臨政蒞治之
始其志漫無所定而惟優豫晏逸以自詭於恭
默無爲甚則朝更夕改且行且止而姑託言於
俟時要其終不怠玩且厭棄之矣況善惡易殽
punctuated:
其然而然者矣。人見大君之化之神也，而孰知其易簡直截若此哉！本者何？志是已。機者何？定志是已。「君志定而天下之治成」，程伯子之言有旨哉！

甞聞論治者曰：樹之風聲，彰之物采，陳之藝極，訓之話言，引之常秩，約之紀綱，禁之刑辟，使天下之事秩然惟吾之所欲而不敢違，天下之民肅然惟吾之所使而不敢攜貳，而後天下之治成。玆顧略其文章條敎之節，而歸之人主心志念慮之微，此其故何哉？蓋的張而射者準焉，志有所期也；獸伏而獵者從焉，志有所獲也。志有期，則神凝而不散；志有獲，則力專而不分。以不散之神，重之以不分之力，天下之事隨其所爲，罔不立就，而何疑於治天下也乎！

噫！甚哉，治天下者之不可不定其志也！彼衷無所主者，感物而移；念無所裁者，因時而化。臨政蒞治之始，其志漫無所定，而惟優豫晏逸，以自詭於恭默無爲；甚則朝更夕改，且行且止，而姑託言於俟時。要其終，不怠玩且厭棄之矣。況善惡易殽，
translation_en:
… how it happens. People witness the marvelousness of the great sovereign's transformative influence, yet who knows that it is as simple, easy, and direct as this? What is the root? It is simply the will. What is the pivot? It is simply fixing the will. "When the ruler's will is fixed, the governance of the world is accomplished"—how profound are the words of Master Cheng Bozi [Cheng Hao 程顥]!

I have heard those who discuss governance say: establish moral reputation for them, display emblematic distinctions to them, set forth standards and criteria for them, instruct them with maxims, guide them with constant order, bind them with laws and regulations, and restrain them with penal statutes, so that the affairs of the world are orderly according to whatever one desires without anyone daring to disobey, and the people of the world are reverently compliant with whatever one commands without anyone daring to be disloyal—and only then is the governance of the world accomplished. Yet here, he passes over the details of institutional forms and statutory instructions, and attributes it instead to the subtle workings of the sovereign's mind, will, and thoughts. What is the reason for this? Indeed, when the target is set up, the archer aims at it because his will has something it expects to hit; when the beast lies hidden, the hunter pursues it because his will has something it seeks to capture. When the will has an expectation, the spirit is concentrated and not scattered; when the will seeks a capture, the strength is focused and not divided. Taking an unscattered spirit and reinforcing it with undivided strength, whatever affairs of the world one undertakes will without exception be immediately accomplished—so what doubt could there be about governing the world!

Alas, how imperative it is that one who governs the world must fix his will! Those whose inner minds have no master are moved when stirred by external things; those whose thoughts have no restraint change along with the times. At the beginning of assuming administration and entering upon governance, their will is vague and unsettled, and they merely indulge in hesitant leisure and ease, deceiving themselves that they are practicing reverent silence and non-action; in extreme cases, they change policies from morning to evening, advancing and halting by turns, while provisionally making the excuse that they are waiting for the right time. Looking at how they end up, if they do not grow negligent and trifling, they will surely grow weary of it and abandon it altogether. Moreover, good and evil are easily confounded, …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
忠邪莫辨而吾以疑似兩可之見當其衝將以
爲善旋自疑之欲以爲惡又自是之旣以爲忠
復自遠之方以爲邪隨自信之而天下之變始
雜然交集於吾前而終不得其所當唯無本也
惟無機也大君者則不然誠知乎天下之治也
有本而圖天下之治也有機于是稽古正學純
心用賢明善惡之歸辨忠邪之分以聖人之訓
爲必可從以先王之治爲必可法自羲黃堯舜
以及禹湯文武其所以正心脩身以達之天下
===
者取以爲吾志之的百務未遑而其志之所定
固已先天下而立其極矣此志一定畢力以從
之其立朝之士佐下風而承德意者又知上意
之所在而不忍負其所期而一時事勢之紛至
沓來可駭可愕可歆可欲舉無足以變遷而移
易者蓋以羲黃堯舜禹湯文武之聖自待而以
羲黃堯舜禹湯文武之治待天下不緩之以縱
弛而亦不促之以紛更不專之以知慮而亦不
飾之以儀文不委之以偏任而亦不矯之以獨
punctuated:
忠邪莫辨，而吾以疑似兩可之見當其衝。將以爲善，旋自疑之；欲以爲惡，又自是之；旣以爲忠，復自遠之；方以爲邪，隨自信之。而天下之變始雜然交集於吾前，而終不得其所當，唯無本也，惟無機也。

大君者則不然。誠知乎天下之治也有本，而圖天下之治也有機。于是稽古正學，純心用賢，明善惡之歸，辨忠邪之分，以聖人之訓爲必可從，以先王之治爲必可法。自羲、黃、堯、舜，以及禹、湯、文、武，其所以正心脩身以達之天下者，取以爲吾志之的。百務未遑，而其志之所定，固已先天下而立其極矣。此志一定，畢力以從之。其立朝之士，佐下風而承德意者，又知上意之所在，而不忍負其所期。而一時事勢之紛至沓來，可駭可愕，可歆可欲，舉無足以變遷而移易者。蓋以羲、黃、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之聖自待，而以羲、黃、堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之治待天下。不緩之以縱弛，而亦不促之以紛更；不專之以知慮，而亦不飾之以儀文；不委之以偏任，而亦不矯之以獨
translation_en:
… and loyalty and treachery cannot be distinguished, while one confronts the brunt of things with dubious and ambivalent views. When about to regard something as good, one soon doubts it oneself; when about to regard something as evil, one then approves of it oneself; having regarded someone as loyal, one again distances oneself from him; just as one regards someone as treacherous, one immediately trusts him oneself. Thus the changes of the world begin to crowd together in confusion before one, and in the end one never finds the proper way to handle them—simply because there is no root, and because there is no pivotal mechanism.

The great sovereign, however, is not like this. Truly knowing that the governance of the world has a root, and that planning for the governance of the world has a pivotal mechanism, he thereupon examines antiquity for orthodox learning, employs the worthy with a pure heart, clarifies the ultimate distinction between good and evil, and discriminates the boundary between loyalty and treachery. He regards the instructions of the sages as certainly worthy of being followed, and the governance of the former kings as certainly worthy of being modeled upon. From Fuxi, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun, down to Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, he takes the means by which they rectified their minds and cultivated their persons so as to extend them to all under Heaven, and makes this the target of his own will. Before having leisure for the hundred affairs of state, what his will has settled upon has assuredly already established the supreme standard in advance of the world. Once this will is fixed, he exhausts his strength in pursuing it. Moreover, the gentlemen standing at court, who assist from below and receive his virtuous intentions, know where the sovereign's mind lies and cannot bear to fail his expectations. And as the circumstances and affairs of the moment come crowding in one after another—whether alarming and startling, or alluring and desirable—none at all are sufficient to alter or shift his resolve. For he holds himself to the standard of the sageliness of Fuxi, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, and he holds the world to the standard of the governance of Fuxi, the Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. He neither slackens it through laxity, nor hurries it through chaotic alterations; he neither monopolizes it through personal cleverness and calculation, nor embellishes it with mere ceremonial form; he neither abandons it to partial delegation, nor overcorrects it through solitary…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
斷不沮之以近小而亦不索之以虛無亹亹焉
如射之期的獵之願獲而大君之志定矣由是
志定則神聚神聚則思精思精則氣銳氣銳則
力專力專則事就緒事就緒則民易從民易從
而天下治蓋君不二於所示以倡其民民不亂
於所從以應其上上倡下應較若畫一而萬變
萬化惟其所參伍錯綜而莫不自恊於軌則由
是志羲黃而澹泊敦朴之治成矣志堯舜而風
動從欲之治成矣志禹湯文武而平成允殖咸
===
和永清之治成矣然則志也者其出治之本乎
定志也者其運治之機乎抑定志之云非執一
而已也舉末而後可以言本達變而後可以言
機夫惟志定則神完於內氣必從之神運於上
下必順之是以不求治於四海九州而求治於
古之賢聖不求治於古之賢聖而求治於吾之
心志念慮吾之志慮吾自定之吾自運之則率
其成憲治也于時取古制以變易之者亦治安
其無事治也于時與斯民而更新之者亦治何
punctuated: 斷，不沮之以近小，而亦不索之以虛無。亹亹焉如射之期的、獵之願獲，而大君之志定矣。由是，志定則神聚，神聚則思精，思精則氣銳，氣銳則力專，力專則事就緒，事就緒則民易從，民易從而天下治。蓋君不二於所示以倡其民，民不亂於所從以應其上。上倡下應，較若畫一，而萬變萬化，惟其所參伍錯綜，而莫不自恊於軌則。由是，志羲、黃，而澹泊敦朴之治成矣；志堯、舜，而風動從欲之治成矣；志禹、湯、文、武，而平成允殖、咸和永清之治成矣。然則志也者，其出治之本乎？定志也者，其運治之機乎？抑定志之云，非執一而已也，舉末而後可以言本，達變而後可以言機。夫惟志定，則神完於內，氣必從之；神運於上，下必順之。是以不求治於四海九州，而求治於古之賢聖；不求治於古之賢聖，而求治於吾之心志念慮。吾之志慮，吾自定之，吾自運之，則率其成憲，治也；于時取古制以變易之者，亦治。安其無事，治也；于時與斯民而更新之者，亦治。何
translation_en: …arbitrary decision, nor does he let it be discouraged by what is near and petty, or seek it in emptiness and nothingness. Untiringly—as an archer aims at the target or a hunter longs for his quarry—the great sovereign's resolve is fixed! From this, when resolve is fixed, the spirit is concentrated; when the spirit is concentrated, thought becomes refined; when thought is refined, vital energy becomes keen; when vital energy is keen, effort becomes focused; when effort is focused, affairs fall into order; when affairs fall into order, the people easily follow; and when the people easily follow, the realm is well governed. For the ruler does not waver in what he displays to lead his people, and the people are not confused in what they follow to respond to their superior. With the superior leading and those below responding in clear and uniform accord, amidst ten thousand changes and transformations, however intertwined and complex they may be, none fail to conform naturally to the proper standards. From this, when he sets his resolve upon Fuxi and the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi), a governance of tranquil simplicity and honest plainness is achieved; when he sets his resolve upon Yao and Shun, a governance where the people are moved as by the wind and follow his desires is achieved; when he sets his resolve upon Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, a governance of peaceful order, flourishing abundance, universal harmony, and enduring purity is achieved. If so, then is not resolve the root from which governance springs? Is not fixing one's resolve the pivot upon which governance turns? Yet what is meant by fixing one's resolve is not merely clinging to a single course; only after attending to the branches can one speak of the root, and only after comprehending change can one speak of the pivot. Only when resolve is fixed is the spirit whole within, and vital energy will surely follow it; when the spirit operates above, those below will surely obey it. Therefore, one does not seek governance in the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, but seeks governance in the worthies and sages of antiquity; one does not seek governance in the worthies and sages of antiquity, but seeks governance in the resolve and thoughts of one's own mind. When one's own resolve and thoughts are fixed by oneself and set in motion by oneself, then following established statutes is good governance, and at times taking ancient institutions and altering them is also good governance; resting in non-action is good governance, and at times making a fresh start with the people is also good governance. Why…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
則本端而末舉機運而變通此定說也治天下
者可以知所務矣抑君道卽天道也天道無心
而君道有志得無異耶嗚呼天道齊萬物而理
以宰之君道順萬變而志以定之志以定之守
一之君也理以宰之不二之天也不二之天守
一之君其本同其機同此乾坤之所以不毀而
參贊之所以有常也後之人以煩擾而配天之
健以空寂而象天之虛均之不知乾道矣不知
君道矣而胡以言治哉謹論
===
表
擬宋以敧器論賜宰臣王曾等謝表〔天聖元年〕
曾鳳儀
同考試官教諭朱批能悉敧器故事且得上下交儆意錄之
同考試官學正蕭批忠愛感激得大臣體
考試官教授黃批藻思駢辭足稱麗則
考試官教授郭批爾雅詳剴錄之
punctuated:
則？本端而末舉，機運而變通，此定說也，治天下者可以知所務矣。抑君道卽天道也，天道無心而君道有志，得無異耶？嗚呼！天道齊萬物而理以宰之，君道順萬變而志以定之。志以定之，守一之君也；理以宰之，不二之天也。不二之天、守一之君，其本同，其機同，此乾坤之所以不毀，而參贊之所以有常也。後之人以煩擾而配天之健，以空寂而象天之虛，均之不知乾道矣，不知君道矣，而胡以言治哉！謹論。
表
擬宋以《敧器論》賜宰臣王曾等謝表〔天聖元年〕
曾鳳儀
同考試官教諭朱批：能悉敧器故事，且得上下交儆意，錄之。
同考試官學正蕭批：忠愛感激，得大臣體。
考試官教授黃批：藻思駢辭，足稱麗則。
考試官教授郭批：爾雅詳剴，錄之。
translation_en:
… [Why] is that? When the root is upright, the branches are raised; when the pivot turns, transformations flow freely. This is an established principle, and those who govern the world may thereby know what they must attend to.

Yet the Way of the Ruler is none other than the Way of Heaven. Since the Way of Heaven has no deliberate mind while the Way of the Ruler has fixed resolve, are they not different? Alas! The Way of Heaven brings uniformity to the myriad things and governs them through principle; the Way of the Ruler accords with the myriad changes and settles them through resolve. To settle them through resolve is the mark of a ruler who holds to the One; to govern them through principle is the mark of a Heaven that is without duality. A Heaven without duality and a ruler who holds to the One share the same root and the same pivot. This is why Heaven and Earth (Qian and Kun) are never destroyed, and why the work of assisting in their transforming and nourishing operations remains constant. People of later ages who match the vigor of Heaven with restless meddling, or imitate the emptiness of Heaven with hollow quietude, are equally ignorant of the Way of Heaven and ignorant of the Way of the Ruler—how then can they speak of governance! Humbly discoursed.

Memorial

An Imitation of a Song-Dynasty Memorial of Thanks by Grand Councilor Wang Zeng 王曾 and Others upon Being Bestowed the Discourse on the Tilting Vessel (Qiqi lun) [First year of the Tiansheng era (1023)]

By Zeng Fengyi 曾鳳儀

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhu 朱 comments: "He is thoroughly familiar with the historical allusion of the tilting vessel and moreover grasps the meaning of mutual admonition between sovereign and minister. Record it for publication."

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Xiao 蕭 comments: "Loyal, devoted, and deeply moved with gratitude; it captures the proper bearing of a great minister."

Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Huang 黃 comments: "Refined thoughts and parallel phrasing, worthy of being called ornate yet rule-abiding."

Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Guo 郭 comments: "Elegant, detailed, and incisive. Record it for publication."

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
乾興元年某月某日具官臣王曾等伏蒙
聖恩以
先皇帝所著欹器論頒賜臣曾等謹奉
表稱
謝者伏以
聖主貽謨小物著持盈之訓
仁君繼志遺章發交儆之端
政體攸關
朝端具聳感將
===
恩切榮與懼幷臣曾等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上
言竊惟衢設堯樽廣黎庶太和之樂廟專
殷斝表季昆敦睦之誠湯盤之勸日新武
戶之虞風至雖制器尚象之理攸寓而居
安慮危之思尤深儀鑒于殷周公制宥巵
而示戒禮盡在魯孔子游威廟以興思滿
而覆虛而欹水哉是取中則昃盈則食天
且弗違自法言再衍於重黎迨說苑詳徵
於敬謹以至風人之撲滿尚猶借諷於滑
punctuated: 乾興元年某月某日，具官臣王曾等，伏蒙聖恩，以先皇帝所著《欹器論》頒賜臣曾等，謹奉表稱謝者。伏以聖主貽謨，小物著持盈之訓；仁君繼志，遺章發交儆之端。政體攸關，朝端具聳；感將恩切，榮與懼幷。臣曾等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟衢設堯樽，廣黎庶太和之樂；廟專殷斝，表季昆敦睦之誠。湯盤之勸日新，武戶之虞風至。雖制器尚象之理攸寓，而居安慮危之思尤深。儀鑒于殷，周公制宥巵而示戒；禮盡在魯，孔子游威廟以興思。滿而覆、虛而欹，水哉是取；中則昃、盈則食，天且弗違。自《法言》再衍於《重黎》，迨《說苑》詳徵於《敬謹》，以至風人之「撲滿」，尚猶借諷於滑…
translation_en:
On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of the Qianxing reign (1022), Your servants holding official titles, Wang Zeng 王曾 and others, having humbly received Imperial Grace in the bestowal upon Your servant Zeng and others of the Discourse on the Tilting Vessel (Qiqi lun) composed by the Late Emperor, reverently present this memorial to express our gratitude.

We humbly consider that the sagely ruler bequeathed his counsels, making manifest the admonition on preserving fullness through a small object; the benevolent sovereign carries on his intentions, initiating mutual vigilance between ruler and ministers through the posthumous essay. Because the principles of governance are bound up with this, all at court are deeply stirred; our gratitude grows ever more earnest with Your grace, and honor is joined with trepidation.

Your servants Zeng and others, in utmost fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and submit these words: We humbly reflect that setting out the goblet of Yao on the thoroughfares broadened the joy of supreme harmony among the multitude, and dedicating the jade cup of Yin in the ancestral temple displayed the sincerity of cordial amity among brothers. The basin of Tang exhorted daily renewal, and the doors of Wu warned against the coming of the wind. Although the principle of fashioning vessels by esteeming symbolic images resides therein, the thought of contemplating danger while dwelling in security is deeper still. Taking Yin as a mirror, the Duke of Zhou fashioned the admonitory goblet (youzhi) to display a warning; seeing that the rites were preserved in their entirety in Lu, Confucius visited the temple of solemn majesty [Duke Huan of Lu] and was moved to reflection. When full it overturns, and when empty it tilts—this lesson is drawn from water; when at midday the sun declines, and when full the moon is eclipsed—even Heaven does not contravene this principle. Ever since the Model Sayings (Fayan) elaborated on it again in the "Chong and Li" (Chongli) chapter, and down to the Garden of Persuasions (Shuoyuan) verifying it in detail in the "Reverence and Caution" (Jingjin) chapter, even to the "clay money-box" (puman) of the poets, which still borrowed subtle satire from humorous…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
稽彼長安之辭燈山香何裨治理况大業
之耿詢水戲僅托游觀雖遺模賴杜當陽
而復傳其至意如李賛皇者能幾名存實
泯物是人非無取嬉時有需
聖代我
文祖燕閒之候適詞臣候直之餘挹金勺而進
言屢廻
宸聽侈玉堂之盛事長播藝林
先皇帝雖麻弗麻損之又損告成封禪顧秦漢
===
之侈心不萌疊表禎祥而文景之謙讓恒
在爰自
天禧之載首頒
雲漢之章指禹桀之所繇假弦韋而為喻三時
召對酒德之論竝傳兩府拜觀肉食之徒自
警忽及
鼎成之日遺弓與兹器而竝留追惟
衣綴之時憑几聽遺音而逾烈豈期
初政再覩
punctuated: 稽。彼長安之辭燈山香，何裨治理？况大業之耿詢水戲，僅托游觀。雖遺模賴杜當陽而復傳，其至意如李賛皇者能幾？名存實泯，物是人非，無取嬉時，有需聖代。我文祖燕閒之候，適詞臣候直之餘，挹金勺而進言，屢廻宸聽；侈玉堂之盛事，長播藝林。先皇帝雖麻弗麻，損之又損，告成封禪，顧秦漢之侈心不萌；疊表禎祥，而文景之謙讓恒在。爰自天禧之載，首頒雲漢之章，指禹桀之所繇，假弦韋而為喻。三時召對，《酒德》之論竝傳；兩府拜觀，肉食之徒自警。忽及鼎成之日，遺弓與兹器而竝留；追惟衣綴之時，憑几聽遺音而逾烈。豈期初政，再覩
translation_en:
… humorous admonition. What benefit to governance were Chang'an's rhapsodies on lantern mountains and incense? Still less Geng Xun's (耿詢) water-powered spectacles of the Daye era (605–618), which served merely for sightseeing and pleasure. Although its surviving model was passed down again thanks to Du of Dangyang (Du Yu 杜預), how many have grasped its deepest meaning like Li of Zanhuang (Li Deyu 李德裕)? When the name remains but the reality is lost, and the vessel stays the same while the people have changed, it holds no value for a frivolous age, yet awaits a sacred dynasty.

During moments of leisure for our Cultured Ancestor (Emperor Taizong of Song), just as the literary officials finished waiting on duty, they drew water with the golden ladle and offered counsel, repeatedly turning the imperial ear; this was celebrated as a grand occasion of the Jade Hall (Hanlin Academy), long broadcast through the forest of letters. The Late Emperor (Emperor Zhenzong of Song), though enjoying peace, did not take peace for granted [reading 麻 as 休], diminishing his desires again and again. He announced the completion of the Feng and Shan sacrifices, yet the extravagant ambitions of Qin and Han never sprouted; auspicious omens were repeatedly presented in memorials, yet the modest deference of Emperors Wen and Jing of Han was ever present. Thus from the years of the Tianxi era (1017–1021), he first bestowed his resplendent imperial composition, pointing out the paths by which Yu succeeded and Jie fell, and borrowing the bowstring and soft leather strap as metaphors. Summoned for audience at three periods, the discourse on the "Virtue of Wine" was transmitted alongside it; when the Two Administrations (the Secretariat-Chancellery and the Bureau of Military Affairs) respectfully viewed it, the high-ranking officials ("meat-eaters") took warning for themselves.

Suddenly came the day when the tripod was cast (the emperor's death), and the fallen bow was left behind together with this vessel; recalling the moment when the funerary vestments were set out, leaning on the jade stool to hear his dying words made the grief all the more acute. How could we have expected that at the outset of the new administration, we would once again behold…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
睿謨茲蓋伏遇
○○○○
岐嶷夙成
元良蚤著朝
長信而仰承坤德若周文之事太任按
山陵而丕振乾綱如虞舜之放伯鯀甫及
諒闇之畢時惟不言言乃雍屬當
象魏之陳慮善而動動輒吉謂羹墻之
佇想無如恪守
===
洪規總琬琰之空懸不若恭敷
大訓啓
天章之秘閣開
寶笈之眞言
睿藻昭回恍若日星垂照
奎文飛動迥如河洛迎來一覽而重奉
龍顏載讀而永存龜鑑
音徽若接涕淚交零臣會等濫
先朝侍從之班叨揆地承君之選受
punctuated: 睿謨。茲蓋伏遇○○○○岐嶷夙成，元良蚤著。朝長信而仰承坤德，若周文之事太任；按山陵而丕振乾綱，如虞舜之放伯鯀。甫及諒闇之畢，時惟不言，言乃雍；屬當象魏之陳，慮善而動，動輒吉。謂羹墻之佇想，無如恪守洪規；總琬琰之空懸，不若恭敷大訓。啓天章之秘閣，開寶笈之眞言。睿藻昭回，恍若日星垂照；奎文飛動，迥如河洛迎來。一覽而重奉龍顏，載讀而永存龜鑑。音徽若接，涕淚交零。臣會等濫先朝侍從之班，叨揆地承君之選，受
translation_en:
…imperial counsels.

This is because we humbly encounter Your Majesty [○○○○], whose towering intelligence was early formed and whose supreme goodness was manifest betimes. Paying court at the Palace of Prolonged Credibility (Changxin Palace), You reverently uphold the maternal virtue of Earth, just as King Wen of Zhou served Tai Ren; inspecting the imperial mausoleums, You grandly assert the sovereign authority of Heaven, just as Shun of Yu banished Count Gun. Just at the conclusion of the period of mourning in silence, You did not speak before the time, so when You speak all are harmonious; right at the moment of posting the laws upon the palace gates, You deliberate on the good before acting, so whenever You act it is auspicious. Holding that yearning for the late sovereign in one's soup and on the walls is not as good as reverently adhering to his great regulations, and that merely hanging up jade tablets in vain is not as good as respectfully disseminating his grand instructions, You have unlocked the secret pavilion of the Pavilion of Heavenly Writings (Tianzhang Pavilion) and opened the true words of the precious book-chests. The imperial compositions shine and revolve, just like the sun and stars hanging down their light; the star-like calligraphy flies and moves, far surpassing the diagrams welcomed from the Yellow and Luo Rivers. At a single glance, we once more behold the Dragon Countenance; upon reading it again, we forever preserve a tortoise-shell mirror of warning. As if encountering his voice and glorious presence, our tears and snivel fall together.

Your servant Wang Zeng 王曾 and others, having unworthily occupied the ranks of attendants in the former reign, and having undeservedly been chosen to assist the sovereign in the seat of the chief councilors, have received…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
□再世銜戢終天敢不奉以撝謙益守盤盂之
戒挹而能損寧罹覆餗之譏感履盛之無
常馬匹自亡於幾望思惡盈之當避龜腸
不奪於朶頤伏願
遠師四守之格辭近體
二宗之成法高不危滿不溢長守貴於當年
父作之子述之允執中於永世臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
李登
同考試官教諭殷批〔頌美〕
聖德繼以忠愛而燁然皆古文辭士非第以觚藻鳴也他日得盡臣職亦左劵哉
punctuated:
□再世，銜戢終天。敢不奉以撝謙，益守盤盂之戒；挹而能損，寧罹覆餗之譏？感履盛之無常，馬匹自亡於幾望；思惡盈之當避，龜腸不奪於朶頤。伏願遠師四守之格辭，近體二宗之成法。高不危，滿不溢，長守貴於當年；父作之，子述之，允執中於永世。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策
第一問
李登
同考試官教諭殷批：〔頌美聖德，繼以忠愛，而燁然皆古文辭。士非第以觚藻鳴也，他日得盡臣職，亦左劵哉！〕
translation_en:
…[?] through two reigns, harboring gratitude for the rest of our lives. How could we dare not uphold this with modest humility, abiding ever more by the admonitions inscribed on basins and bowls; drawing back so as to diminish ourselves, how could we incur the ridicule of overturning the cauldron’s food? Moved by the impermanence of treading at the height of prosperity, when the horse is lost as the moon approaches full; mindful that theLoathing of fullness must be avoided, the tortoise’s sustenance is not snatched away by a greedy jaw. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will take as your distant model the standard words on the Four Preservations, and closely embody the established laws of the Two Ancestors. High yet not in danger, full yet not overflowing, long preserving nobility in the present age; what the father initiates, the son transmits, sincerely holding fast to the Mean for eternal generations. Your servants, unable to contain the extreme of our earnest and anxious reverence as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to the Sage, respectfully present this memorial of gratitude for the imperial hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Li Deng 李登
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Yin 殷: [He praises the Sacred Virtue and follows with loyal affection, all resplendent in ancient literary diction. This scholar does not merely make a name for himself with ornate writing; that he will one day fulfill his duties as a minister is assured as if by a tally!]

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鍾批創守一道吾子能備述
祖功宗德深仁厚澤焉言深得告君之體
考試官教授黃批忠愛必防其漸讜論也
考試官教授郭批是有志於格心者
聖人有先天而創大業者天下歸功焉有後天
而弘大化者天下歸德焉功不在一時而
在百世之後者其所貽者孫謀也德不在
一時而在百世之前者其所繩者
祖武也功與德不可岐而二者也故夫創有德
===
而守有功振廢之謂功垂訏之謂德二者
相因以成其盛者也執事頌
國美揚
聖哲欲
人主上登三下咸五而先以
高皇帝之大功與所以垂治安之道而至今者
為問甚盛心也愚敢以不敏對蓋孔子嘗
觀河洛而歎曰微禹吾其魚乎已又美齊
氏之績而曰微管仲吾其被髮左衽矣夫
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鍾批：創守一道，吾子能備述祖功宗德、深仁厚澤焉，言深得告君之體。
考試官教授黃批：忠愛必防其漸，讜論也。
考試官教授郭批：是有志於格心者。
聖人有先天而創大業者，天下歸功焉；有後天而弘大化者，天下歸德焉。功不在一時而在百世之後者，其所貽者孫謀也；德不在一時而在百世之前者，其所繩者祖武也。功與德，不可岐而二者也。故夫創有德而守有功，振廢之謂功，垂訏之謂德，二者相因以成其盛者也。執事頌國美、揚聖哲，欲人主上登三、下咸五，而先以高皇帝之大功與所以垂治安之道而至今者為問，甚盛心也。愚敢以不敏對？蓋孔子嘗觀河洛而歎曰：「微禹，吾其魚乎！」已又美齊氏之績而曰：「微管仲，吾其被髮左衽矣。」夫
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhong comments: Founding and preserving follow a single Way. You have been able to recount in full the achievements of the Ancestors and the virtues of the Forebears, along with their profound benevolence and generous grace; your words deeply grasp the proper form for advising the sovereign.
Examiner Professor Huang comments: Loyalty and devotion must guard against the incipient signs of decline—this is righteous counsel.
Examiner Professor Guo comments: Here is one who aspires to rectify the ruler's heart.
When a sage acts ahead of Heaven to found a great enterprise, the empire attributes achievement to him; when he acts in sequence with Heaven to broaden great transformation, the empire attributes virtue to him. When achievement does not rest in a single era but endures a hundred generations afterward, what it bequeaths is counsel for descendants; when virtue does not rest in a single era but reaches back a hundred generations before, what it continues is the footsteps of the Ancestors. Achievement and virtue cannot be bifurcated into two separate things. Therefore, in founding there is virtue, and in preserving there is achievement; reviving what has fallen into ruin is called achievement, and handing down grand plans is called virtue. The two build upon one another to bring about flourishing. Your Excellency praises the beauties of the dynasty and extols the sagely wisdom of our rulers, wishing for the sovereign to ascend to the level of the Three Kings above and match the Five Emperors below, and thus you first ask about the great achievements of the High Emperor [Taizu] and the Way by which he handed down peace and order down to the present day—this is a most magnificent intention. How dare I decline to reply on account of my dullness? Indeed, Confucius once gazed upon the Yellow and Luo Rivers and sighed, saying: "Were it not for Yu, we should all have been fishes!" Later he also praised the accomplishments of the house of Qi, saying: "Were it not for Guan Zhong, we should be wearing our hair unbound and buttoning our robes on the left." Now, …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
禹之功誠大然是時原隰之膏沃比耦而
黍稌者尚有之即不治猶不至盡天下而
不爲人至管仲之季北不過山戎跳梁燕
薊之末垂南不過楚蠶食江漢諸姬而已
而所謂楚者猶任中國之衣冠而談禮樂
管仲亦僅能膺懲而扞圉我耳孔子尚稱
服其仁而況於元以荒服奴虜之衆纍我
中國而悉臣之舉一世之豪傑頫首而事
椎結之主俛耳而聽侏離之令俗日化於
===
===
淫哇而不自覺故夫踐元而土者腥土也
臣元而人者行禽也
高皇帝起淮右提三尺劒以與羣雄角而勝之
乘勝而北驅虜而置之大漠之外乾坤闢
而再位日月滌而重朗海嶽奠而如故民
人復而冠履夫豈直得聖人之威哉即軒
轅遜五兵而大禹讓玄圭矣
高皇帝猶不自聖兢兢焉奉
大寳于盤水馭六馬以朽索雞鳴而起未辨色
punctuated: 禹之功誠大，然是時原隰之膏沃，比耦而黍稌者尚有之，即不治，猶不至盡天下而不爲人。至管仲之季，北不過山戎跳梁燕、薊之末垂，南不過楚蠶食江、漢諸姬而已；而所謂楚者，猶任中國之衣冠而談禮樂，管仲亦僅能膺懲而扞圉我耳。孔子尚稱服其仁，而況於元以荒服奴虜之衆，纍我中國而悉臣之，舉一世之豪傑，頫首而事椎結之主，俛耳而聽侏離之令，俗日化於淫哇而不自覺。故夫踐元而土者，腥土也；臣元而人者，行禽也。高皇帝起淮右，提三尺劒以與羣雄角而勝之，乘勝而北，驅虜而置之大漠之外。乾坤闢而再位，日月滌而重朗，海嶽奠而如故，民人復而冠履，夫豈直得聖人之威哉？即軒轅遜五兵，而大禹讓玄圭矣。高皇帝猶不自聖，兢兢焉奉大寳于盤水，馭六馬以朽索，雞鳴而起，未辨色
translation_en: …The merit of Yu 禹 was truly great; yet at that time, in the rich and fertile plains and lowlands, there were still those who plowed side by side and grew millets, so even had the waters not been controlled, it still would not have come to the point where the entire world ceased to be human. Down to the time of Guan Zhong 管仲, in the north it was no more than the Mountain Rong 山戎 rampaging along the far frontiers of Yan 燕 and Ji 薊, and in the south no more than Chu 楚 nibbling away like silkworms at the various Ji-surname states along the Yangtze and Han rivers; moreover, what was called Chu still wore the robes and caps of the Central States and discoursed on rites and music, while Guan Zhong was merely able to smite and chastise them and defend our borders. Even so, Confucius praised and admired his benevolence—how much more so when the Yuan 元, with its hordes of wild-zone slaves and caitiffs, bound our Central States and made subjects of them all! Every hero of the age bowed his head to serve a mallet-haired ruler and bent his ears to obey barbarous-tongued commands, as customs daily degenerated into lewdness and depravity without their even realizing it. Therefore, the land trodden under the Yuan was foul-smelling land; the people who served as subjects of the Yuan were walking beasts. The Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e., Emperor Taizu) rose up west of the Huai River, wielding a three-foot sword to contend with the rival warlords and defeat them; riding on victory, he marched north, expelling the caitiffs and placing them beyond the Great Desert. Heaven and Earth were opened anew and restored to their positions; the sun and moon were washed clean and shone brightly once more; the seas and mountains were settled as of old; the common people recovered their caps and shoes. Was this merely attaining the majesty of the sages? Even Xuanyuan 軒轅 (the Yellow Emperor) would yield to him in the five weapons, and Great Yu 大禹 would defer to him with the dark jade tablet! Yet the Exalted Emperor still did not regard himself as a sage. Cautiously andtremblingly, he held the Great Treasure as if carrying a basin of water, and drove six horses as if with rotten reins; he rose at the crowing of the cock, and before the colors of dawn could be distinguished…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而視
朝不以寒暑間者戒滋逸也
六宮取充位而已無燕趙二八之奉戒滋蕩
也賜租之
詔無歲而不下戒盡民也一記閱江樓幾成而
罷之終其身不爲
離宮別館戒游豫也去嶽瀆神祇之濫封而
歸本號戒褻神也滇詔近臥榻十七年而
始克平戒黷兵也朝鮮畔安南阻日本貳
===
閉關而聽其自服而不之討戒啓釁也廢
丞相析中書省而六之不得相彈壓戒專
國也五都督府握兵籍而不與調發兵部
得調發而不治兵戒專戎也釋襁褓之敎
凝旒垂拱而不置
母后席戒內干也外戚食國租而不與政戒外
移也
南面三十年而不改元薄海內外稱臣妾而不
加
punctuated: 而視朝，不以寒暑間者，戒滋逸也。六宮取充位而已，無燕、趙二八之奉，戒滋蕩也。賜租之詔，無歲而不下，戒盡民也。一記閱江樓，幾成而罷之，終其身不爲離宮別館，戒游豫也。去嶽瀆神祇之濫封而歸本號，戒褻神也。滇詔近臥榻，十七年而始克平，戒黷兵也。朝鮮畔、安南阻、日本貳，閉關而聽其自服，而不之討，戒啓釁也。廢丞相，析中書省而六之，不得相彈壓，戒專國也。五都督府握兵籍而不與調發，兵部得調發而不治兵，戒專戎也。釋襁褓之敎，凝旒垂拱，而不置母后席，戒內干也。外戚食國租而不與政，戒外移也。南面三十年而不改元，薄海內外稱臣妾而不加
translation_en: …and held court [before daybreak], never interrupting this on account of cold or heat, so as to guard against growing indolence. For the Six Palaces, he selected consorts merely to fill the ranks, without the service of sixteen-year-old beauties from Yan and Zhao, so as to guard against growing dissipation. Edicts remitting taxes were handed down without fail every year, so as to guard against exhausting the people. Once, after composing a record for the Yuejiang Tower (Yuejiang lou), when it was nearly completed he halted it, and throughout his entire life he never built detached palaces or separate villas, so as to guard against pleasure excursions. He abolished the excessive enfeoffments of the spirits of the sacred peaks and great rivers and restored their original titles, so as to guard against profaning the spirits. Even though the Dian region [Yunnan] lay right beside his couch, it was only after seventeen years that he conquered and pacified it, so as to guard against the wanton use of arms. When Chosŏn [Korea] wavered, Annam obstructed, and Japan proved duplicitous, he closed the passes and left them to submit of their own accord rather than launching punitive expeditions against them, so as to guard against provoking border hostilities. He abolished the Grand Councilor (chengxiang) and divided the Secretariat (zhongshu sheng) into the Six Ministries so that none could dominate the others, so as to guard against the monopolization of state power. The Five Chief Military Commissions (wu dudu fu) held the military registers but had no part in mobilizing or dispatching troops, while the Ministry of War (bingbu) had the authority to mobilize and dispatch troops but did not directly command soldiers, so as to guard against the monopolization of military power. Setting aside the tutelage of infancy, the ruler sat with solemn crown tassels and robes hanging down, without establishing a seat for an Empress Dowager [to rule as regent], so as to guard against interference from the inner palace. Consort clans lived off state stipends but did not participate in governance, so as to guard against authority shifting to maternal relatives. He reigned facing south for thirty years without changing his era name, and although all within and beyond the seas declared themselves his subjects and handmaidens, he did not add…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
徽號戒侈心也
高皇帝雖以
神武蓋一世而抑其才以下一世之賢士其尊
在
九重而洞徹其肺腑以與閭閻之志通其開闢
之績足以當
天心是故歷十餘祀而
天眷益厚其深澤膠固於民志是故歷危疑震
撼之際而不動其紀法足以綱維乎後代
===
是故指鹿訓狐之輩欲竊之而不能久執
事之所稱
高皇帝者功而愚則謂
高皇帝之所長有天下者不盡以功也繼
高皇而聖者莫若
成祖人見其聯數十萬之眾垂百戰而再造
區夏
六龍之駕四出塞而單于請
命餘皇之師徧海內而越裳重譯凡有血氣莫
punctuated: 徽號，戒侈心也。高皇帝雖以神武蓋一世，而抑其才以下一世之賢士；其尊在九重，而洞徹其肺腑以與閭閻之志通。其開闢之績，足以當天心，是故歷十餘祀而天眷益厚；其深澤膠固於民志，是故歷危疑震撼之際而不動；其紀法足以綱維乎後代，是故指鹿訓狐之輩欲竊之而不能久。執事之所稱高皇帝者，功；而愚則謂高皇帝之所長有天下者，不盡以功也。繼高皇而聖者，莫若成祖。人見其聯數十萬之眾，垂百戰而再造區夏；六龍之駕四出塞，而單于請命；餘皇之師徧海內，而越裳重譯；凡有血氣，莫
translation_en: …honorific titles, as a precaution against an extravagant heart. Although the High Emperor (Gao Huangdi, i.e., the Hongwu Emperor) surpassed his entire generation in divine martial prowess, he restrained his own talents so as to humble himself before the worthy scholars of the age; though his exalted station was within the ninefold palace enclosures, he laid bare his innermost thoughts so as to communicate with the aspirations of the common folk in their villages. His achievements in founding the realm were sufficient to match the mind of Heaven, and therefore after more than ten generations Heaven's favor has grown ever deeper; his profound beneficence was firmly bound to the people's will, and therefore even when passing through moments of crisis, doubt, and upheaval, it remained unshaken; his regulations and laws were sufficient to serve as the guiding framework for posterity, and therefore even when those of the ilk who point at a deer and call it a horse or train foxes to cry out sought to usurp power, they could not endure for long. What you, sir, praise in the High Emperor is his meritorious achievement; yet I in my simplicity would say that the means by which the High Emperor secured enduring possession of All Under Heaven did not lie entirely in meritorious achievement. Among those who succeeded the High Emperor in sageliness, none equaled the Ancestor of Accomplishment (Chengzu, i.e., the Yongle Emperor). People see that he marshaled armies of several hundred thousand men and fought nearly a hundred battles to refashion the Chinese realm; that his imperial carriage drawn by six dragons went forth beyond the frontier four times until the Chanyu begged for commands; and that his fleets of great warships ranged across the seas until peoples as distant as Yuechang came through multiple interpreters—so that among all living beings with blood and breath, there were none who did not…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
不尊親以爲是
成祖功乎不知其大指乃在親近儒臣杜絕女
謁表章六經却請封禪而所謂功者不與
也繼
成祖而聖者莫若
孝皇其媺政固不可更僕數也大要在奉
兩宮睦諸邸
御經筵
親朝政禮耆舊優言路畏天警悲人窮躬節儉
===
敦仁恕蓋十八年如一日焉人以爲
孝皇德乎哉
鼎成之日而深山邃壑田畯紅女號泣思慕
若孺子之於慈父母故内訌於瑾雄寧彬
外躙於鐇濠劉齊藍鄢輩而天下晏如也
是則
孝皇之功所以不朽也我
主上御極之載距
高帝戊申所二百餘矣天道運而人事應之煥
punctuated: 不尊親，以爲是成祖功乎？不知其大指乃在親近儒臣，杜絕女謁，表章六經，却請封禪，而所謂功者不與也。繼成祖而聖者，莫若孝皇。其媺政固不可更僕數也，大要在奉兩宮、睦諸邸、御經筵、親朝政、禮耆舊、優言路、畏天警、悲人窮、躬節儉、敦仁恕，蓋十八年如一日焉。人以爲孝皇德乎哉？鼎成之日，而深山邃壑、田畯紅女，號泣思慕，若孺子之於慈父母。故内訌於瑾、雄、寧、彬，外躙於鐇、濠、劉、齊、藍、鄢輩，而天下晏如也。是則孝皇之功所以不朽也。我主上御極之載，距高帝戊申所二百餘矣。天道運而人事應之，煥
translation_en: …did not honor and love him—would they consider this to be the achievement of Chengzu [the Yongle Emperor]? They do not know that his grand purpose actually lay in keeping Confucian officials close, barring female petitioners from the court, exalting the Six Classics, and rejecting requests to perform the feng and shan sacrifices, whereas what people call "achievements" had no part in it. Among those who succeeded Chengzu in sagehood, none could match Emperor Xiao [the Hongzhi Emperor]. His admirable policies certainly cannot be counted even if one changes servants to keep tally, yet the main essentials lay in serving the Two Palaces, maintaining harmony among the princely establishments, attending the Classics Colloquium, personally overseeing court administration, treating veteran elders with ritual courtesy, favoring the avenues of remonstrance, standing in awe of Heaven's warnings, grieving over the people's distress, personally practicing frugality, and cultivating benevolence and forbearance—for eighteen years as if a single day. Would people consider this merely the virtue of Emperor Xiao? On the day the tripod was cast [i.e., when the emperor passed away], in deep mountains and remote valleys, farmhands and weaving women wailed and yearned for him like young children for their loving parents. Therefore, although the realm suffered internal subversion from [Liu] Jin, [Zhang] Xiong, [Qian] Ning, and [Jiang] Bin, and external trampling by the likes of [Zhu] Zhifan, [Zhu] Chenhao, Liu [Liu], Qi [Yanming], Lan [Tingrui], and Yan [Benshu], the empire remained tranquil. This, then, is why the achievement of Emperor Xiao is imperishable. The year in which our reigning Sovereign ascended the throne is some two hundred years and more distant from the wushen year [1368] of the High Emperor [the Hongwu Emperor]. The Way of Heaven revolves and human affairs respond to it, brilliantly…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
然鼎革以昭
中興之治是天下之大期也屬者歲頗登匈
奴解辮南越授首無兵革之警中外得以
精意而承令是天下之大機也
主上以冲睿握
大寶凝然不動聲色尊嚴若神委政耆碩講明
經誼一二元老相與夾輔內外
宮府一體政不旁落即書史所載周成漢昭
之世何敢望萬一焉是天下之大本也期
===
不可忽機不可失而本不可不預培而默
滋今虎觀諸儒日横經而講者無非三代
帝王之訓而大臣之所進說圖解其善惡
凜乎萬世龜鑑也第不知燕閒濩獲之際
亦嘗內驗之身心而外驗政事乎
人主一身父母宗子其精神上與天相流通而
下與萬姓不隔者也上帝臨汝無貳爾心
一夫不獲恫瘝乃身蓋凜乎其可畏而惻
乎其不容已者也故
punctuated: 然鼎革，以昭中興之治，是天下之大期也。屬者歲頗登，匈奴解辮，南越授首，無兵革之警，中外得以精意而承令，是天下之大機也。主上以冲睿握大寶，凝然不動聲色，尊嚴若神，委政耆碩，講明經誼，一二元老相與夾輔內外，宮府一體，政不旁落，即書史所載周成、漢昭之世，何敢望萬一焉？是天下之大本也。期不可忽，機不可失，而本不可不預培而默滋。今虎觀諸儒日横經而講者，無非三代帝王之訓；而大臣之所進說圖解，其善惡凜乎萬世龜鑑也。第不知燕閒濩獲之際，亦嘗內驗之身心而外驗政事乎？人主一身，父母宗子，其精神上與天相流通，而下與萬姓不隔者也。「上帝臨汝，無貳爾心。」「一夫不獲，恫瘝乃身。」蓋凜乎其可畏，而惻乎其不容已者也。故
translation_en:
…renewing and transforming all things so as to manifest the governance of a dynastic restoration—this is the great appointed epoch of the realm. Recently, the harvests have been quite abundant, the Xiongnu have unbound their queues in submission, and the Southern Yue have offered up their heads; there are no alarms of war, and those within and without the court are able to concentrate their minds on carrying out orders—this is the great opportunity of the realm. His Majesty holds the Great Treasure in his youthful wisdom, composed and unmoved in voice or countenance, august as a spirit, entrusting governance to venerable and eminent ministers and elucidating the meanings of the Classics. One or two elder statesmen join in assisting both inside and outside the court; the Palace and the Government form a single body, and political authority does not fall into side hands. Even the reigns of King Cheng of Zhou (Zhou Cheng) and Emperor Zhao of Han (Han Zhao) recorded in the histories—how could they dare hope to match even a ten-thousandth part of this? This is the great foundation of the realm.

The appointed epoch must not be neglected, the opportunity must not be lost, and the foundation must not fail to be cultivated in advance and silently nourished. Today, what the scholars of the White Tiger Hall (Huguan) daily expound with the Classics open before them is nothing other than the instructions of the emperors and kings of the Three Dynasties; and the explanations and illustrated commentaries presented by the grand ministers, showing good and evil, are awe-inspiring mirrors for ten thousand generations. Yet one does not know whether, in moments of private leisure and seclusion [?], His Majesty also examines them inwardly in his own person and mind, and tests them outwardly in the affairs of governance?

The sovereign in his single person is the eldest son of the great lineage of Heaven and Earth, the parents of all; his vital spirit communicates above with Heaven and is not separated below from the myriad people. "God on High looks down upon you; have no duplicity in your heart." "If a single man does not find his place, it is as pain and sickness in your own person." Indeed, how awe-inspiringly fearful this is, and how compassionately irrepressible! Therefore…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
人主之念不可使少怠懼其日安於佚也緣詐
不可使早開懼其旁入於欲竇也才不可
使有餘懼其求於治之外也左右不可使
便辟懼其唯言而莫與違也我
二祖
一宗之政不下榻而可以按求至二帝三王之
心法又不在簡冊而在方寸耳
人主中心無爲以守至正公卿大夫日取
祖宗法夾持之如是而財不裕民不安夷狄不
賓服禮樂敎化不漸興者吾不信也夫以
高皇帝之烈崔巍昭烜與天地竝而
後皇以厪厪守成之政仰而思媲不亦計左失
當哉而愚復以厪厪守成之說進得無益
其左也雖然
人主薄近代陋
舊章以爲非至治之績而必欲上等於堯舜其
志非不恢乎大也然出之不以本而行之
不以漸掇拾經史之陳言而施之不相入
punctuated: 人主之念，不可使少怠，懼其日安於佚也；緣詐不可使早開，懼其旁入於欲竇也；才不可使有餘，懼其求於治之外也；左右不可使便辟，懼其唯言而莫與違也。我二祖一宗之政，不下榻而可以按求；至二帝三王之心法，又不在簡冊而在方寸耳。人主中心無爲，以守至正，公卿大夫日取祖宗法夾持之，如是而財不裕、民不安、夷狄不賓服、禮樂敎化不漸興者，吾不信也。夫以高皇帝之烈，崔巍昭烜，與天地竝，而後皇以厪厪守成之政，仰而思媲，不亦計左失當哉？而愚復以厪厪守成之說進，得無益其左也？雖然，人主薄近代、陋舊章，以爲非至治之績，而必欲上等於堯、舜，其志非不恢乎大也。然出之不以本，而行之不以漸，掇拾經史之陳言，而施之不相入
translation_en:
… the ruler's thoughts must not be allowed the slightest laxity, for fear that he will grow daily more comfortable in idleness; opportunities for deceit must not be allowed to open early, for fear that they will slip sideways into the apertures of desire; talent must not be allowed to be in excess, for fear that he will seek after things beyond good governance; and those in his entourage must not be allowed to be sycophantic, for fear that they will merely echo his words and none will oppose him. The governance of our Two Founders and One Ancestor [Taizu, Chengzu, and Xuanzong/Xiaozong] can be examined and sought without even descending from one's couch; as for the mental discipline (xinfa) of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, it resides not in bamboo slips and books, but right within the square inch of the heart. If the ruler remains non-purposive (wuwei) in his heart so as to guard the utmost rectitude, and the excellencies, ministers, and grand masters daily take the laws of the ancestors to uphold and assist him from either side—if, doing this, wealth is not abundant, the people are not at peace, the Yi and Di barbarians do not submit as guests, and rites, music, and moral transformation do not gradually flourish, I would not believe it.

Now, given the illustrious achievements of the High Emperor [Taizu], towering and brilliantly radiant, standing on a par with Heaven and Earth, if a later sovereign, through a governance of merely maintaining the existing order, looks up and hopes to match him, is that not a mistaken and inappropriate calculation? And if I, in my foolishness, again offer the doctrine of merely maintaining the existing order, would that not compound the mistake? Even so, when a ruler disdains recent eras and scorns the old statutes, considering them not to be the achievements of supreme governance, and insists on equaling Yao and Shun above, his ambition is certainly grand and expansive. Yet if he brings it forth without grounding it in the root, and carries it out without proceeding gradually—picking up stale words from the Classics and Histories and applying them to incompatible…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之俗强物之情而就我此王安石之所欣
然以興而韓富司馬之所愀然而深憂者
也孔子曰如有王者必世而後仁又曰無
欲速無見小利無欲速則必求所以寛收
其效者無見小利則必有所𠯁究其大者
請更得從容而愚始敢以文帝之謙讓而
未遑者一進
第二問
曾鳳儀
===
同考試官教諭朱 批 該洽之學精覈之識忠愛之忱
俱於是策見之
同考試官學正蕭 批 象緯菑祥天官家類能言之至
其所以格天者自非博雅深識之士弗能悉也此策條答輿衍璨若星懸末
於交儆三致意焉其達天人之際而懷忠思獻者乎
考試官教授黃 批 歸重於脩省尤見忠愛
考試官教授郭 批 論脩德格天有裨治道
執事發策而以上天之運象與災祥之應
否為問諸生鄙人也上之不能窮神知化
punctuated:
之俗，强物之情而就我，此王安石之所欣然以興，而韓、富、司馬之所愀然而深憂者也。孔子曰：「如有王者，必世而後仁。」又曰：「無欲速，無見小利。」無欲速，則必求所以寛收其效者；無見小利，則必有所𠯁究其大者。請更得從容，而愚始敢以文帝之「謙讓而未遑」者一進。

第二問
曾鳳儀
同考試官教諭朱〔批：該洽之學，精覈之識，忠愛之忱，俱於是策見之。〕
同考試官學正蕭〔批：象緯菑祥，天官家類能言之；至其所以格天者，自非博雅深識之士弗能悉也。此策條答輿衍，璨若星懸，末於交儆三致意焉，其達天人之際而懷忠思獻者乎！〕
考試官教授黃〔批：歸重於脩省，尤見忠愛。〕
考試官教授郭〔批：論脩德格天，有裨治道。〕

執事發策，而以上天之運象與災祥之應否為問。諸生，鄙人也。上之，不能窮神知化，
translation_en:
… Incompatible customs, and forcing the nature of things to conform to oneself—this is what Wang Anshi 王安石 delightedly rose up to undertake, and what Han Qi 韓琦, Fu Bi 富弼, and Sima Guang 司馬光 looked upon with sorrow and deep anxiety. Confucius said: "If a true king were to arise, it would surely take a generation before benevolence prevailed." He also said: "Do not desire quick results; do not look to small advantages." If one does not desire quick results, one will surely seek the means to reap results with forbearance; if one does not look to small advantages, one will surely have the wherewithal to fully investigate what is great. I beg that we be granted more unhurried time, and only then would this foolish student dare to present the example of Emperor Wen of Han, who "humbly declined and had not yet found the leisure."

Second Policy Question
Zeng Fengyi 曾鳳儀
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Zhu 朱, comments: "Comprehensive learning, precise and incisive insight, and sincere loyalty and affection for the sovereign are all evident in this policy essay."
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Xiao 蕭, comments: "Astronomical phenomena and portents of disaster and auspiciousness are things that specialists in astrology are generally able to speak of; as for the means by which to move Heaven, none but a scholar of broad refinement and deep insight could fully expound them. This policy essay answers item by item with rich abundance, shining brightly like stars suspended in the sky, and at the close it repeatedly stresses mutual admonition. Is he not one who comprehends the nexus of Heaven and humankind and cherishes loyalty with a desire to offer counsel?"
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Huang 黃, comments: "Placing the ultimate emphasis on self-cultivation and introspection especially shows loyalty and affection for the sovereign."
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Guo 郭, comments: "Its discussion of cultivating virtue to move Heaven is beneficial to the way of governance."

Your Reverence has issued the policy question, asking about the cyclical revolutions and phenomena of High Heaven and whether disasters and auspicious portents correspond to human affairs. I, a student, am a rustic person. Above, I cannot fathom the marvelous and know transformation…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以契上帝陟降之精而下之束於制不能
窺見天官推步占候之法毋乃以臆問而
令諸生以臆對乎雖然竊有以窺問者之
旨不在天而在人也蓋執事之問三而人
事不與焉其曰陽九百六者自然之運也
載於太乙肘後甚詳曰凡四百五十六年
而一陽九二百八十八年而一百六陽九
奇數也爲陽數窮百六陰數也爲陰數窮
皆所謂厄候也攷之羿浞而得陽九七周
===
赧而得陽九八漢延熹光和而得陽九九
隋大業而得陽九十周厲幽而其間得百
六十二敬王而得百六十三六國與秦之
際而得百六十四晉爲十六國而得百六
之數極而反於一五代而得百六之數三
其分裂乖散可謂章章應矣然舜禹而得
百六之數七小甲雍巳而得陽九之數五
百六之數九庚乙武丁而得陽九之數六
不降而得百六之數八盤庚小辛而得百
punctuated: 以契上帝陟降之精，而下之束於制，不能窺見天官推步占候之法，毋乃以臆問而令諸生以臆對乎？雖然，竊有以窺問者之旨，不在天而在人也。蓋執事之問三，而人事不與焉。其曰「陽九」、「百六」者，自然之運也，載於《太乙肘後》甚詳。曰：凡四百五十六年而一陽九，二百八十八年而一百六。陽九，奇數也，爲陽數窮；百六，陰數也，爲陰數窮，皆所謂厄候也。攷之羿、浞而得陽九七，周赧而得陽九八，漢延熹、光和而得陽九九，隋大業而得陽九十；周厲、幽而其間得百六十二，敬王而得百六十三，六國與秦之際而得百六十四，晉爲十六國而得百六之數極而反於一，五代而得百六之數三，其分裂乖散，可謂章章應矣。然舜、禹而得百六之數七，小甲、雍巳而得陽九之數五、百六之數九，庚乙、武丁而得陽九之數六，不降而得百六之數八，盤庚、小辛而得百
translation_en:
… so as to accord with the subtle essence of the Lord on High's ascent and descent; and at the lower level, being bound by state regulations, I am unable to peer into the astronomical officials' methods of calendrical calculation and divination by celestial signs. Would this not be asking by conjecture and making the students reply by conjecture? Even so, I venture to have glimpsed the intent of the questioner: it lies not in Heaven, but in human affairs.

Now, Your Excellency's questions are three, and human affairs are not explicitly among them. What is called "Yang Nine" (yangjiu) and "Hundred Six" (bailiu) refers to the cycles of nature, which are recorded in great detail in the Taiyi Elbow-Side Handbook (Taiyi zhouhou). It states that every four hundred and fifty-six years there is one Yang Nine, and every two hundred and eighty-eight years there is one Hundred Six. Yang Nine is an odd number, representing the exhaustion of yang numbers; Hundred Six is an even number, representing the exhaustion of yin numbers. Both are what are called eras of calamity.

If we examine this in history: under Yi and Zhuo [of the Xia], the cycle reached the seventh Yang Nine; under King Nan of Zhou, it reached the eighth Yang Nine; during the Yanxi (158–167) and Guanghe (178–184) reigns of the Han, it reached the ninth Yang Nine; and during the Daye reign (605–618) of the Sui, it reached the tenth Yang Nine. Between Kings Li and You of Zhou, it reached the twelfth Hundred Six; under King Jing of Zhou, it reached the thirteenth Hundred Six; at the juncture of the Six States and the Qin, it reached the fourteenth Hundred Six; when the Jin fractured into the Sixteen Kingdoms, the count of Hundred Six reached its limit and reverted to one; and during the Five Dynasties, it reached the third Hundred Six. In those times of division, rupture, and dispersion, the correspondence can indeed be called manifestly clear!

Yet under Shun and Yu, the cycle reached the seventh Hundred Six; under Xiaojia and Yongji [of the Shang], it reached the fifth Yang Nine and the ninth Hundred Six; under Geng, Yi, and Wuding [of the Shang], it reached the sixth Yang Nine; under Bujiang [of the Xia], it reached the eighth Hundred Six; under Pangeng and Xiaoxin [of the Shang], it reached the …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
六之數十周成康而得百六之數十一漢
明章而得百六之數十五唐文皇而得百
六之數二此於時不大小稱治哉而又胡
以盭戾若此也夫氣運不足言也至於近
而可推者日月薄蝕及五星躔度正犯之
類是也象見而天下之禍福因之所謂天
感人也卒來而不可究者彗孛凌變寒暑
霜雹震𩆝水旱之類是也幾動而天之災
祥應之所謂人感天也日月之交月行黃
===
道而日爲掩則日食是曰陰勝陽其變重
月行在望與日衝月入於日暗虛之內則
月食是曰陽勝陰其變輕聖人扶陽而尊
君曰日君道也於其食謹書而備戒之然
竟春秋二百四十二年所著見不過三十
六而已前漢二百一十三年而食者五十
三後漢百九十六年而食者七十二豈春
秋之際爲能治於漢耶說者謂史佚而不
盡載近矣而是所謂日食者其盡能爲災
punctuated: 六之數十，周成、康而得百六之數十一，漢明、章而得百六之數十五，唐文皇而得百六之數二。此於時不大小稱治哉？而又胡以盭戾若此也？夫氣運不足言也。至於近而可推者，日月薄蝕及五星躔度正犯之類是也，象見而天下之禍福因之，所謂天感人也；卒來而不可究者，彗孛凌變、寒暑、霜雹、震𩆝、水旱之類是也，幾動而天之災祥應之，所謂人感天也。日月之交，月行黃道而日爲掩，則日食，是曰陰勝陽，其變重；月行在望，與日衝，月入於日暗虛之內，則月食，是曰陽勝陰，其變輕。聖人扶陽而尊君，曰：「日，君道也。」於其食，謹書而備戒之。然竟《春秋》二百四十二年，所著見不過三十六而已；前漢二百一十三年而食者五十三，後漢百九十六年而食者七十二。豈春秋之際爲能治於漢耶？說者謂史佚而不盡載，近矣；而是所謂日食者，其盡能爲災
translation_en:
… the tenth "Hundred-and-Six" cycle; Kings Cheng and Kang of Zhou (Zhou Cheng Kang 周成康) coincided with the eleventh "Hundred-and-Six" cycle; Emperors Ming and Zhang of Han (Han Ming Zhang 漢明章) coincided with the fifteenth "Hundred-and-Six" cycle; and the Cultured Emperor of Tang (Tang Wenhuang 唐文皇, i.e., Emperor Taizong) coincided with the second "Hundred-and-Six" cycle. Were these eras not in large or small measure praised as well-governed? Why then do the calendrical calculations clash so perversely with reality like this?

Indeed, cosmic cycles of fortune are not worth discussing. As for phenomena that are proximate and calculable, these include such things as solar and lunar eclipses, as well as the orbital degrees and direct encroachments of the Five Planets. When celestial signs appear and the misfortunes and blessings of the realm follow from them, this is what is called Heaven affecting Man. As for phenomena that arrive suddenly and cannot be fathomed in advance, these include such things as the anomalous changes and encroachments of扫 and bushy comets, unseasonable cold and heat, frost and hail, thunderbolts and torrential rains, and floods and droughts. When subtle triggers stir below and Heaven's calamities or auspicious omens respond to them, this is what is called Man affecting Heaven.

At the conjunction of the sun and moon, if the moon travels along the ecliptic and obscures the sun, then the sun is eclipsed; this is called yin overcoming yang, and the anomaly is grave. When the moon is at full phase in opposition to the sun, and the moon enters into the dark void opposite the sun (Earth's shadow), then the moon is eclipsed; this is called yang overcoming yin, and the anomaly is light. The Sage upheld yang and revered the ruler, saying, "The sun is the Way of the ruler." Whenever it was eclipsed, he carefully recorded it to provide full warning. Yet throughout the two hundred and forty-two years of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋), those clearly recorded were no more than thirty-six. In the Former Han, over two hundred and thirteen years, there were fifty-three solar eclipses; in the Later Han, over one hundred and ninety-six years, there were seventy-two. Could it be that the Spring and Autumn period was better governed than the Han? Commentators say that the scribes lost records and did not record them all, which comes close to the truth; yet as for these so-called solar eclipses, could they all have brought disaster…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於漢否也自日月而下者毋過五星爲其
能盡天之五行也歲星最吉其所居國不
可伐能伐人填星次之凡國居久則福厚
熒惑最凶所居國受殃太白次之辰星又
次之要之犯道變色則皆足以爲災久伏
不出則必化而爲彗彗之所指靡不立禍
然亦安能一一而令人應耶夫吉星不能
挽之而使留凶曜不能推之而使去則所
以感人者亦遼邈也吾姑舉數者以證之
===
夫呂后以日食而逝然此非易姓比也歿
未幾而眞主自代來以二十二年之治而
永漢祚於四百日食抑何祥也秦王以太
白經天而有天下然此非人主比也立未
幾而仁義行有效以二十三年之治而昌
唐曆於三百安在太白之爲天下兵也文
帝時一日而裂山者二十九一雨而爲日
者二十五壞民居至八千之衆法以爲君
道廢壞民失所應也夫君道不壞而民安
punctuated: 於漢否也？自日月而下者，毋過五星，爲其能盡天之五行也。歲星最吉，其所居國不可伐，能伐人；填星次之，凡國居久則福厚。熒惑最凶，所居國受殃；太白次之；辰星又次之。要之，犯道變色，則皆足以爲災；久伏不出，則必化而爲彗，彗之所指，靡不立禍。然亦安能一一而令人應耶？夫吉星不能挽之而使留，凶曜不能推之而使去，則所以感人者亦遼邈也。吾姑舉數者以證之。夫呂后以日食而逝，然此非易姓比也，歿未幾而眞主自代來，以二十二年之治而永漢祚於四百，日食抑何祥也！秦王以太白經天而有天下，然此非人主比也，立未幾而仁義行有效，以二十三年之治而昌唐曆於三百，安在太白之爲天下兵也！文帝時，一日而裂山者二十九，一雨而爲日者二十五，壞民居至八千之衆，法以爲君道廢壞、民失所應也。夫君道不壞而民安
translation_en:
…to the Han or not? Below the sun and moon, nothing surpasses the Five Planets, for they fully embody the Five Phases of Heaven. The Year Star [Jupiter] is the most auspicious: the state in whose celestial sector it resides cannot be attacked, and is able to attack others; the Quelling Star [Saturn] comes next: whenever it resides long in a state's sector, blessings are abundant. The Dazzling Deluder [Mars] is the most baleful: the state in whose sector it resides suffers calamity; the Great White [Venus] comes next; and the Chronogram Star [Mercury] comes after that. In sum, when they transgress their paths or change color, all are sufficient to cause disaster; when they remain hidden for a long time without appearing, they inevitably transform into comets, and wherever a comet points, immediate misfortune never fails to follow. Yet how could they possibly elicit a human response in every single instance? Now, since auspicious stars cannot be pulled back and made to stay, and baleful luminaries cannot be pushed away and made to leave, the way in which they affect human affairs is distant and obscure indeed. Let me provisionally cite a few examples to prove this.

Now, Empress Lü 呂后 died following a solar eclipse, yet this was nothing like a change of ruling surname. Shortly after her death, the true ruler arrived from Dai 代; through twenty-two years of governance he extended the Han 漢 imperial fortune to four hundred years—how auspicious, then, was that solar eclipse! The Prince of Qin 秦王 [Li Shimin 李世民] came to possess the empire when the Great White crossed the meridian in daylight, yet he was no ordinary ruler. Shortly after he ascended the throne, his practice of benevolence and righteousness proved effective; through twenty-three years of governance he made the Tang 唐 dynastic calendar flourish for three hundred years—where, then, was the Great White'sBringing of warfare to the empire? In the time of Emperor Wen 文帝, twenty-nine mountains cracked open in a single day, and a single rain lasted for twenty-five days, destroying as many as eight thousand民 [commoners'] homes. According to the standard prognostic rules, this is the response to the way of the ruler falling into ruin and the people losing their livelihood. Yet when it came to the way of the ruler not being ruined and the people enjoying peace…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
佚孰有踰文帝者也又其四年六月雨雪
法以為誅殺過當應也君仁而不過誅殺
孰有踰文帝者也世治則鳳凰見麒麟遊
芝草生鳳一見於漢桓之元嘉再見於靈
之光和蒼麟十六驂駕於石虎芝草數萬
供養於宣和彼四君者是遵何德哉世之
為解者曰三代而上人主之精誠與上帝
相為流通上帝亦日卑其視聽而待之是
人主與天一也故一遇變而立應一脩德
===
而立改三代而下既不克齋明其德以默
與之契而又未甞中心慄慄以承其變是
人主與天二也是以有應有不應也然所
謂九年之水於堯而七年之旱於湯者亦
未聞其能逆銷之也則夫萐脯蓂莢屈軼
鮭臙之類吾不敢盡以為和德應也則又
曰帝堯之世羲和欽昊天而其仲若叔分
殷四時矣夫以杳渺不易測之政冠萬機
而推策无可據之人踞四岳九官十二牧
punctuated: 佚，孰有踰文帝者也？又其四年六月雨雪，法以為誅殺過當應也。君仁而不過誅殺，孰有踰文帝者也？世治則鳳凰見、麒麟遊、芝草生。鳳一見於漢桓之元嘉，再見於靈之光和；蒼麟十六，驂駕於石虎；芝草數萬，供養於宣和。彼四君者，是遵何德哉？世之為解者曰：「三代而上，人主之精誠與上帝相為流通，上帝亦日卑其視聽而待之，是人主與天一也。故一遇變而立應，一脩德而立改。三代而下，既不克齋明其德以默與之契，而又未甞中心慄慄以承其變，是人主與天二也，是以有應有不應也。」然所謂九年之水於堯，而七年之旱於湯者，亦未聞其能逆銷之也。則夫萐脯、蓂莢、屈軼、鮭臙之類，吾不敢盡以為和德應也。則又曰：「帝堯之世，羲和欽昊天，而其仲若叔分殷四時矣。夫以杳渺不易測之政冠萬機，而推策无可據之人踞四岳、九官、十二牧
translation_en:
… and at ease—who has ever surpassed Emperor Wen (Wendi 文帝) in this? Moreover, in the sixth month of the fourth year of his reign, it snowed. According to the rules of divination, this is the response to excessive executions and killings. Yet when it comes to a ruler being benevolent and not excessive in executions and killings, who has ever surpassed Emperor Wen? It is said that when the world is well-governed, phoenixes appear, unicorns (qilin 麒麟) roam, and numinous mushrooms (zhicao 芝草) grow. Yet the phoenix appeared once during the Yuanjia 元嘉 era of Emperor Huan of Han (Han Huan 漢桓), and appeared again during the Guanghe 光和 era of Emperor Ling (Ling 靈); sixteen azure unicorns were harnessed to the carriage of Shi Hu 石虎; and tens of thousands of numinous mushrooms were cultivated as offerings during the Xuanhe 宣和 era. Those four rulers—what virtue did they follow?

Those in the world who offer an explanation say: "In the Three Dynasties and earlier, the utmost sincerity of the ruler was in mutual communion with the Lord on High (Shangdi 上帝), and the Lord on High likewise daily lowered His sight and hearing to attend to him; thus the ruler and Heaven were one. Therefore, as soon as an anomaly was encountered, there was an immediate response, and as soon as virtue was cultivated, there was an immediate reversal. From the Three Dynasties onward, rulers have neither been able to purify and brighten their virtue so as to silently accord with Heaven, nor have they ever received its anomalies with trembling in their hearts; thus the ruler and Heaven are two. For this reason, sometimes there is a response and sometimes there is no response." Yet as for the so-called nine years of floods under Yao 堯 and seven years of drought under Tang 湯, we have never heard that they were able to dispel them in advance either. Then as for such things as the *shafu* 萐脯 fan-plant, the *mingjia* 蓂莢 calendar-plant, the *quyi* 屈軼 pointing-grass, and the *guiyan* 鮭臙 [?], I dare not take them all to be responses to harmonious virtue.

Others again say: "In the age of Sovereign Yao (Di Yao 帝堯), Xi 羲 and He 和 reverently followed vast Heaven, and their younger brothers the Zhong 仲 and Shu 叔 separately regulated the four seasons. Now, placing governance over what is obscure, distant, and not easily fathomed at the very head of the myriad affairs of state, and setting men whose calculations have no tangible basis above the Four Peaks (Siyue 四岳), the Nine Offices (Jiuguan 九官), and the Twelve Pastors (Shi'er mu 十二牧)…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之上其事若迂而甚專篤是以職脩而動
輒驗漢興太史公之職等於卜筮供奉而
今且以一書筭白丁充之矣夫安能望其
明天道而察民故也是或一道也則又曰
分野非故也夫以益州而遠屬魏以冀州
而屬蕞爾之衛燕在北而東配析木魯在
東而西配降婁秦西北而鶉首次東南吳
越東南而星紀次東北蓋自古猶疑之况
於今荊揚二州地半天下而戶口人物實
===
當天下十之八夫躔度安得而不下移也
且當春秋戰國時國各以地應今廢郡國
而盡欲以朝事當之又安能一一驗也是
又一道也凡此皆執事之所疑也愚則以
爲天地大矣人於其間取吾形氣之似者
而欲配之已取吾機之相通者而測之已
又取吾法之可推者而模範之以爲天地
在是矣其合者固恒而不合者亦恒也當
嘉靖時彗若蚩尤之旗無所不犯山陝之
punctuated: 之上，其事若迂而甚專篤，是以職脩而動輒驗。漢興，太史公之職等於卜筮供奉，而今且以一書筭白丁充之矣，夫安能望其明天道而察民故也？是或一道也。則又曰：分野非故也。夫以益州而遠屬魏，以冀州而屬蕞爾之衛；燕在北而東配析木，魯在東而西配降婁，秦西北而鶉首次東南，吳、越東南而星紀次東北，蓋自古猶疑之。况於今荊、揚二州，地半天下，而戶口人物實當天下十之八，夫躔度安得而不下移也？且當春秋、戰國時，國各以地應；今廢郡國，而盡欲以朝事當之，又安能一一驗也？是又一道也。凡此皆執事之所疑也。愚則以爲天地大矣，人於其間，取吾形氣之似者而欲配之，已取吾機之相通者而測之，已又取吾法之可推者而模範之，以爲天地在是矣。其合者固恒，而不合者亦恒也。當嘉靖時，彗若蚩尤之旗，無所不犯；山、陝之
translation_en:
… above [the Four Peaks, the Nine Ministers, and the Twelve Pastors]. Though their business seemed remote from practical affairs, it was pursued with great specialization and devotion; therefore their duties were well-maintained and their observations regularly proved accurate. With the rise of the Han, the office of the Grand Historian (Taishigong) was treated on a par with diviners and court attendants, and today it is even filled by mere clerks and unlettered commoners skilled only in writing and arithmetic! How, then, could one hope for them to illuminate the Way of Heaven and investigate the affairs of the people? This is perhaps one explanation.

Others say: The system of astrological field-allocations (fenye) is no longer what it was of old.
