title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
四十二年而千萬世揆是也故經不敢續
也亦無所事續也至於史則不然一代缺
而一代之跡泯如也一郡國缺而一郡國
之跡泯如也賢者不幸而不見德不肖者
幸而不見懲故夫三代非無史也周衰天
子之史不在周而寄於齊晉之盟主盟主
衰而又分寄於列國國自為史人自為筆
至秦務師吏斥百家而史亦隨燼矣五帝
之事若有若無三王之事若存若亡則非
===
史之罪也祖龍為之也執事試進操觚之
士而質之史其論三代有不尊稱尚書者
乎然自舜禹湯武及桀紂而外有能舉少
康武丁太康孔甲之詳以復者否周之季
有不尊稱春秋者乎然自桓文而上有能
舉宣平共和之詳者否三漢而下有不稱
官晉齊諧六代期期唐書蕪宋史而夷穢
遼金元三氏者乎然一展卷而千六百年
之人若新而其跡若臚列也則是史之存
punctuated: 四十二年而千萬世揆是也。故經不敢續也，亦無所事續也。至於史則不然，一代缺而一代之跡泯如也，一郡國缺而一郡國之跡泯如也。賢者不幸而不見德，不肖者幸而不見懲。故夫三代非無史也，周衰，天子之史不在周而寄於齊、晉之盟主；盟主衰，而又分寄於列國，國自為史，人自為筆。至秦務師吏，斥百家，而史亦隨燼矣。五帝之事若有若無，三王之事若存若亡，則非史之罪也，祖龍為之也。執事試進操觚之士而質之史，其論三代，有不尊稱《尚書》者乎？然自舜、禹、湯、武及桀、紂而外，有能舉少康、武丁、太康、孔甲之詳以復者否？周之季，有不尊稱《春秋》者乎？然自桓、文而上，有能舉宣、平、共和之詳者否？三漢而下，有不稱官晉、齊諧六代、期期《唐書》、蕪《宋史》，而夷穢遼、金、元三氏者乎？然一展卷而千六百年之人若新，而其跡若臚列也，則是史之存
translation_en: … [two hundred and] forty-two years, yet ten thousand generations take their standard from this. Therefore, one does not dare to write a continuation to a Classic, nor is there any need to continue it. As for history, however, it is not so. If a single dynasty is missing, the traces of that dynasty vanish completely; if a single commandery or principality is missing, the traces of that commandery or principality vanish completely. The worthy unfortunately do not have their virtue made manifest, while the unworthy fortunately escape having their wickedness chastised. Thus, the Three Dynasties were not without histories. When the Zhou declined, the history of the Son of Heaven no longer resided in Zhou, but was lodged with the covenant-leaders of Qi and Jin. When the covenant-leaders declined, it was further dispersed and lodged among the various states, each state compiling its own history and each man writing with his own brush. By the time of Qin, they devoted themselves to taking legal officials as teachers and rejected the Hundred Schools, and the histories were accordingly reduced to ashes along with them. That the affairs of the Five Emperors seem at once to have existed and not existed, and the affairs of the Three Kings seem at once preserved and lost, is not the fault of history; it was the doing of the Ancestral Dragon [Qin Shi Huang]. Suppose Your Excellency were to summon scholars who wield the writing tablet and question them about history: when discussing the Three Dynasties, is there anyone who does not revere and praise the Book of Documents (Shangshu)? Yet apart from Shun, Yu, Tang, and Wu, as well as Jie and Zhou, is there anyone who can recount in reply the detailed affairs of Shao Kang, Wu Ding, Tai Kang, or Kong Jia? For the later period of the Zhou, is there anyone who does not revere and praise the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)? Yet prior to Dukes Huan and Wen, is there anyone who can recount the detailed affairs of Kings Xuan and Ping, or the Gonghe regency? From the three Han dynasties downward, is there anyone who does not speak of the History of the Jin as bureaucratic [?], the Six Dynasties as mere tales of Qi谐 [fanciful anecdotes], the History of the Tang as stuttering, and the History of the Song as overgrown with weeds, while treating the three histories of the Liao, Jin, and Yuan as barbaric and defiled? Yet as soon as one unrolls the scrolls, the people of sixteen hundred years appear as if new, and their deeds are as if set out in order before us. This, then, is the difference between whether histories survive…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
與不存也愚非謂晉氏六季唐宋而下之
能史也謂治史之有地也凡天下之言史
者有二家其編年者居其一而左氏爲最
紀傳者居其一而司馬氏爲最左氏之始
末在事而司馬氏之始末在人重在事則
束於事而不能旁及人苦於略而不徧重
在人則束於人其事不能無重出而互見
苦於繁而不能竟故法左以備一時之覽
而法司馬以成一代之業可相有而不可
===
偏廢者也自漢孝獻帝命荀悅約略班史
之文而用左法凡三十篇曰漢紀而袁宏
復爲東漢紀亦三十篇其文辭華實略相
當後世頗稱述焉而其它如張璠孫盛干
寶徐賈裴子野吳均何之元王劭柳芳崔
龜從之流曰春秋曰紀曰略曰志曰曆大
約又因二紀而爲書執事謂寥寥者非也
特其書多散佚不傳耳繼司馬而盛者則
無如班氏而范曄之後漢陳壽之三國亦
punctuated: 與不存也。愚非謂晉氏、六季、唐、宋而下之能史也，謂治史之有地也。凡天下之言史者有二家：其編年者居其一，而左氏爲最；紀傳者居其一，而司馬氏爲最。左氏之始末在事，而司馬氏之始末在人。重在事則束於事而不能旁及，人苦於略而不徧；重在人則束於人，其事不能無重出而互見，苦於繁而不能竟。故法左以備一時之覽，而法司馬以成一代之業，可相有而不可偏廢者也。自漢孝獻帝命荀悅約略班史之文而用左法，凡三十篇，曰《漢紀》；而袁宏復爲《東漢紀》，亦三十篇。其文辭華實略相當，後世頗稱述焉。而其它如張璠、孫盛、干寶、徐賈、裴子野、吳均、何之元、王劭、柳芳、崔龜從之流，曰《春秋》、曰《紀》、曰《略》、曰《志》、曰《曆》，大約又因二《紀》而爲書。執事謂寥寥者，非也，特其書多散佚不傳耳。繼司馬而盛者，則無如班氏；而范曄之《後漢》、陳壽之《三國》，亦
translation_en: … or do not survive. I am not saying that the Jin dynasty, the Six Dynasties, the Tang, the Song, and later eras were skilled in history; I am saying that there is ground upon which to study their history. In general, those in the world who speak of history fall into two schools: the annalistic is one, of which Master Zuo [Zuo Qiuming 左丘明] is the finest; the纪传 (biographical-thematic) is the other, of which Master Sima [Sima Qian 司馬遷] is the finest. Master Zuo traces beginnings and ends through events, whereas Master Sima traces beginnings and ends through individuals. When the emphasis is on events, one is bound by the events and cannot branch out to side matters, so readers suffer from its brevity and lack of comprehensiveness; when the emphasis is on individuals, one is bound by the individuals, so the events cannot avoid repetition and cross-referencing, and readers suffer from its prolixity and inability to finish it. Therefore, emulating Zuo so as to provide a survey for a given moment, and emulating Sima so as to complete the enterprise of an entire dynasty, are approaches that can complement one another and must not be one-sidedly discarded. Ever since Emperor Xiaoxian of the Han commanded Xun Yue 荀悅 to abridge the text of Ban's [Ban Gu 班固] history using Zuo's method, amounting to thirty chapters in all and entitled Annals of the Han (Han ji 漢紀), Yuan Hong 袁宏 in turn composed the Annals of the Eastern Han (Dong Han ji 東漢紀), also in thirty chapters. In literary ornamentation and substance the two are roughly matched, and later generations have praised and cited them considerably. As for others of the sort of Zhang Fan 張璠, Sun Sheng 孫盛, Gan Bao 干寶, Xu Guang 徐廣 [written 徐賈 in text?], Pei Ziye 裴子野, Wu Jun 吳均, He Zhiyuan 何之元, Wang Shao 王劭, Liu Fang 柳芳, and Cui Guicong 崔龜從, whose works were called Spring and Autumn (Chunqiu 春秋), Annals (Ji 紀), Outlines (Lue 略), Treatises (Zhi 志), or Calendars (Li 曆), on the whole they too modeled their books on those two Annals. When Your Excellency says that such works were few and far between, that is not so; it is merely that most of their books have been scattered and lost and are no longer transmitted. As for those who succeeded Sima and flourished, none equaled the Ban family; and Fan Ye's 范曄 Later Han (Hou Han shu 後漢書) and Chen Shou's 陳壽 Three Kingdoms (Sanguo zhi 三國志) are also…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其亞焉大約如司馬而小變其凡例或不
能備表志如壽耳自是而後以人主之命
撰者則房玄齡等之於晉沈約之於宋蕭
子顯之於南齊姚思廉之於梁陳魏收之
於魏令狐德棻等之於周魏徵等之於隋
劉昫等及歐陽脩宋祁之前後於唐盧多
遜等之於五代歐陽玄等之於宋遼金是
也其自撰者則伏無忌劉珎蔡邕之爲東
觀記謝承之爲書華嶠之爲典張勃之爲
===
錄何法盛之爲說崔鴻之爲十六國春秋
何承天徐衍之爲宋鄧彥海之爲代李百
藥之爲北齊是也歐陽脩紀新唐而劉昫
寢志五代而盧多遜廢則或以其文哉述
左氏者宋涑水司馬光氏故好爲史而當
熙豐之際不勝其愛君之念纂資治通鑑
以上之起周威烈而迄後周世宗於治體
無所係則寧削正史而不書有所裨則旁
採異書而不廢雖其繁簡不能超時而自
punctuated: 其亞焉。大約如司馬而小變其凡例，或不能備表、志，如壽耳。自是而後，以人主之命撰者，則房玄齡等之於《晉》，沈約之於《宋》，蕭子顯之於《南齊》，姚思廉之於《梁》、《陳》，魏收之於《魏》，令狐德棻等之於《周》，魏徵等之於《隋》，劉昫等及歐陽脩、宋祁之前後於《唐》，盧多遜等之於《五代》，歐陽玄等之於《宋》、《遼》、《金》是也。其自撰者，則伏無忌、劉珎、蔡邕之爲《東觀記》，謝承之爲《書》，華嶠之爲《典》，張勃之爲《錄》，何法盛之爲《說》，崔鴻之爲《十六國春秋》，何承天、徐衍之爲《宋》，鄧彥海之爲《代》，李百藥之爲《北齊》是也。歐陽脩紀《新唐》而劉昫寢，志《五代》而盧多遜廢，則或以其文哉！述左氏者，宋涑水司馬光氏故好爲史，而當熙、豐之際，不勝其愛君之念，纂《資治通鑑》以上之。起周威烈而迄後周世宗，於治體無所係，則寧削正史而不書；有所裨，則旁採異書而不廢。雖其繁簡不能超時而自…
translation_en: … rank next after them. In general, they followed Sima Qian while slightly altering his editorial principles, or else could not include full tables and treatises, as was the case with Chen Shou. Thereafter, those compiled by order of the sovereign were: Fang Xuan齡 房玄齡 and others on the Jin; Shen Yue 沈約 on the Song; Xiao Zixian 蕭子顯 on the Southern Qi; Yao Silian 姚思廉 on the Liang and Chen; Wei Shou 魏收 on the Wei; Linghu Defen 令狐德棻 and others on the Zhou; Wei Zheng 魏徵 and others on the Sui; Liu Xu 劉昫 and others, as well as Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 and Song Qi 宋祁 successively, on the Tang; Lu Duoxun 盧多遜 and others on the Five Dynasties; and Ouyang Xuan 歐陽玄 and others on the Song, Liao, and Jin. Those compiled privately were: Fu Wuji 伏無忌, Liu Zhen 劉珎, and Cai Yong 蔡邕 with the Dongguan Records (Dongguan ji 東觀記); Xie Cheng 謝承 with his Book (Shu 書); Hua Qiao 華嶠 with his Canon (Dian 典); Zhang Bo 張勃 with his Record (Lu 錄); He Fasheng 何法盛 with his Explanations (Shuo 說); Cui Hong 崔鴻 with his Spring and Autumn Annals of the Sixteen Kingdoms (Shiliuguo chunqiu 十六國春秋); He Chengtian 何承天 and Xu Yan 徐衍 on the Song; Deng Yanhai 鄧彥海 on the Dai; and Li Baiyao 李百藥 on the Northern Qi. When Ouyang Xiu recorded the New Tang History (Xin Tang shu 新唐書), Liu Xu's work was set aside; when he wrote the history of the Five Dynasties, Lu Duoxun's work fell into disuse—was this not perhaps because of his literary style! As for those who continued the tradition of Zuo Qiuming, Sima Guang 司馬光 of Sushui 涑水 in the Song dynasty was by nature fond of writing history, and during the Xining and Yuanfeng eras (1068–1085), overcome by his devotion to his sovereign, he compiled the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government (Zizhi tongjian 資治通鑑) and presented it to the throne. Beginning with King Weilie of Zhou and ending with Shizong of the Later Zhou, wherever matters had no bearing on the principles of governance, he would rather excise them from the standard histories and leave them unrecorded; wherever they offered some benefit, he would gather them from side sources and unofficial books without discarding them. Although in its fullness and brevity it could not transcend its age to independently…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
爲法然世主稱良焉夫
明興其治統政化人才卓然越百世而於史抑
何湮略弗振也夫
金匱石室之閎度非草茅所與聞然往往傳
之薦紳云革除靖難之際其筆不能無曲
與諱也輸款而美其知義抗節而誣其乞
哀乃至
英憲孝之際秉如椽者陳廬陵劉博野焦泌陽
之輩往往鴟張其臆一人而代各賢否一
===
事而人各是非甚或責闕供於仁孝之里
詆掠金於戡定之臣將何所取衷哉野史
亡慮數十百家其在
朝者脩郄而滅其公是逞已而欺其獨非在
野者剽一時之耳而遂爲目信他人之舌
而用爲筆則又不可信也家乘稍具生卒
世系遷轉履歷而已要之無非諛墓者改
事之非而稱是略人之美而歸已則又不
可信也愚故不自量輒因執事之間而有
punctuated: 爲法，然世主稱良焉。夫明興，其治統、政化、人才卓然越百世，而於史抑何湮略弗振也！夫金匱石室之閎度，非草茅所與聞，然往往傳之薦紳云：革除、靖難之際，其筆不能無曲與諱也。輸款而美其知義，抗節而誣其乞哀。乃至英、憲、孝之際，秉如椽者陳廬陵、劉博野、焦泌陽之輩，往往鴟張其臆：一人而代各賢否，一事而人各是非；甚或責闕供於仁孝之里，詆掠金於戡定之臣，將何所取衷哉？野史亡慮數十百家：其在朝者，脩郄而滅其公是，逞已而欺其獨非；在野者，剽一時之耳而遂爲目，信他人之舌而用爲筆，則又不可信也。家乘稍具生卒、世系、遷轉、履歷而已，要之無非諛墓者：改事之非而稱是，略人之美而歸已，則又不可信也。愚故不自量，輒因執事之間而有
translation_en: … establish his own standard, yet the ruler of the age praised it as excellent. Now, with the rise of the Ming, its legitimate succession of governance, transformative administration, and men of talent stand preeminent beyond a hundred generations—yet why is its historiography so obscured, sketchy, and unrevived? The grand repositories of the Golden Casket and Stone Chamber are not matters that a rustic commoner is privy to hear of, yet it is often passed down among the gentry that at the juncture of the Jianwen reign's erasure (Gechu) and the Campaign to Clear Away Disorders (Jingnan), the historians' brushes could not be free of distortion and taboo. Those who tendered allegiance were praised for knowing righteousness, while those who upheld their integrity in resistance were slandered as having begged for pity. Coming down to the reigns of Emperors Yingzong, Xianzong, and Xiaozong, those who wielded the rafter-like grand historiographical brush—men of the ilk of Chen Xun 陳循 of Luling, Liu Ji 劉吉 of Boye, and Jiao Fang 焦芳 of Biyang—frequently gave arrogant rein to their personal prejudices: the very same person was judged worthy in one reign and unworthy in another, and the very same affair was deemed right by one man and wrong by another. It even went so far as blaming the native village of the benevolent and filial [Zou Zhi 鄒智 / Zhang元禎?] for failing to provide supplies [?], or slandering the minister who quelled the rebellion [Yu Qian 于謙 / Wang Shouren 王守仁] for plundering gold—where, then, can one find an impartial standard of truth? As for unofficial histories, there are no fewer than several dozen or a hundred schools. Those written by men at court nurse personal grudges and extinguish what is publicly acknowledged as right, indulging themselves and deceiving others with their solitary denunciations; those written by men in retirement plagiarize what is heard for a moment and treat it as what they have witnessed with their own eyes, trusting the tongues of others and using them as their own brush—thus they too cannot be trusted. Family chronicles merely record dates of birth and death, genealogies, and the sequence of official promotions and careers; in sum, they are nothing more than grave-flattering writings that alter the wrongs of an affair to call them right, and gloss over the merits of others to claim them for one's own—thus they too cannot be trusted. Stupid though I am, I therefore do not measure my own limitations, and readily avail myself of the space of Your Excellency's inquiry [reading 間 as 問: question] to…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
請夫班氏脩其父業而仇者以私史間之
乃章帝益出秘書給筆札於蘭臺之署而
俾續成史以獻帝之世天下日尋干戈而
猶能命荀悅脩漢紀況於今
聖天子秉
睿哲履
昌運日以
文敎揆海內而公卿大夫熟於墳典丘索之
業者哉有如一旦悉出
===
金匱石室之閟而錄其副以授夫載筆之臣
而益以郡國志記及向所云野史家乘之
可采者使公平該博之士持衡其是非而
爾雅遒古之才藻潤其辭事會典之所輯
星官之所職六尚書之故牘可以書可以
志可以表而我
明一代之業當無遜於西京矣其事體稍重大
而有益於治道者或起自趙宋而至先朝
用左氏之體而達涑水氏之忠微益以文
punctuated: 請。夫班氏脩其父業，而仇者以私史間之，乃章帝益出秘書，給筆札於蘭臺之署，而俾續成史。以獻帝之世，天下日尋干戈，而猶能命荀悅脩《漢紀》，況於今聖天子秉睿哲，履昌運，日以文敎揆海內，而公卿大夫熟於《墳》《典》《丘》《索》之業者哉？有如一旦悉出金匱石室之閟，而錄其副以授夫載筆之臣，而益以郡國志記，及向所云野史、家乘之可采者，使公平該博之士持衡其是非，而爾雅遒古之才藻潤其辭事。《會典》之所輯，星官之所職，六尚書之故牘，可以書，可以志，可以表，而我明一代之業，當無遜於西京矣。其事體稍重大而有益於治道者，或起自趙宋而至先朝，用左氏之體而達涑水氏之忠，微益以文…
translation_en: … request. Now, when Ban Gu (班氏) carried on his father's work, his enemies slandered him for writing a private history; yet Emperor Zhang (章帝) brought out even more secret palace books, supplied him with brush and writing tablets in the office of the Orchid Terrace (蘭臺), and enabled him to continue and complete the history. Even in the reign of Emperor Xian (獻帝), when the empire was daily engaged in warfare, he was still able to command Xun Yue (荀悅) to compile the Han Annals (Hanji 漢紀). How much more so today, when our Sacred Son of Heaven, endowed with profound wisdom and treading a prosperous era, daily measures all within the seas through literary and moral teaching, and when our dukes, ministers, and grand masters are thoroughly versed in the learning of the Three Mounds, Five Canons, Eight索, and Nine邱 (Fundian Qiusuo 墳典丘索)? Suppose that one day all the secret archives of the golden coffers and stone chambers were brought out, and copies of them were transcribed and handed over to the historiography officials; and that these were supplemented with the gazetteers and records of commanderies and principalities, as well as whatever is worth adopting from the unofficial histories and family genealogies mentioned earlier; and that impartial and erudite scholars were made to weigh their truth and falsehood, while talents of refined, vigorous, and ancient style embellished their diction and narratives. What is compiled in the Collected Statutes (Huidian 會典), what is managed by the astrological officials, and the old archives of the Six Ministries—these could be made into treatises, monographs, and chronological tables, and the historiographical achievement of our own Ming dynasty would surely not be inferior to that of the Western Han! As for matters of somewhat greater weight that are beneficial to the way of governance—perhaps starting from the Zhao Song dynasty down to the previous reigns of our own dynasty—if we employ the annalistic form of Zuo Qiuming (左氏) to convey the loyal spirit of Sima Guang of Sushui (涑水氏), slightly augmenting the literary style…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而嚴刈其雜合所謂通鑑者而上之虎觀
諸儒得進讀於燕間而
黼座之表廻
清矚於乙夜其為益非淺尠也或謂眾力易就
也然見錯而辭不馴獨為不易也然志專
而體不雜故夫左氏也司馬班氏也壽與
曄也非晋唐與宋之可儗也歐陽氏史五
代而傳史新唐而不傳無它眾力與獨之
異也夫所謂獨者執事毋亦難其人乎愚
===
以天下大矣不敢逆縮焉而謂無人愚故
尚欲法司馬氏而竊意其於帝紀孔氏之
文訓故尚書家語而節略之以為不稱又
生不及遇左氏傳故其敘春秋諸世家舛
忽而不詳好自發其意故於刺客游俠貨
殖佞幸之倫旁採而不忍斥有能刪節其
凡例自羲黃而下迨於今為一家言以藏
之名山大川愚且願為之執鞭而終其身
也執事毋以為迂否
punctuated: 而嚴刈其雜，合所謂《通鑑》者而上之虎觀，諸儒得進讀於燕間，而黼座之表，廻清矚於乙夜，其為益非淺尠也。或謂眾力易就也，然見錯而辭不馴；獨為不易也，然志專而體不雜。故夫左氏也、司馬班氏也、壽與曄也，非晋、唐與宋之可儗也。歐陽氏史《五代》而傳，史《新唐》而不傳，無它，眾力與獨之異也。夫所謂獨者，執事毋亦難其人乎？愚以天下大矣，不敢逆縮焉而謂無人。愚故尚欲法司馬氏，而竊意其於帝紀、孔氏之文，訓故《尚書》、《家語》而節略之，以為不稱；又生不及遇《左氏傳》，故其敘春秋諸世家，舛忽而不詳；好自發其意，故於刺客、游俠、貨殖、佞幸之倫，旁採而不忍斥。有能刪節其凡例，自羲、黃而下迨於今，為一家言，以藏之名山大川，愚且願為之執鞭而終其身也。執事毋以為迂否？
translation_en:
…while strictly pruning away its miscellaneous elements, combining it with the so-called Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian) and presenting it to the White Tiger Hall (Huguan). Then the Confucian scholars could advance to read it aloud during moments of imperial leisure, and from beyond the imperial throne His Majesty could turn his clear gaze upon it during the second watch of the night—the benefit of this would be far from slight.

Some say that a work of collective effort is easy to complete, yet its views are disparate and its diction unrefined; a work done by a single hand is not easy, yet its purpose is focused and its form unmixed. Thus Master Zuo (Zuo Qiuming 左丘明), the Sima (Sima Qian 司馬遷) and Ban (Ban Gu 班固) clans, as well as Chen Shou 陳壽 and Fan Ye 范曄, cannot be matched by the histories compiled in the Jin, Tang, and Song dynasties. Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修 wrote the history of the Five Dynasties (Wudai shi) and it was handed down with acclaim, whereas when he worked on the New History of the Tang (Xin Tangshu) it was not so esteemed [?]. There is no other reason for this than the difference between collective effort and solitary authorship.

As for what is called solitary authorship, does Your Excellency not also find it difficult to find the right person for it? In my humble view, the realm is vast, and I dare not shrink back in advance and declare that there is no such person. Indeed, I would still wish to take Master Sima as a model, though I privately think that in the "Basic Annals of the Emperors" and the writings on Confucius, his glossing and abridging of the Book of Documents (Shangshu) and the Family Sayings of Confucius (Kongzi jiayu) fell short of the mark; moreover, in his lifetime he did not have the chance to encounter Zuo's Commentary (Zuozhuan) in full, so his accounts of the various Hereditary Houses of the Spring and Autumn period are muddled, negligent, and lacking in detail; and because hewas fond of expressing his own personal sentiments, when it came to the likes of assassins, wandering knights-errant, moneymakers, and sycophantic favorites, he gathered stories from all sides and could not bear to exclude them. If there were someone capable of paring down and refining his general principles, compiling the history from Fuxi 伏羲 and the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) down to the present day as the words of a single school, to be stored away in famous mountains and great rivers, I in my foolishness would gladly act as his whip-bearer for the rest of my life! Would Your Excellency not consider this impractical?

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第四問
周弘禴
同考試官敎諭左批〔人才最關世道此作推論源委〕
〔而惓惓於上下虛實之際有深長思矣〕
考試官敎授黃批〔上下今古照應名流語極剴切〕
〔可以觀于所養矣錄之以式〕
考試官敎授郭批〔諤諤之意渾渾之辭〕
天下未嘗乏才也人主欲就天下之治故
不得不求之以實天下之所謂才者因而
===
自就其欲故不得不應之以虛應之以虛
虛之久而人主卒無以得其實也不獲已
而相襲以成虛求之以實而竟無得也人
主之求亦虛而天下之材卒無以自見其
實上與下交爲虛而名與實相爲悖如之
何其得用人之益也夫豈唯無益且有大
損今夫山鷄之於長離也鍮石之於金也
碔砆之於玉也杞柳之於楩梓也君子見
而惡之爲其殽名實也猶之乎可也若夫
punctuated:
第四問

周弘禴

同考試官敎諭左批：〔人才最關世道，此作推論源委，而惓惓於上下虛實之際，有深長思矣。〕

考試官敎授黃批：〔上下今古，照應名流，語極剴切，可以觀于所養矣，錄之以式。〕

考試官敎授郭批：〔諤諤之意，渾渾之辭。〕

天下未嘗乏才也。人主欲就天下之治，故不得不求之以實；天下之所謂才者，因而自就其欲，故不得不應之以虛。應之以虛，虛之久，而人主卒無以得其實也，不獲已而相襲以成虛。求之以實而竟無得也，人主之求亦虛，而天下之材卒無以自見其實。上與下交爲虛，而名與實相爲悖，如之何其得用人之益也？夫豈唯無益，且有大損。今夫山鷄之於長離也，鍮石之於金也，碔砆之於玉也，杞柳之於楩梓也，君子見而惡之，爲其殽名實也，猶之乎可也。若夫
translation_en:
Fourth Policy Question

Zhou Hongyue 周弘禴

Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Zuo: [Men of talent are of the utmost importance to the way of the world. This essay traces the origins and developments of the matter, and shows an earnest concern for the distinction between emptiness and substance on the part of both superiors and inferiors; it reflects deep and far-reaching thought.]

Comment by Examiner, Instructor Huang: [Surveying past and present and keeping eminent figures in view, its words are exceedingly incisive and to the point. One can observe from this what he has cultivated in himself; it is recorded here as a model.]

Comment by Examiner, Instructor Guo: [Forthright in intent, vigorous and profound in expression.]

The empire has never lacked talent. Because the ruler wishes to achieve good governance in the empire, he cannot but seek talent with substance; yet because those in the empire who are called men of talent take advantage of this to pursue their own desires, they cannot but respond to him with emptiness. When they respond to him with emptiness, and this emptiness persists for a long time, the ruler in the end has no way to obtain true substance from them, and out of helplessness follows suit in perpetuating emptiness. Having sought talent with substance and ultimately obtained nothing, the ruler's own seeking becomes empty as well, and the men of talent in the empire in the end have no way to manifest their true substance. When superior and inferior engage with one another in emptiness, and name and reality run counter to each other, how can one possibly reap the benefits of employing men? Indeed, not only is there no benefit, there is great harm. Now then, as for the pheasant compared to the phoenix (changli 長離), brass compared to gold, bastard gems (wufu 碔砆) compared to jade, and the willow compared to the楠 (pian 楩) and catalpa (zi 梓) trees—when the gentleman sees them, he detests them because they confound name and reality; yet even so, these are still tolerable. When it comes to…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
征鳥冠而似鳳脩蛇角而似龍則見者且
却避矣何也謂其似之能爲害也執事之
策諸生果取其實乎抑欲得其似而遽已
也愚嘗論世而竊思唐虞之際矣禹稷契
咎繇各以其職成天下治歸而陳謨訓而
靡匪心法也亦靡匪至文也凡執事之所
謂事功文章節義理學者固無繇見也三
代而後治日以駁而名始出矣漢高帝不
愛眞王徹侯之印以羶悅天下而所謂求
===
賢詔曰從吾游者吾能尊顯之其意不過
欲盡一世之才而爲我用而世之應之者
毋論其時蕭曹韓彭之屬而已也輔相則
魏弱侯丙少卿將帥則衛長平霍冠軍趙
營平受遺則霍博陸戡難則周絳侯條侯
父子循良則黃潁川龔渤海韓馮翊材幹
則趙張二京兆尹扶風奉使則張博望蘇
屬國立功則傅介子甘陳之屬人主之求
材也若探囊而取之所求立至其效用也
punctuated: 征鳥冠而似鳳，脩蛇角而似龍，則見者且却避矣。何也？謂其似之能爲害也。執事之策諸生，果取其實乎？抑欲得其似而遽已也？愚嘗論世，而竊思唐、虞之際矣。禹、稷、契、咎繇各以其職成天下治，歸而陳謨訓，而靡匪心法也，亦靡匪至文也。凡執事之所謂事功、文章、節義、理學者，固無繇見也。三代而後，治日以駁，而名始出矣。漢高帝不愛眞王、徹侯之印以羶悅天下，而所謂求賢詔曰：「從吾游者，吾能尊顯之。」其意不過欲盡一世之才而爲我用。而世之應之者，毋論其時蕭、曹、韓、彭之屬而已也。輔相則魏弱侯、丙少卿，將帥則衛長平、霍冠軍、趙營平，受遺則霍博陸，戡難則周絳侯、條侯父子，循良則黃潁川、龔渤海、韓馮翊，材幹則趙、張二京兆、尹扶風，奉使則張博望、蘇屬國，立功則傅介子、甘、陳之屬。人主之求材也，若探囊而取之，所求立至；其效用也，
translation_en:
… when a bird of prey wears a crest so as to resemble a phoenix, or a giant serpent grows horns so as to resemble a dragon, those who see them will shrink back and flee. Why is this? Because such a resemblance is capable of causing real harm. In posing this policy question to us candidates, does Your Excellency truly seek the reality, or do you wish merely to obtain a resemblance and stop right there?

I have examined the ages of the past and privately reflected upon the era of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]. Yu, Ji, Xie, and Gao Yao each fulfilled their respective offices to bring about order throughout the realm; when they returned to court and set forth their counsels and instructions, there was nothing that was not the transmission of the mind, and nothing that was not supreme literature. All that Your Excellency refers to as practical achievements, literary composition, moral integrity, and the study of principle had no separate labels by which to be seen.

After the Three Dynasties, governance grew daily more impure, and such names first emerged. Emperor Gao of Han did not begrudge the seals of true kings and penetrant marquises to entice and delight the world, and in his so-called Edict Seeking the Worthy he declared: "Those who associate with me, I can make honored and illustrious." His intention was nothing more than to exhaust the talents of the entire generation and put them to his own use. And as for those in the world who responded to him, it was not merely men like Xiao [He], Cao [Can], Han [Xin], and Peng [Yue] of that immediate time! For grand counselors, there were Wei Xiang (Ruo Weng) [?] and Bing Ji (Shaoqing); for generals and commanders, Wei Qing (Marquis of Changping), Huo Qubing (Marquis of Guanjun), and Zhao Chongguo (Marquis of Yingping); for receiving the testamentary charge, Huo Guang (Marquis of Bolu); for quelling rebellions, Zhou Bo (Marquis of Jiang) and his son the Marquis of Tiao [Zhou Yafu]; for benevolent and upright local officials, Huang Ba of Yingchuan, Gong Sui of Bohai, and Han Yanshou of Zuopingyi; for men of administrative capability, the two Metropolitan Governors Zhao Guanghan and Zhang Chang, and Yin Wenggui of Youfufeng; for envoys on foreign missions, Zhang Qian (Marquis of Bowang) and Su Wu (Director of Dependent States); and for establishing exploits abroad, men such as Fu Jiezi, Gan Yanshou, and Chen Tang. When the ruler sought talent, it was like reaching into a bag to take it out—what he sought arrived immediately; and when they rendered service, …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
若探符而合之所效立驗故終西漢之世
人主之用在下而不在上而天下之權在
上而不在下雖以元成偷而夷狄賓服黎
庶愉樂郡國之政脩而國勢彊者其人才
爲國盡也光武感二龔諸賢之事故欲風
天下以節義友莊光而不之臣褒卓太傅
俾冠元勳而天下翕然改觀矣是故安隗
抗節于堅苦逢周矯志于冥逸陸戴致躬
於府主弘彪昭讓於姻封卽欲出而用世
===
者靡不束髮自勵羔鴈成羣舒徐而應步
武鼎鉉而年且老矣而李太尉陳太傅又
以勁節峻行而鼓舞之李元禮范孟博之
流爲之祓濯縷剔君俊顧及之說興而天
下之賢士君子日與權戚宦寺角而漢事
變矣當是時人主與左右之好惡伸於上
而天下之是非各伸於下是故終東漢之
世而賢人君子與社稷而俱盡者或以謂
節義激之也晉氏談玄老而王樂爲之倡
punctuated: 若探符而合之，所效立驗。故終西漢之世，人主之用在下而不在上，而天下之權在上而不在下。雖以元、成偷，而夷狄賓服，黎庶愉樂，郡國之政脩而國勢彊者，其人才爲國盡也。光武感二龔諸賢之事，故欲風天下以節義，友莊光而不之臣，褒卓太傅俾冠元勳，而天下翕然改觀矣。是故安、隗抗節于堅苦，逢、周矯志于冥逸，陸、戴致躬於府主，弘、彪昭讓於姻封。卽欲出而用世者，靡不束髮自勵，羔鴈成羣，舒徐而應，步武鼎鉉，而年且老矣。而李太尉、陳太傅又以勁節峻行而鼓舞之，李元禮、范孟博之流爲之祓濯縷剔，「君、俊、顧、及」之說興，而天下之賢士君子日與權戚、宦寺角，而漢事變矣。當是時，人主與左右之好惡伸於上，而天下之是非各伸於下。是故終東漢之世，而賢人君子與社稷而俱盡者，或以謂節義激之也。晉氏談玄老，而王、樂爲之倡，
translation_en: …was like drawing a tally and matching its halves: the results they rendered were immediately verified. Therefore, throughout the era of the Western Han, the practical application of the ruler's will lay with those below rather than above, while the authority over the realm remained above rather than below. Even with Emperors Yuan and Cheng being lax, the foreign tribes submitted in allegiance, the common people were content and joyful, the governance of commanderies and kingdoms was well-ordered, and the state's power was strong, because its men of talent exhausted themselves for the state. Emperor Guangwu, moved by the deeds of the Two Gongs (Gong Sheng 龔勝 and Gong She 龔舍) and other worthies, wished to inspire the realm with moral integrity and righteousness. He treated Zhuang Guang 莊光 (Yan Ziling 嚴子陵) as a friend rather than making him a subject, and he commended Grand Mentor Zhuo (Zhuo Mao 卓茂), placing him at the head of the foremost meritorious officials; thereupon the entire realm harmoniously changed its outlook. Consequently, Yuan An 袁安 and Kui Xiao 隗囂 [? or Ren Wei 任隗] upheld their integrity through steadfast hardship, Feng Meng 逢萌 and Zhou Dang 周黨 elevated their aspirations in obscure reclusion, Lu Xu 陸續 and Dai Jiu 戴就 devoted their lives to their prefectural lords, and Ding Hong 丁鴻 and Liu Biao 劉愷 [? Biao 彪] manifested yielding over marriage and enfeoffment. Even among those who wished to come forth and be of service to the world, there was none who did not bind up his hair and spur himself on; even when ritual gifts of lambs and wild geese arrived in flocks, they responded unhurriedly, and by the time they stepped into the highest ministerial offices, they were already old in years. Moreover, Defender-in-chief Li (Li Gu 李固) and Grand Mentor Chen (Chen Fan 陳蕃) further galvanized them with unyielding integrity and lofty conduct; men of the ilk of Li Yuanli 李元禮 (Li Ying 李膺) and Fan Mengbo 范孟博 (Fan Pang 范滂) cleansed and scrutinized on their behalf; the classifications of "Lords" (jun), "Heroes" (jun), "Exemplars" (gu), and "Guides" (ji) arose; and the worthy scholars and gentlemen of the realm contended daily with powerful imperial in-laws and eunuchs, whereupon the affairs of Han took a turn for the worse. At that time, the likes and dislikes of the ruler and his entourage were asserted from above, while the judgments of right and wrong of the realm were each asserted from below. Therefore, that by the end of the Eastern Han era its worthy men and gentlemen perished together with the altars of state—some say it was because moral integrity had been pushed to extremes. The Jin dynasty discoursed on Mysterious Learning and Laozi, with Wang (Wang Yan 王衍) and Yue (Yue Guang 樂廣) acting as its pioneers; …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
至於東晉浸淫極矣建安脩麗辭而曹劉
爲之冠至於六代浮靡極矣夫以五胡索
虜日侵尋於干戈而爲之君臣者嬉嬉焉
以清談麗辭而待之社稷幾何而不削且
淪廢也然是數者皆上以是求而下以是
應者也至於南渡之宋其國勢無以大過
於東晉六代而一時諸賢名理學者潔脩
其行而高其說意欲一洗千古而空之而
上接三代之緒顧日以恢復之義聞於朝
===
而莫之響應也日以格致誠正之說聞於
黼扆而莫之究用也退而脩明六經尊其
統而正之曰宇宙之在漢唐惛惛耳至宋
而始大明也藉令玄談麗辭者曰吾不益
晉六代也若安能救宋亡嗚呼宋亡非諸
賢罪也蓋下以是待上求而上顧不以是
待下應也至我
高皇帝神武定天下而一時忠藎石畫之士若
徐中山常開平李韓公劉誠意輩各出其
punctuated: 至於東晉，浸淫極矣；建安脩麗辭而曹、劉爲之冠，至於六代，浮靡極矣。夫以五胡、索虜日侵尋於干戈，而爲之君臣者嬉嬉焉以清談、麗辭而待之，社稷幾何而不削且淪廢也？然是數者，皆上以是求而下以是應者也。至於南渡之宋，其國勢無以大過於東晉、六代，而一時諸賢名理學者，潔脩其行而高其說，意欲一洗千古而空之，而上接三代之緒。顧日以恢復之義聞於朝，而莫之響應也；日以格致誠正之說聞於黼扆，而莫之究用也。退而脩明六經，尊其統而正之，曰：「宇宙之在漢、唐，惛惛耳，至宋而始大明也。」藉令玄談、麗辭者曰：「吾不益晉、六代也，若安能救宋亡？」嗚呼！宋亡非諸賢罪也，蓋下以是待上求，而上顧不以是待下應也。至我高皇帝神武定天下，而一時忠藎石畫之士，若徐中山、常開平、李韓公、劉誠意輩，各出其
translation_en:
… and by the Eastern Jin, this gradual saturation had reached its extreme. The Jian'an era cultivated ornate diction with Cao [Zhi] and Liu [Zhen] at its head, and by the Six Dynasties, such frivolity and extravagance had reached their extreme. Now, with the Five Barbarians and the Plait-wearing Caitiffs [Northern Wei] daily encroaching with shields and spears, while those who were rulers and ministers met them merrily with pure conversation and ornate diction, how long could the altars of state go without being whittled away and sinking into ruin? Yet in these several cases, it was always a matter of superiors seeking this from above and inferiors responding with it from below.

When it came to the Song after its crossing to the south, its national strength did not greatly surpass that of the Eastern Jin or the Six Dynasties. Meanwhile, the worthies of the age who were famed for the Learning of Principle (lixue) purely cultivated their conduct and elevated their doctrines, intending to wash away and empty out a thousand ages of the past and reconnect upward with the lineage of the Three Dynasties. Yet though they daily made the righteous cause of restoration heard at court, none echoed in response; though they daily made the doctrines of investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind heard before the imperial screen, none put them to thorough use. Withdrawing, they cultivated and elucidated the Six Classics, honoring the orthodox transmission and rectifying it, saying: "During the Han and Tang, the universe was merely in a state of dim confusion; only with the Song has it first become greatly illuminated." Suppose those who engaged in abstruse talk and ornate diction were to say: "We were of no benefit to the Jin and the Six Dynasties, yet how were people like you able to save the Song from perishing?" Alas! The fall of the Song was not the fault of those worthies. Rather, those below awaited the ruler's seeking with these principles, whereas the ruler above did not await their response on those terms.

When it came to our Exalted Emperor [Hongwu], who pacified the realm with divine martial prowess, the loyal, devoted men of rock-solid counsel of the time—such as Xu, Prince of Zhongshan [Xu Da 徐達], Chang, Prince of Kaiping [Chang Yuchun 常遇春], Li, Duke of Han [Li Shanchang 李善長], and Liu, Earl of Chengyi [Liu Ji 劉基]—each brought forth his…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
長以就功名之會所謂雲蒸龍變蓋先後
無偶焉而
上甫下金陵賢故元大夫福壽旌之為予祠春
秋祭已才故元學士危素授之官而為其
失節竄臨淮不復用微示天下以軌矣而
是時方拮据馬上業乃馳書幣而聘宋文
憲王忠文陶安魏觀輩俾之司
綸綍而所以獎慰
恩禮有加蓋彬彬稱多賢焉而是諸賢者君子
猶謂其因沿勝國之陋而不能昭明
一代之盛以為負然亡何而忠文與吳忠節能
殉滇孫左司能殉閩葉南昌能殉楚熊岐
寧能殉虜至於鼎革之際而麻枲之列為
方為鐵為陳為卓之流其爭先而就義者
何眾也則是
高皇帝以實求而天下以實應也夫
高皇帝未嘗不言理學也其文辭發於論心論
洪範諸書而其事見於尊崇夫子及
punctuated: 長，以就功名之會，所謂雲蒸龍變，蓋先後無偶焉。而上甫下金陵，賢故元大夫福壽，旌之，為予祠，春秋祭；已才故元學士危素，授之官，而為其失節，竄臨淮，不復用，微示天下以軌矣。而是時方拮据馬上業，乃馳書幣而聘宋文憲、王忠文、陶安、魏觀輩，俾之司綸綍，而所以獎慰恩禮有加，蓋彬彬稱多賢焉。而是諸賢者，君子猶謂其因沿勝國之陋，而不能昭明一代之盛，以為負。然亡何，而忠文與吳忠節能殉滇，孫左司能殉閩，葉南昌能殉楚，熊岐寧能殉虜；至於鼎革之際，而麻枲之列，為方、為鐵、為陳、為卓之流，其爭先而就義者何眾也！則是高皇帝以實求，而天下以實應也。夫高皇帝未嘗不言理學也，其文辭發於《論心》、《論洪範》諸書，而其事見於尊崇夫子，及
translation_en: …talents to seize the opportunity for merit and fame—what is called “clouds rising and dragons transforming”—truly unmatched before or since. And when His Majesty had just taken Jinling 金陵, he honored Fushou 福壽, a Grand Master of the former Yuan, as a worthy, commending him and granting him a shrine with spring and autumn sacrifices; subsequently, recognizing the talent of Wei Su 危素, an Academician of the former Yuan, he conferred office upon him, yet because he had compromised his integrity, banished him to Linhuai 臨淮 and never employed him again—thus subtly showing the empire the standard of conduct. At that time, while still toiling over the enterprise of conquering on horseback, he dispatched letters and gifts of silk to invite such men as Song Wenxian 宋文憲 (Song Lian 宋濂), Wang Zhongwen 王忠文 (Wang祎 王禕), Tao An 陶安, and Wei Guan 魏觀, entrusting them with the drafting of imperial decrees, and the gracious courtesy with which he encouraged and comforted them was extraordinary, so that in refined abundance the court was celebrated for its many worthies. Yet regarding these worthies, gentlemen still said that they followed the narrow habits of the conquered dynasty and were unable to brightly manifest the splendor of a new era, considering them to have fallen short. Before long, however, Wang Zhongwen and Wu Zhongjie 吳忠節 (Wu Yun 吳雲) proved able to die as martyrs in Dian 滇 (Yunnan), Left Director Sun 孫左司 (Sun Yan 孫炎) died as a martyr in Min 閩 (Fujian) [?], Prefect of Nanchang Ye 葉南昌 (Ye Chen 葉琛) died as a martyr in Chu 楚, and Xiong of Qining 熊岐寧 (Xiong Ding 熊鼎) died as a martyr among the northern caitiffs; and when it came to the time of the dynastic transition [the Jingnan succession crisis], among those arrayed like hemp and ramie, men of the caliber of Fang 方 (Fang Xiaoru 方孝孺), Tie 鐵 (Tie Xuan 鐵鉉), Chen 陳 (Chen Di 陳迪), and Zhuo 卓 (Zhuo Jing 卓敬)—how numerous were those who vied to be first to go to their deaths for righteousness! This was because Emperor Gao 高皇帝 sought with substance, and the empire responded with substance. Now, Emperor Gao did not fail to speak of the Learning of Principle (lixue 理學); his literary expressions of it were set forth in such writings as the Discourse on the Mind (Lun xin 論心) and the Discourse on the Great Plan (Lun Hongfan 論洪範), while his deeds were seen in his veneration of the Master [Confucius] and…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
詔天下先以經術而取士大指欲搢紳士大夫
發明心得之學以黼黻
皇猷佐理國事無愧夫子之敎而已不欲令其
標户别軌以出於所謂功業節義文章之
外而創爲尊也
列聖益培植之蓋百餘年而諸搢紳大夫往往
以實應故楊文貞李文達輩出而爲輔蹇
忠定夏忠靖王忠肅王端毅馬端肅劉忠
宣輩出而握銓樞于肅愍王文成出而戡
===
大難庶幾哉事功有徵矣而李劉章鍾之
抗疏是以諫明節也陳劉孫許之殉義是
以守明節也所謂以實應者猶故也當弘
正間天下不勝其質人文之所蘊崇浡發
而爲李何徐薛輩相與脩明騷雅西京之
業頗翕然爭言古矣執事乃謂其少伸而
多抑何也驟習之而稍怠事則抑驟言之
而稍駭聽則抑露其華天下以其華而掩
其實則抑欲自致於用天下不信其用而
punctuated: 詔天下先以經術而取士，大指欲搢紳士大夫發明心得之學，以黼黻皇猷，佐理國事，無愧夫子之敎而已，不欲令其標户别軌，以出於所謂功業、節義、文章之外而創爲尊也。列聖益培植之，蓋百餘年而諸搢紳大夫往往以實應。故楊文貞、李文達輩出而爲輔，蹇忠定、夏忠靖、王忠肅、王端毅、馬端肅、劉忠宣輩出而握銓樞，于肅愍、王文成出而戡大難，庶幾哉事功有徵矣！而李、劉、章、鍾之抗疏，是以諫明節也；陳、劉、孫、許之殉義，是以守明節也。所謂以實應者，猶故也。當弘、正間，天下不勝其質，人文之所蘊崇，浡發而爲李、何、徐、薛輩，相與脩明《騷》《雅》、西京之業，頗翕然爭言古矣。執事乃謂其少伸而多抑，何也？驟習之而稍怠事則抑；驟言之而稍駭聽則抑；露其華，天下以其華而掩其實則抑；欲自致於用，天下不信其用而
translation_en: … issuing decrees to the realm to put classical learning first in selecting scholars. His broad aim was simply to have the gentry and scholar-officials elucidate the learning they had grasped in their own minds, so as to adorn the imperial plan, assist in administering the affairs of state, and be worthy of the Master's teachings; he did not wish to let them set up separate sects and divergent paths to establish a novel preeminence outside of what are called meritorious achievement, moral integrity, and literary composition. Successive Emperors nurtured this further, and for over a hundred years the various gentry and grandees time and again responded with substance. Thus men such as Yang Wenzhen [Yang Shiqi 楊士奇] and Li Wenda [Li Xian 李賢] emerged to serve as grand counselors; men such as Jian Zhongding [Jian Yi 蹇義], Xia Zhongjing [Xia Yuanji 夏原吉], Wang Zhongsu [Wang Ao 王翺], Wang Duanyi [Wang恕], Ma Duansu [Ma Wensheng 馬文升], and Liu Zhongxuan [Liu Daxia 劉大夏] emerged to hold the pivots of personnel and military affairs; and Yu Sumin [Yu Qian 于謙] and Wang Wencheng [Wang Shouren 王守仁] emerged to quell great crises—practical achievements were nigh well attested indeed! Meanwhile, the defiant memorials of Li [Li Shimi 李時勉], Liu [Liu Qiu 劉球], Zhang [Zhang Lun 章綸], and Zhong [Zhong Tong 鍾同] manifested moral integrity through remonstrance; the martyrdom for righteousness of Chen [Chen Zushou 陳祚? / Chen選?], Liu [Liu成?], Sun [Sun Sui 孫燧], and Xu [Xu Da 許達] manifested moral integrity through steadfastness in duty. What is called responding with substance remained just as before. During the Hongzhi (1488–1505) and Zhengde (1506–1521) reigns, the empire grew weary of unadorned plainness, and what had accumulated in literary culture burst forth in men like Li [Li Mengyang 李夢陽], He [He Jingming 何景明], Xu [Xu Zhenqing 徐禎卿], and Xue [Xue Hui 薛蕙], who together revived and illuminated the legacy of the *Elegies of Chu* (Chuci), the *Odes* (Shijing), and the Western Han, and people quite unanimously vied in speaking of antiquity. Why then does Your Excellency say that they were seldom encouraged and mostly suppressed? When they abruptly practiced it and slightly neglected official business, they were suppressed; when they abruptly spoke of it and slightly startled listeners, they were suppressed; when they displayed their florid brilliance, and the world took that brilliance to obscure their substance, they were suppressed; when they wished to apply themselves to practical use, and the world did not believe in their usefulness, but…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
信其無可用則抑然文士類多沾沾自喜
上者厭薄一切而下者相傾爲競也自喜
則途分而不爲黨厭薄一切則多避而無
所營相傾爲競則各露其短而不能掩故
其爲損淺也事功之臣大者股肱腹心而
次亦禦圉干城亡論已德靖之季而天下
相率尚通以就功善恣肆諱而爲恢廓善
干謁諱而爲敏捷善詞刺諱而能用間善
乾沒諱而能用仁甚或竭天下之力之半
===
以內投虢而外就私然舉事一不當而持
衡之臣猶得以議其後其爲益與損半也
節義之士致命而遂志者尚已其大之批
龍鱗抗論
扆陛之上次亦請
尚方搜城社折檻鎖樹而不動天下高其風
而願爲之下然亦有因是而遂自謂高恣
行胸臆而莫之能挽天下敢議而不敢折
顧其介特自好必不忍舍其舊而下之也
punctuated: 信其無可用，則抑。然文士類多沾沾自喜，上者厭薄一切，而下者相傾爲競也。自喜則途分而不爲黨；厭薄一切則多避而無所營；相傾爲競則各露其短而不能掩：故其爲損淺也。事功之臣，大者股肱腹心，而次亦禦圉干城，亡論已。德、靖之季，而天下相率尚通以就功：善恣肆，諱而爲恢廓；善干謁，諱而爲敏捷；善詞刺，諱而能用間；善乾沒，諱而能用仁；甚或竭天下之力之半，以內投虢而外就私。然舉事一不當，而持衡之臣猶得以議其後，其爲益與損半也。節義之士，致命而遂志者尚已。其大之批龍鱗，抗論扆陛之上，次亦請尚方，搜城社，折檻鎖樹而不動。天下高其風而願爲之下。然亦有因是而遂自謂高，恣行胸臆而莫之能挽，天下敢議而不敢折。顧其介特自好，必不忍舍其舊而下之也，
translation_en:
…believe they are of no practical use, and thus they are suppressed. Yet literary men are mostly self-satisfied and complacent; the superior among them disdain everything, while the inferior contend by undermining one another. Because they are self-satisfied, their paths diverge and they do not form factions; because they disdain everything, they mostly withdraw and scheme after nothing; because they contend by undermining one another, each exposes his own shortcomings and cannot conceal them. Therefore, the harm they cause is shallow.

As for ministers of practical achievement, the greatest are the limbs, trunk, and trusted confidants of the ruler, while the next best are also defenders of the frontiers and bulwarks of the state—these need no discussion. Toward the end of the Zhengde (1506–1521) and Jiajing (1522–1566) reigns, however, the realm followed one another in prizing accommodation in order to accomplish results: those skilled in unbridled license euphemized it as broad-minded magnanimity; those skilled in currying favor euphemized it as nimble resourcefulness; those skilled in prying and spying [?] euphemized it as the ability to employ espionage; those skilled in embezzlement euphemized it as the ability to practice benevolence. In extreme cases, they even exhausted half the strength of the realm to ingratiate themselves with favorites within the court [?] while pursuing private ends abroad. Yet the moment they managed an affair improperly, the ministers holding the scales of evaluation could still criticize them afterward; thus the benefit and the harm they brought were equal.

As for men of principled righteousness, those who lay down their lives to fulfill their aspirations are the most exalted. The greatest among them brush against the dragon's scales and argue defiantly before the imperial screen and throne-steps; the next best request the imperial sword from the Directorate for Imperial Manufactories, root out the foxes and rats in the city walls and altars, or break the palace balustrade and chain themselves to trees without wavering. The world esteems their moral character and willingly humbles itself before them. Yet there are also those who on this account consider themselves lofty, willfully acting out their own impulses so that no one can restrain them, while the world dares to criticize them in private but dares not rebuke them to their faces. Still, because they are fiercely independent and cherish their own integrity, they certainly cannot bear to abandon their former principles and stoop to baseness;…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其爲益大而爲損小也自理學出而三者
俱下風矣卽篤行如河汾卓識如新建如
新會而疇得而議之彼能見其大者遠者
而芥視此數端而亦宜也奈何籠天下之
鮮脩尠學者而合之取其最汙最下而謂
爲遠且大也尠學則避之聞見之外以爲
良鮮脩則避之性命之表以爲卓隨處體
認則隨處緣而喻利萬物一體則一體賢
不肖而便其私一語合則囂囂然而遽謂
堯舜一不合則嘵嘵然而詈其非人稍抑
必借巧而更揚此負必要彼而求勝故夫
理學之爲益者大而其爲損者亦非小也
夫所謂理學者非能外是三者而創爲高
者也其矩矱在心而其用在倫常日用之
內出之而業則爲事功功成而紀述之則
爲文章功有尼而不得遂則爲節義而其
體固未嘗變也然則執事者亦務以實求
之而已求之而應以實則進之求之而應
punctuated: 其爲益大而爲損小也。自理學出，而三者俱下風矣。卽篤行如河汾，卓識如新建、如新會，而疇得而議之？彼能見其大者、遠者，而芥視此數端，而亦宜也。奈何籠天下之鮮脩尠學者而合之，取其最汙最下，而謂爲遠且大也？尠學，則避之聞見之外以爲良；鮮脩，則避之性命之表以爲卓。「隨處體認」，則隨處緣而喻利；「萬物一體」，則一體賢不肖而便其私。一語合，則囂囂然而遽謂堯、舜；一不合，則嘵嘵然而詈其非人。稍抑，必借巧而更揚；此負，必要彼而求勝。故夫理學之爲益者大，而其爲損者亦非小也。夫所謂理學者，非能外是三者而創爲高者也。其矩矱在心，而其用在倫常日用之內。出之而業，則爲事功；功成而紀述之，則爲文章；功有尼而不得遂，則爲節義；而其體固未嘗變也。然則執事者亦務以實求之而已。求之而應以實，則進之；求之而應
translation_en:
…their benefit is great and their harm is small. Ever since the Learning of Principle (lixue) emerged, those three have all been relegated to an inferior position. Indeed, when it comes to earnest conduct like that of Master Hefen [Xue Xuan 薛瑄], or lofty insight like that of Master Xinjian [Wang Shouren 王守仁] and Master Xinhui [Chen Xianzhang 陳獻章], who could possibly find fault with them? Capable of perceiving what is great and far-reaching, it was only fitting that they regarded these several pursuits as mere trifles. Yet why is it that today people gather together all those in the empire who lack moral cultivation and learning, adopting what is most sordid and base while calling it far-reaching and great? Lacking learning, they take refuge beyond the realm of sensory knowledge and call it "innate goodness"; lacking cultivation, they take refuge outside the bounds of human nature and destiny and call it "transcendence." Preaching "experiential realization everywhere," they instead seize every opportunity to pursue profit; preaching "forming one body with all things," they lump the worthy and the unworthy together to serve their own selfish ends. When a single word agrees with them, they clamorously and hastily proclaim someone a Yao or a Shun; when a single word disagrees, they stridently revile him as less than human. If slightlychecked, they invariably resort to cleverness to exalt themselves anew; if defeated on one point, they inevitably shift to another to seek victory. Therefore, while the benefit of the Learning of Principle is great, the harm it can cause is by no means small either.

Now, what is called the Learning of Principle cannot set itself apart from those three things to invent some lofty realm of its own. Its standard and measure reside in the mind, while its application lies within the constant human relationships and daily life. When brought forth as enterprise, it becomes practical achievement; when achievements are accomplished and recorded, it becomes literary composition; when achievement is obstructed and cannot be fulfilled, it becomes moral integrity—yet its fundamental substance has never changed. This being so, those in authority should simply devote themselves to seeking men on the basis of substance. When you seek them and they respond with substance, advance them; when you seek them and they respond…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
以虛則退之而天下自是無虛應矣夫精
白一德竭肺腑而媚其上者應之者責也
責行辨志眈眈逐逐以來賢者而不示好
尚之隙以為天下窺此非應之者責也愚
生之見乃爾毋亦以為虛而弁髦焉
第五問
鄒觀光
同考試官教諭陳批
國家大計在漕運邊防此作指陳得失灼有成筭且氣雄詞古滾滾不窮非充養之士何
===
以得此錄之
考試官教授黃批論治河治邊勢審事宜識時務
者乎其人耶
考試官教授郭批任大决疑如指諸掌
執事以天下大筭試諸生而諸生業鉛槧
者見以為計畫無所之耳雖然不敢不罄
一得以對夫所謂天下大筭者邊防也漕
計也
國家建都燕蓋北迫虜而南仰三吳之粟以
punctuated:
以虛，則退之，而天下自是無虛應矣。夫精白一德，竭肺腑而媚其上者，應之者責也；責行辨志，眈眈逐逐以來賢者，而不示好尚之隙以為天下窺，此非應之者責也。愚生之見乃爾，毋亦以為虛而弁髦焉。

第五問
鄒觀光
同考試官教諭陳批：國家大計在漕運、邊防。此作指陳得失，灼有成筭，且氣雄詞古，滾滾不窮，非充養之士，何以得此？錄之。
考試官教授黃批：論治河、治邊，勢審事宜。識時務者乎，其人耶！
考試官教授郭批：任大决疑，如指諸掌。

執事以天下大筭試諸生，而諸生業鉛槧者，見以為計畫無所之耳。雖然，不敢不罄一得以對。夫所謂天下大筭者，邊防也，漕計也。國家建都燕，蓋北迫虜，而南仰三吳之粟以
translation_en:
…with emptiness, then dismiss them; and from then on there will be no empty responses in the realm. To maintain pure and unblemished virtue, pouring out one's innermost heart in devotion to one's superiors—this is the responsibility of those who respond. To demand substantive conduct and discern true intentions, earnestly and eagerly drawing in worthy men without revealing any gap of personal preference for the world to peer into and exploit—this is not the responsibility of those who respond. Such is the view of this foolish student; do not take it as empty talk and cast it aside like a worn-out cap.

Fifth Question
Zou Guanguang 鄒觀光
Associate Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳 comments: The great plans of the state lie in grain transport and frontier defense. This essay points out the successes and failures with clear, well-formed calculations. Moreover, its vigor is heroic and its diction ancient, flowing on inexhaustibly. Were he not a scholar of deep cultivation, how could he achieve this? Record it.
Examiner, Professor Huang 黃 comments: In discussing river control and frontier management, he assesses the circumstances and weighs what is appropriate. One who understands the affairs of the times—is it not this man!
Examiner, Professor Guo 郭 comments: Shouldering great responsibilities and resolving doubts, as easily as pointing to the palm of one's hand.

Your Reverences have tested us students on the great calculations of the realm, yet students who occupy themselves with writing brush and tablets are often seen as having no recourse when it comes to practical planning. Even so, I dare not fail to exhaust my humble understanding in reply. Now, what are called the great calculations of the realm are frontier defense and plans for canal transport. The state established its capital at Yan 燕 [Beijing], which presses close to the northern caitiffs in the north while depending in the south upon the grain of the Three Wu 三吳 region to…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
自給故邊譬之肩背也漕河譬之喉咽也
夫肩背喉咽者人之所恃以爲命也奈之
何其易言之也當今爲邊害者莫如虜而
爲漕害者莫如黃河其悍猛善潰奔突而
來若震霆而莫可禦迅疾若風雨而莫之
控揣爲勢同也居數歲輒一潰潰輒入爲
候同也其潰而入縱橫汗漫而無所不陷
害聽其來聽其息而手足無所措其不敵
同也厚集而禦之乘險而拒之爲堤爲墻
===
數千里咫尺之地瑕而是數千里者皆瑕
矣其不易防同也未至而請爲備大司農
靳金錢弗肯予卽予之而覈者乘其後旣
至而備大司農推金錢以予之予而不必
盡用於邊與漕也其積弊同也蓋嘉靖中
而虜之雄若俺答者率其黠弟悍子以數
十萬騎牧於雲中上谷之間而與我共不
入犯三輔則東躙遼西齧晉又西而掠秦
凉夏朔之境中國罷於奔命者三十年矣
punctuated: 自給，故邊譬之肩背也，漕河譬之喉咽也。夫肩背、喉咽者，人之所恃以爲命也，奈之何其易言之也！當今爲邊害者莫如虜，而爲漕害者莫如黃河。其悍猛善潰，奔突而來，若震霆而莫可禦；迅疾若風雨，而莫之控揣：爲勢同也。居數歲輒一潰，潰輒入：爲候同也。其潰而入，縱橫汗漫而無所不陷害，聽其來、聽其息而手足無所措：其不敵同也。厚集而禦之，乘險而拒之，爲堤、爲墻，數千里咫尺之地瑕，而是數千里者皆瑕矣：其不易防同也。未至而請爲備，大司農靳金錢弗肯予，卽予之而覈者乘其後；旣至而備，大司農推金錢以予之，予而不必盡用於邊與漕也：其積弊同也。蓋嘉靖中，而虜之雄若俺答者，率其黠弟悍子，以數十萬騎牧於雲中、上谷之間而與我共，不入犯三輔，則東躙遼、西齧晉，又西而掠秦、凉、夏、朔之境，中國罷於奔命者三十年矣。
translation_en: …supply itself. Thus, the frontier may be compared to the shoulders and back, and the Grand Canal to the throat. Now, the shoulders, back, and throat are what a person relies upon for life—how could one speak of them lightly! At present, nothing does greater harm to the frontier than the northern caitiffs, and nothing does greater harm to the canal transport than the Yellow River. Fierce, violent, and prone to bursting through, they come rushing and charging like a thunderbolt that cannot be withstood; swift as wind and rain, they cannot be reined in or fathomed—in their momentum, they are the same. Every few years they inevitably burst through once, and whenever they burst through, they penetrate inside—in their periodicity, they are the same. When they burst through and penetrate inside, they spread wild and unchecked in every direction, engulfing and harming everything in their path, while we can only let them come and let them subside, at a loss as to where to place hand or foot—in our inability to match them, they are the same. We mass heavy forces to withstand them and take advantage of strategic terrain to repel them, building dikes and building walls over several thousand li; yet if there is a flaw in a single foot of ground, all those several thousand li become flawed—in the difficulty of defending against them, they are the same. When one requests to make preparations before they arrive, the Minister of Revenue begrudges the funds and refuses to grant them, or even if he grants them, auditors follow right behind; when one makes preparations after they have arrived, the Minister of Revenue hands over the funds generously, yet what is granted is not necessarily all used for the frontier or the canal—in their accumulated abuses, they are the same. Indeed, during the Jiajing era (1522–1566), a chieftain among the caitiffs such as Altan Khan (Anda 俺答) led his cunning younger brothers and fierce sons, pasturing hundreds of thousands of horsemen between Yunzhong 雲中 and Shanggu 上谷 and sharing the region with us; when they did not invade the metropolitan area (Sanfu 三輔), they trampled Liaodong 遼 in the east, gnawed at Shanxi (Jin 晉) in the west, and farther west plundered the borders of Shaanxi (Qin 秦), Liangzhou 凉, Ningxia 夏, and Shuozhou 朔, exhausting China in rushing about to meet emergencies for thirty years…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
天子爲之北顧而興嗟至數四廢
旰食乃隆慶中俺答不勝其孽稚之愛而輸
其要領以款我縛中行翕侯於鼎俎之上
谷蠡屠耆而下解辮請命者數百人
國家因其人而假以封爵大小羈縻之然不
爲給祿食也以漢文之盛猶廑廑稱兄弟
國焉而我
明若天之覆彼而日益尊彼不能講敵禮也漢
供呼韓邪歲費四十四億而我市馬不過
===
一二邑之租而已不爲傾左藏也且納款
之端在彼而不在我制款之權在我而不
在彼卽魏絳楊雄所稱何啻焉或以爲虜
詐而款我非也虜不款我何以制之而彼
故爲詐且俺答誠老厭兵其孽稚誠感我
之厚待而思效順夫焉得爲詐也又謂虜
卒解媾輕騎鬨於互市之下而疾馳叩居
庸鹵昌平緩急何以應之又非也夫虜將
大舉必先厚集諸部祠蹛林暴糗晾騎形
punctuated: 天子爲之北顧而興嗟，至數四廢旰食。乃隆慶中，俺答不勝其孽稚之愛，而輸其要領以款我，縛中行、翕侯於鼎俎之上，谷蠡、屠耆而下，解辮請命者數百人。國家因其人而假以封爵，大小羈縻之，然不爲給祿食也。以漢文之盛，猶廑廑稱兄弟國焉，而我明若天之覆彼而日益尊，彼不能講敵禮也；漢供呼韓邪，歲費四十四億，而我市馬不過一二邑之租而已，不爲傾左藏也。且納款之端，在彼而不在我；制款之權，在我而不在彼。卽魏絳、楊雄所稱，何啻焉！或以爲虜詐而款我，非也。虜不款，我何以制之，而彼故爲詐？且俺答誠老厭兵，其孽稚誠感我之厚待而思效順，夫焉得爲詐也？又謂虜卒解媾，輕騎鬨於互市之下，而疾馳叩居庸、鹵昌平，緩急何以應之？又非也。夫虜將大舉，必先厚集諸部，祠蹛林，暴糗晾騎，形
translation_en: The Son of Heaven looked north on account of this and sighed, to the point of repeatedly foregoing his evening meal. Then, during the Longqing era (1567–1572), Anda [Altan Khan], overcome by his affection for his favored young grandson, offered his submission to make peace with us. He bound up our equivalents of Zhonghang Yue and the Yihou [Zhao Xin] and delivered them over to the executioner's block, while from the Guli and Tuqi kings on down, several hundred men undid their braids and begged for our commands. The dynasty took advantage of these men as they were and granted them noble titles, keeping both great and small under loose rein (jimi), yet without providing them with stipends or grain. Even at the height of Emperor Wen of Han, he still barely managed to call them a "brotherly state," whereas our Ming covers them like Heaven and grows ever more exalted, so that they cannot claim the status of ceremonial equals. When the Han supplied Huhanye, it cost forty-fourhundred million cash a year, whereas our horse markets take no more than the tax revenue of one or two counties, without draining the imperial treasury. Moreover, the initiative in submitting to peace came from them and not from us, while the authority to control the peace settlement rests with us and not with them. Even what Wei Jiang and Yang Xiong praised is far surpassed by this! Some consider that the caitiffs are deceiving us in making peace; this is wrong. If the caitiffs did not make peace, what means would we have to control them such that they would deliberately resort to deceit? Besides, Anda has truly grown old and weary of war, and his favored young grandson truly feels gratitude for our generous treatment and wishes to render obedience—how could this be deceit? Others say that if the caitiffs suddenly break off the peace, raise an uproar with light cavalry right beneath the border markets, and gallop swiftly to strike at Juyong Pass and pillage Changping, how would we respond in an emergency? This too is wrong. For whenever the caitiffs are about to launch a major incursion, they must first assemble their various tribes in force, sacrifice at Dailin, dry their parched grain in the sun, and air out their mounts; their…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
見勢動而我故得先爲備也大約
中國因款而息肩而得專精於虜則可因款
而息肩而遂忘虜則不可夫所謂專精者
何也比薊鎭歲益省調發各邊鮮按伏贏
金錢當以萬計不可裒而積之近鎭乎秋
稍登商賈時集贖鍰爵貰不可捐而平糴
以實邊乎鹽筴屯政不可時舉乎冗卒不
可汰而驍騎不可益練乎山海而西以至
鴈門不可削夷而爲險乎猶未也而虜酋
===
計巳耄且斃耳其貳者必黃台吉而是孽
孫故不變也其勢必內猜而不相容降人
之在寘顏者因中行翕侯之縛而中恨且
自疑也當其時有能兩匈奴其國而中度
遼且爲維州其降人乎是一大奇也然而
不敢盡言也漕之役當嘉靖末而黃河決
而東注自華山入飛雲橋截沛以入昭陽
湖逆歷湖陵以至谷亭四十里其南溢於
徐爲巨浸
punctuated:
見勢動，而我故得先爲備也。大約中國因款而息肩，而得專精於虜則可；因款而息肩，而遂忘虜則不可。夫所謂專精者何也？比薊鎭歲益省調發，各邊鮮按伏，贏金錢當以萬計，不可裒而積之近鎭乎？秋稍登，商賈時集，贖鍰爵貰，不可捐而平糴以實邊乎？鹽筴屯政，不可時舉乎？冗卒不可汰，而驍騎不可益練乎？山海而西以至鴈門，不可削夷而爲險乎？猶未也。而虜酋計巳耄且斃耳，其貳者必黃台吉，而是孽孫故不變也，其勢必內猜而不相容。降人之在寘顏者，因中行翕侯之縛，而中恨且自疑也。當其時，有能兩匈奴其國而中度遼，且爲維州其降人乎？是一大奇也，然而不敢盡言也。

漕之役，當嘉靖末而黃河決而東注，自華山入飛雲橋，截沛以入昭陽湖，逆歷湖陵以至谷亭四十里；其南溢於徐，爲巨浸。
translation_en:
… their formations will become visible and their momentum set in motion, so that we will naturally be able to prepare for them in advance. In general, if China takes advantage of the peace settlement to rest its shoulders and thereby concentrate its energies on the northern caitiffs, that is acceptable; if it takes advantage of the peace settlement to rest its shoulders and consequently forgets about the caitiffs, that is not acceptable. Now, what is meant by concentrating our energies? Recently, the Jizhou Defense Command has increasingly saved on troop deployments each year, and the various frontier sectors rarely have to set ambushes, so the surplus funds must amount to tens of thousands—could these not be gathered and stored in the nearby defense commands? When the autumn harvest comes in somewhat well and merchants gather from time to time, could the proceeds from redemption fines and the sale of ranks not be allocated to buy grain at equitable prices in order to provision the frontier? Could the salt monopoly and military farming administration not be timely promoted? Could superfluous soldiers not be weeded out, and valiant cavalrymen be further trained? From Shanhai Pass westward all the way to Yanmen Pass, could the terrain not be scarped and leveled to create strategic barriers? Even this is not all. By calculation, the caitiff chieftain [Altan Khan] is already senile and will soon die. His successor will surely be Huang Taiji [Sengge Düüreng], yet that bastard grandson [Dayan Noyan / Baya'ud Ba'atur] will certainly not alter his stance; by force of circumstance, they will inevitably suspect one another internally and be unable to tolerate each other. And the Chinese defectors residing in豐州 [Zhiyan, i.e.,豐州灘] harbor resentment within and doubt their own safety because of the binding up of those like Zhonghang Yue and the Xihou [Zhao Xin, i.e., Zhao Quan and his associates]. When that time comes, will there be someone capable of splitting their polity into two Xiongnu states and establishing an administration like the General Who Crosses the Liao (Duliao jiangjun) in between, while treating those defectors as at Weizhou? That would be a grand masterstroke, though it is something I dare not speak of in full.

As for the grand canal works: at the end of the Jiajing reign, the Yellow River breached its banks and poured eastward. From Huashan it entered Feiyun Bridge, cut across Pei County to enter Zhaoyang Lake, and flowed backward past Huling for forty li to Guting; to the south it overflowed into Xuzhou, creating a vast inundation. …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
天子爲之南顧而興嗟亦數四勑
宵旰而大司空出計以爲仍故道則河益狎
而攻無已强捍之則暫見其利而終釀害
謀於捍與徙之間而行求廢趾有河自南
陽折而南東至於夏村又東南至於留城
而浚之橇攡版築之役興而謗騰上謂捐
天下之財以填無益之壑
天子意不能無動而會采輔臣言委計視河者
乃止前後役夫九萬有奇白金以兩計者
===
四十萬而粟石稱是兩歲之間漕道通而
大司空再受
賞而吏士
賜爵有差或謂河不久復當變胡以費水衡
錢萬萬者非也漢武帝之塞瓠子避河害
耳而至發卒數萬人自湛白馬玉璧羣臣
從官自將軍而下皆負薪置决口功成而
築宮以侈之今玆通漕大計胡言費也或
謂不當逆拒河也逆之則决而爲漕害順
punctuated: 天子爲之南顧而興嗟，亦數四勑宵旰。而大司空出計，以爲仍故道則河益狎而攻無已；强捍之則暫見其利，而終釀害。謀於捍與徙之間，而行求廢趾。有河自南陽折而南東至於夏村，又東南至於留城，而浚之。橇攡版築之役興，而謗騰上，謂捐天下之財，以填無益之壑。天子意不能無動，而會采輔臣言，委計視河者乃止。前後役夫九萬有奇，白金以兩計者四十萬，而粟石稱是。兩歲之間，漕道通而大司空再受賞，而吏士賜爵有差。或謂河不久復當變，胡以費水衡錢萬萬者，非也。漢武帝之塞瓠子，避河害耳，而至發卒數萬人，自湛白馬玉璧，羣臣從官自將軍而下，皆負薪置决口，功成而築宮以侈之。今玆通漕大計，胡言費也？或謂不當逆拒河也，逆之則决而爲漕害，順
translation_en: The Son of Heaven looked south on account of this and sighed, repeatedly issuing edicts as he toiled before dawn and ate late into the night. The Minister of Works (Da sikong 大司空) then put forward a plan, holding that if the old channel were retained, the Yellow River would encroach ever more brazenly and attack without cease; whereas if it were forcibly held back, one might see a temporary advantage, yet in the end brew disaster. Deliberating between holding it back and shifting its course, he went out to search for abandoned ancient channels. There was a river bed that turned southeast from Nanyang 南陽 to Xiacun 夏村, and then further southeast to Liucheng 留城, which he had dredged. As the labor of mud-sledges and rammed-earth construction got underway, slanderous criticisms rose up to the throne, claiming that the wealth of the empire was being thrown away to fill a useless ditch. The Son of Heaven could not help being swayed in his mind, yet happening to adopt the words of the Grand Secretaries, he entrusted the full responsibility to the official inspecting the river, and the criticisms ceased. From start to finish, the conscripted laborers numbered over ninety thousand, the silver counted in taels came to four hundred thousand, and the grain in piculs matched that amount. Within two years, the Grand Canal route was opened to traffic; the Minister of Works was twice rewarded, and officials and subalterns were bestowed ranks by degrees. Some say that the Yellow River will before long change course again, so why expend hundreds of millions of coins from the treasury? This is wrong. When Emperor Wu of the Han 漢武帝 plugged the breach at Huzi 瓠子, it was merely to avoid damage from the river; yet he went so far as to mobilize tens of thousands of soldiers, personally sank a white horse and jade bi-disks into the waters, and had all his ministers and attendant officials from generals on down carry bundles of brushwood to place in the breach, even building a palace to celebrate the achievement once the work was done. Now, when this is a grand plan for opening the grain transport route, how can anyone speak of the expense? Others say that one ought not go against the Yellow River to repel it—that if one goes against it, it will breach its banks and become a menace to the grain transport, whereas if one follows…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之則借以爲漕利又非也夫河性能决而
不能安爲順也言借河利者引寇而入室
者也然則爲今之計者如之何曰河决有
漸也度其來或增築堤以抗之或决其下
流而别引之霖溢有時也多集木石以爲
楗嚴耳目以爲偵而已自淮而北則多橫
潰而成溢自淮而南則或漲入而成塞皆
不可不預計而逆爲之所也夫漕河通而
海運之說漸絀矣海運之說得之漕河阻
===
而後入其言大計二曰歲往返不過四月
而艘卒以三之二而自便耗餘可小裁而
羨鏹可積也曰縣官卽萬一以喉咽憂能
别於喉咽之外而濟大命誠亦利便哉然
而不克如勝國終始之海利者何也勝國
業下宋而宋之戈船下瀨之卒嘯聚而不
敢歸者無慮數萬此其人皆習風濤躑躅
待命者也朱清張瑄一劇盜耳驟以東南
天下之半而委之金虎符萬戶而下聽其
punctuated: 之則借以爲漕利，又非也。夫河性能决而不能安爲順也，言借河利者，引寇而入室者也。然則爲今之計者如之何？曰：河决有漸也，度其來，或增築堤以抗之，或决其下流而别引之；霖溢有時也，多集木石以爲楗，嚴耳目以爲偵而已。自淮而北，則多橫潰而成溢；自淮而南，則或漲入而成塞，皆不可不預計而逆爲之所也。夫漕河通而海運之說漸絀矣。海運之說，得之漕河阻而後入，其言大計二：曰歲往返不過四月，而艘卒以三之二而自便，耗餘可小裁而羨鏹可積也；曰縣官卽萬一以喉咽憂，能别於喉咽之外而濟大命，誠亦利便哉！然而不克如勝國終始之海利者，何也？勝國業下宋，而宋之戈船、下瀨之卒，嘯聚而不敢歸者無慮數萬，此其人皆習風濤，躑躅待命者也。朱清、張瑄一劇盜耳，驟以東南天下之半而委之，金虎符萬戶而下，聽其
translation_en: … with it, one can borrow its power to benefit the Grand Canal—this too is wrong. For the nature of the Yellow River is that it is prone to bursting its banks and cannot peacefully remain compliant. Those who speak of borrowing the River's advantage are inviting bandits into the house. Then what should be our plan today? I say: the breaching of the River happens gradually. By gauging its approach, we can either build up the dikes to resist it, or open up its lower reaches to divert it elsewhere. Flooding from heavy rains occurs at seasonal times; we need only gather ample timber and stone for pilings, and keep strict watch with our eyes and ears to monitor it. North of the Huai River, it mostly bursts wildly across the land and causes inundation; south of the Huai River, it sometimes swells into the channel and causes silting. In all these cases, we must plan ahead and prepare measures for it in advance. Now, once the Grand Canal is open, arguments for maritime transport gradually recede. The arguments for maritime transport gained traction only after the Grand Canal was blocked. In broad terms, they make two main points: first, that the annual round trip takes no more than four months, leaving the boatmen free to attend to their own affairs for two-thirds of the year, while wastage allowances can be slightly reduced and surplus funds accumulated; second, that if the state should by any chance suffer anxiety over its vital throat [the Grand Canal], being able to sustain its great mandate via a route outside that throat is indeed advantageous and convenient! Yet why is it that we cannot match the maritime benefits enjoyed from beginning to end by the conquered dynasty [the Yuan]? After the conquered dynasty had subjugated the Song, the soldiers of the Song warship and rapid-current fleets who banded together and dared not return home numbered easily in the tens of thousands. These men were all accustomed to wind and waves, pacing about and awaiting orders. Zhu Qing 朱清 and Zhang Xuan 張瑄 were mere notorious pirates, yet half the empire in the southeast was suddenly entrusted to them. From Myriarchs bearing golden tiger tallies on down, they were allowed to…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
自爵賞而不從中命也錢穀聽其自出沒
而不從中訾也故清瑄得以畢見其才而
為百餘年之利然國紀潰而清瑄亦倂族
矣今亡論守臣自一嚬笑外斤斤束三尺
士亦安能舍燕中牘而見富貴乎夫艘與
卒陽為募而陰則拘攝也別妻子若脫褓
見制閫若束濕不待納之鯨鯢之口而稱
就死矣吾固筴海漕之不可以久也然亦
知創之者之甚難而湮之者之甚易乎哉
===
一旦有緩急鑿空而後思其故則晚矣夫
邊計博而悍銳之臣亦或有理先帥之緒
而思復河套者乎藉令
國家都長安借河套之地以為外屏而益斥
遠虜可復也長安今不得言重矣我以十
萬之衆逐虜而虜果去也勢必設八衛衛
五千人而後成軍何所取調也若移鎮何
鎮可移也勢必錯衛所州邑得二萬民戶
以配之何戶可徙也勢必築五六城以犬
punctuated:
自爵賞，而不從中命也；錢穀聽其自出沒，而不從中訾也。故清、瑄得以畢見其才，而為百餘年之利。然國紀潰而清、瑄亦倂族矣。今亡論守臣自一嚬笑外斤斤束三尺，士亦安能舍燕中牘而見富貴乎？夫艘與卒陽為募而陰則拘攝也，別妻子若脫褓，見制閫若束濕，不待納之鯨鯢之口而稱就死矣。吾固筴海漕之不可以久也，然亦知創之者之甚難，而湮之者之甚易乎哉？一旦有緩急，鑿空而後思其故，則晚矣。
夫邊計博，而悍銳之臣亦或有理先帥之緒而思復河套者乎？藉令國家都長安，借河套之地以為外屏，而益斥遠虜，可復也。長安今不得言重矣。我以十萬之衆逐虜，而虜果去也，勢必設八衛，衛五千人而後成軍，何所取調也？若移鎮，何鎮可移也？勢必錯衛所、州邑，得二萬民戶以配之，何戶可徙也？勢必築五六城以犬
translation_en:
…bestow ranks and rewards on their own without awaiting orders from the central court; and they were permitted to manage money and grain at their own discretion without being audited from the center. Thus Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan were able to display their talents to the fullest and create a benefit that lasted for over a hundred years. Yet the laws and discipline of the state collapsed, and Qing and Xuan likewise had their entire clans exterminated. Today, not to mention that territorial officials—beyond a single frown or smile—are strictly bound by the three-foot statute books, how could officers possibly bypass the dossiers in the capital [Yanzhong] to attain wealth and rank? Now, the ships and sailors are ostensibly recruited as volunteers, yet in secret they are seized and conscripted. Parting from their wives and children is like being torn from swaddling clothes, and appearing before the regional commanders is like being bound with wet cords; one does not need to cast them into the jaws of whales and sea-monsters for them to declare that they are going to their deaths! I have certainly calculated that sea transport cannot be sustained for long; yet do people also realize how exceedingly difficult it is for those who pioneer it, and how exceedingly easy it is for those who let it fall into oblivion? Once an emergency arises, to try to open up a route from scratch and only then think back on the old arrangements will be too late.

Now, frontier planning is vast in scope, and among fierce and spirited officials, might there not also be some who would take up theunfinished enterprise of former commanders and contemplate recovering the Ordos Loop [Hetao]? Supposing the State had its capital at Chang'an, relying on the territory of the Ordos Loop as an outer screen so as to drive the caitiffs ever further away, then it would be worth recovering. Today, Chang'an can no longer be called the center of gravity. Even if we were to drive out the caitiffs with a host of a hundred thousand and the caitiffs did indeed depart, circumstances would require establishing eight Guards, with five thousand men per Guard, before a proper army could be formed—from where would these troops be drawn and transferred? If we were to relocate existing Defense Commands, which Defense Command could be relocated? Circumstances would require interspersing Guards, Battalions, subprefectures, and districts, and obtaining twenty thousand civilian households to match them—which households could be moved there? Circumstances would require building five or six walled cities so as to interlock like dog's…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
牙錯何所取土石材木也虜必爭爭當以
兵數萬衛之何所取餉也河地饒即可屯
虜不能無蹂踐乎何以能且耕且戰也虜
旣失地獨不能合東大虜而倂力我乎大
虜即不東獨不能從之而西以取償於京
輔乎我竭天下以奉陝而陝不益安乃以
京輔委者非策也故曰海運可暫通而河
套卒不當復也海縱不暫通吾不可遽而
廢其道河套縱可復吾且緩而待數十年
===
之後嗚呼天下之事見以爲名美而其實
不易舉者固志士才臣所欲迫得以爲功
而元老耆哲之所徘徊而却顧者也虜款
而吾日汲焉若有事即虜無款而吾坦焉
若無事漕通而吾日虞河之決即河決而
吾不虞漕之通舉以提衡天下易易耳寧
獨此二端也
punctuated: 牙錯，何所取土石材木也？虜必爭，爭當以兵數萬衛之，何所取餉也？河地饒，即可屯，虜不能無蹂踐乎？何以能且耕且戰也？虜旣失地，獨不能合東大虜而倂力我乎？大虜即不東，獨不能從之而西，以取償於京輔乎？我竭天下以奉陝，而陝不益安，乃以京輔委者，非策也。故曰：海運可暫通，而河套卒不當復也。海縱不暫通，吾不可遽而廢其道；河套縱可復，吾且緩而待數十年之後。嗚呼！天下之事，見以爲名美而其實不易舉者，固志士才臣所欲迫得以爲功，而元老耆哲之所徘徊而却顧者也。虜款而吾日汲焉若有事，即虜無款而吾坦焉若無事；漕通而吾日虞河之決，即河決而吾不虞漕之通。舉以提衡天下，易易耳，寧獨此二端也！
translation_en:
…interlock like dog's teeth; from where would the earth, stone, and timber be obtained? The caitiffs would certainly contest it, and if they contest it, we would have to defend the workers with tens of thousands of troops; from where would their rations be obtained? The land of the Ordos Loop is fertile and could indeed support military agricultural colonies, but could the caitiffs be prevented from trampling them? How could our men simultaneously farm and fight? Once the caitiffs have lost this territory, could they not join forces with the great caitiff hordes to the east and combine their strength against us? Even if the great caitiff hordes do not move east [?], could they not follow them here to the west [?] to seek compensation in the capital region? For us to exhaust the resources of the realm to support Shaanxi, without making Shaanxi any more secure, and in doing so expose the capital region to danger—this is not a sound strategy. Therefore I say: maritime transport may be temporarily opened, whereas the Ordos Loop ultimately should not be recovered. Even if the sea route is not temporarily opened, we must not hastily abandon its course; even if the Ordos Loop could be recovered, we should still postpone it and wait until several decades have passed.

Alas! Among the affairs of the realm, those that appear splendid in name yet in reality are not easily carried out are naturally what ambitious men and talented ministers eagerly press for in order to claim merit, whereas elder statesmen and seasoned wise men hesitate and look back in caution. If when the caitiffs submit to peace terms we remain daily anxious as though facing hostilities, then even if the caitiffs break the peace we can remain calm as though nothing were amiss; if when the Grand Canal flows smoothly we daily guard against the breaching of the Yellow River, then even if the River breaches its banks we will not have to worry about the passage of the grain tribute. To apply this principle to hold the balance of the entire realm would be easy indeed—how could it be limited to these two matters alone!

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
萬曆元年癸酉秋八月湖廣
鄉試錄成蓋我
皇上龍飛第一科云前是隆慶戊
辰我
皇上以元良正
青宮至壬申以溫文踐
===
紫極而薄海臣庶相與欣欣喁喁
踴躍而起庶幾沐浴維新之
化當是時
上猶在岐嶷也乃世所稱述靡匪
鴻駿之猷由視聽以至敷言不
俟究辨秩秩中矩百辟唯面
簾陛不隔
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
萬曆元年癸酉秋八月，湖廣鄉試錄成，蓋我皇上龍飛第一科云。前是隆慶戊辰，我皇上以元良正青宮；至壬申，以溫文踐紫極。而薄海臣庶，相與欣欣喁喁，踴躍而起，庶幾沐浴維新之化。當是時，上猶在岐嶷也，乃世所稱述，靡匪鴻駿之猷；由視聽以至敷言，不俟究辨，秩秩中矩，百辟唯面，簾陛不隔。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn of the guiyou year, the first year of the Wanli reign (1573), the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination was completed; this was indeed the first examination held since Our August Emperor ascended the dragon throne. Prior to this, in the wuchen year of the Longqing reign (1568), Our August Emperor, as the virtuous heir, was formally established in the Eastern Palace; when the renshen year (1572) arrived, with gentle and refined virtue he ascended to the Purple Pole (the imperial throne). Officials and commoners within the four seas all looked up to him with joy and eager anticipation, leaping up in excitement, hoping to bathe in the transforming influence of the new reign. At that time, the Emperor was still in his tender, precocious boyhood, yet everything the world praised and recounted of him was nothing less than grand and magnificent counsels. From his seeing and hearing to his pronouncement of words, without needing exhaustive deliberation, everything was orderly and conformed to the standard; the hundred officials faced him directly, with neither screen nor palace steps separating them. …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
萬幾之燕卽
御經筵與二三賢碩孜孜講求治
緒而顧其大旨雅以遴人才
飭士習爲重故
勑戒一下而中外紳笏之士惵然
思洗其翕訛之習而夙夜在
公其所登進卽陣海巖穴阻
===
===
深闇習咸麗於光明蓋踰年
而試期至矣今之捧鄉書而
詣
闕庭者皆頃者踴躍而起之士
也豈非甚盛隆際哉雖然我
皇上一鼓舞而天下之治煥然章
明稱爲新矣爾多士旦夕且
punctuated: 萬幾之燕，卽御經筵，與二三賢碩孜孜講求治緒；而顧其大旨，雅以遴人才、飭士習爲重。故勑戒一下，而中外紳笏之士惵然思洗其翕訛之習，而夙夜在公；其所登進，卽陣海巖穴，阻深闇習，咸麗於光明。蓋踰年而試期至矣。今之捧鄉書而詣闕庭者，皆頃者踴躍而起之士也，豈非甚盛隆際哉？雖然，我皇上一鼓舞，而天下之治煥然章明，稱爲新矣；爾多士旦夕且
translation_en: In the leisure from the myriad affairs of state, He at once attends the Classics Mat, diligently investigating the threads of governance with two or three worthy and eminent ministers; and looking at His fundamental aim, He consistently places great weight on selecting men of talent and rectifying the habits of scholars. Thus, once the imperial admonition was handed down, officials wielding court tablets at court and in the provinces were awed into seeking to cleanse themselves of the habit of sycophancy and slander, devoting themselves to public duty day and night; and among those promoted and advanced, even those from the farthest seas [?] and mountain caves, once obstructed by deep obscurity and benighted customs, have all come into the radiance of light. Indeed, after a year had passed, the time for the examination arrived. Those who now hold their letters of provincial recommendation and proceed to the palace court are all scholars who just recently rose up with eager enthusiasm—is this not a most flourishing and glorious juncture? Even so, with a single rousing stimulus from our August Emperor, the governance of the realm has become brilliantly manifest and may be called renewed; as you many scholars are morning and evening about to…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
效用亦思所以新其德以仰
承
至意乎哉夫植幹者節也豫幾者
識也展采者才也然而不根
於德而有至者否也卽多士
所陳析經術治道不斤斤守
其陳言而時發其超然之見
===
而稱新矣乎不佞不能信異
日之必盡讎其言也夫感激
慷慨以見節而謂之新權奇
達變以見識而謂之新斡濟
倜儻以見才而謂之新銳不
敢謂新也銳所謂新者一切
適已自好岐路之見蕩然而
punctuated: 效用，亦思所以新其德以仰承至意乎哉？夫植幹者，節也；豫幾者，識也；展采者，才也。然而不根於德而有至者，否也。卽多士所陳，析經術治道，不斤斤守其陳言，而時發其超然之見，而稱新矣乎？不佞不能信異日之必盡讎其言也。夫感激慷慨以見節，而謂之新；權奇達變以見識，而謂之新；斡濟倜儻以見才，而謂之新：銳不敢謂新也。銳所謂新者，一切適已自好、岐路之見，蕩然而
translation_en: … render service; have you also considered how to renew your virtue so as to look up and fulfill the Supreme Intention? Now, what establishes one's backbone is integrity; what anticipates subtle incipient signs is insight; and what displays one's brilliance is talent. Yet has anyone ever reached the highest attainment without these being rooted in virtue? Even if in what you many scholars have set forth—analyzing classical learning and the way of governance—you do not rigidly cling to stale words, but at times express transcendent views, can this be called renewal? I, unworthy as I am, cannot be certain that in future days your actions will necessarily match your words in full. Now, to show integrity through impassioned fervor and call that renewal; to show insight through tactical ingenuity and adaptability and call that renewal; or to show talent through bold and uninhibited management of affairs and call that renewal—I, Rui, dare not call these renewal. What I, Rui, call renewal is to sweep away and …

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
盡滌之純乎精白而後庶幾
新耳不然而封蔀日蔽雖有
三美將焉出之是故節也矜
名識也誨巧才也拂經如是
而
人主亦奚賴也始銳之來也汎乎
雲夢之澤而其陰有浮浸焉
===
河伯之所夸大也而土人曰
是漲也新易涸也稍改而之
大江浩淼朗曠行乎日夜而
不息知其出嶓冢導岷波而
下也有本者如是是之取耳
夫植德以利用隨所用而不
違德庶幾乎無負甚盛隆際
punctuated: 盡滌之，純乎精白，而後庶幾新耳。不然，而封蔀日蔽，雖有三美，將焉出之？是故節也矜名，識也誨巧，才也拂經，如是而人主亦奚賴也？始銳之來也，汎乎雲夢之澤，而其陰有浮浸焉，河伯之所夸大也，而土人曰：「是漲也，新易涸也。」稍改而之大江，浩淼朗曠，行乎日夜而不息，知其出嶓冢、導岷波而下也。有本者如是，是之取耳。夫植德以利用，隨所用而不違德，庶幾乎無負甚盛隆際…
translation_en: …completely wash them away, becoming purely and spotlessly white—only then does one come close to being renewed. Otherwise, if one is obscured daily by the screen of selfish narrowness, even if one possesses the three fine qualities, from what could they emerge? Therefore, one's integrity becomes mere boasting for fame, one's insight becomes a lesson in cunning, and one's talent goes against constant principles; if it is like this, what can the ruler rely upon? When I, Rui, first came here, I floated across the Yunmeng Marsh, and on its northern side there were overflowing waters—such as the Earl of the River would boast of—yet the locals said, "This is floodwater; what is newly risen easily dries up." Changing course slightly, I went to the Great River [Yangzi], vast, boundless, bright, and open, flowing day and night without cease, and I knew that it issues from Mount Bozhong and guides the waves of Mount Min downward. That which has a source is like this, and this is what one takes as a model! Now, if one establishes virtue in order to make practical use of it, and in whatever way one is employed does not depart from virtue, one will perhaps not fail to live up to this most flourishing and exalted juncture…

title: 萬曆元年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
矣周之詩云周雖舊邦其命
維新而又云濟濟多士文王
以寧夫文王安能舍多士而
新周哉銳不佞敬以是勗其
試事則前序悉之矣
江西九江府儒學教授黃銳
謹序
punctuated:
矣。周之《詩》云：「周雖舊邦，其命維新。」而又云：「濟濟多士，文王以寧。」夫文王安能舍多士而新周哉？銳不佞，敬以是勗。其試事，則前序悉之矣。
江西九江府儒學教授黃銳謹序。
translation_en:
…! An ode of Zhou in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) says: "Although Zhou is an old state, its Mandate is newly given." And it also says: "Stately are the many gentlemen; through them King Wen enjoys peace." Indeed, how could King Wen have set aside those many gentlemen and yet renewed Zhou? Unworthy though I, Rui, am, I respectfully offer these words in encouragement. As for the affairs of the examination, the preceding preface has already recounted them in full.
Respectfully prefaced by Huang Rui 黃銳, Instructor (jiaoshou) in the Confucian School of Jiujiang Prefecture in Jiangxi.
